## AI分析总结

## 1. 主要更新类型

- **功能新增 + 性能优化**：为 AdamW 优化器引入主机侧（CPU）状态卸载能力，通过配置项 `state_offload: cpu` 启用，属于显存优化类特性。

## 2. 关键变更点及与项目方向的关系

- 核心变更：训练过程中将 AdamW 的优化器状态（动量 m 与方差 v，通常相当于 2 倍参数量的显存占用）从 GPU 显存卸载到主机内存，按需换入换出。
- 与项目整体方向高度契合：VeOmni 的目标是"以模型为中心的分布式配方库，扩展任意模态模型训练"。大参数量、多模态模型的训练对显存极其敏感，优化器状态是显存三大占用（参数、梯度、优化器状态）中最大的一项。该功能直接服务于"Scaling"这一核心诉求，使用户能在有限显存下训练更大规模或多模态融合模型。

## 3. 对项目的影响和潜在意义

- **降低显存门槛**：显著减少 GPU 显存峰值，使单卡/少卡环境训练更大模型成为可能，或允许增大 batch size 与序列长度以提升训练效率。
- **增强实用性**：多模态模型（视觉、语音、文本等分支叠加）参数量增长迅速，该特性为社区用户提供了一条可行的低成本扩展路径，扩大了项目的适用场景。
- **与既有配方体系融合**：作为 ckpt/optim 配置体系的一部分，用户可通过简单配置开关启用，保持了 VeOmni "Recipe Zoo" 即插即用的设计理念。

## 4. 值得关注的技术点

- **状态换入换出策略**：CPU↔GPU 数据传输的粒度与时机（如同步换出、异步流水线）直接影响训练吞吐，如何在显存节省与通信开销之间取得平衡是关键。
- **与混合精度/分布式并行的兼容性**：AdamW 状态在 fp32 下维护，需与 ZePO、FSDP 等并行策略及梯度累积正确协同，避免状态一致性问题。
- **配置化设计**：`state_offload: cpu` 作为显式开关，体现了项目对不同硬件条件的自适应能力，也便于 A/B 性能对比。

## 5. 对项目发展的影响

结合 README 所述背景，VeOmni 致力于成为多模态大模型训练的分布式基础设施。本提交从**资源效率**维度补齐了关键一环：在不改变算法语义的前提下，通过系统级内存管理释放显存，使"Scaling Any Modality"从愿景更贴近工程现实。它降低了多模态模型训练的硬件门槛，有利于吸引更多研究者基于 VeOmni 复现和扩展论文成果（对应其 arXiv 论文），并为后续更大规模配方（如更长上下文、更多模态分支）的落地预留了显存空间。总体而言，这是一次务实的基础设施增强，强化了项目在分布式训练生态中的竞争力。

## LightX2V 昨日提交分析（第 1/1 批，共 2 条）

### 1. 主要更新类型
- **[77bb43d]** Bug修复 + 性能优化（显存/内存释放）
- **[55aa706]** 功能新增（编译、预热与新平台支持）

### 2. 关键变更点与项目方向的关系

**[77bb43d] 修复 MiniMax-H3 文本编码器驻留时的主机内存泄漏**
- 背景：当 `text_encoder_cpu_offload: false` 时，`load_text_encoder` 用 `to_cuda()` 把编码器搬到加速器上，却仍保留主机侧 `pin_*` 副本——而这些副本此后再无人读取，白白占用约 47 GiB（默认 pinned 不可换出；即使 `pinned: false` 也会因 host-to-device 拷贝变脏，沦为不可回收的 `Private_Dirty`）。
- 修复方式：新增 `_Qwen3VLTextBackboneWeights.release_host_weights()`，在驻留分支 `to_cuda()` 之后立即丢弃所有主机权重张量并记录释放量；`to_cpu()` 回退逻辑保持兼容（无主机副本时从设备拷回）；卸载配置路径完全不受影响。
- 实测：RSS 从 ~120 GiB 降至 75.7 GiB，`Private_Dirty` 归零，加载与推理耗时、GPU 峰值均无回退。已知遗留：加载期间峰值 `VmHWM` 仍约 118 GiB（主机/设备双份的瞬时并存）。

**[55aa706] Seko 支持编译、预热及 Metax / MUSA 平台**
- 为轻量推理框架补上编译加速与 warmup 能力，并扩展国产加速卡（摩尔线程 MUSA、沐曦 Metax）适配。

### 3. 对项目的影响和潜在意义
- 第一条提交把"驻留模式"从一个隐性内存陷阱变成真正省 40+ GiB 主机内存的可用选项，直接影响大规模部署的机器成本与并发容量——这正契合 LightX2V "Light"（轻量推理）的核心定位。
- 第二条提交扩大平台覆盖面与运行时性能手段，提升框架在异构国产硬件生态中的可用性。

### 4. 值得关注的技术点
- **pinned / 非 pinned 两种主机副本的不可回收机制**：pinned 内存不可换出；私有映射因脏页也变 `Private_Dirty`——修复前后的对比说明"释放"必须针对张量 storage 本体，而非仅做 `del` 引用。
- **驻留与卸载双路径的兼容设计**：释放只发生在驻留分支，卸载路径仍按请求读取主机副本，体现了对多粒度 offload（model/block）配置的细致区分。
- **加载峰值的诚实披露**：PR 明确指出 `VmHWM` 峰值未改善，为后续优化（如分段搬运、流式释放）留下议题。
- **验证方法严谨**：给出完整平台、配置、对照表格（RSS、映射、耗时、GPU 峰值），可复现性强。

### 5. 对项目发展的整体影响
基于 README——LightX2V 是面向轻量视频生成的推理框架，强调低开销与多平台——这两条提交共同强化了框架的两个关键支柱：**一是**通过消除宿主机内存浪费，使高分辨率长视频（如 768x1344、5 s）的驻留式推理在显存充裕的机器上更经济；**二是**通过编译/预热与国产加速卡支持，降低部署门槛、扩展硬件生态。二者都直接服务于"更轻、更快、更广适配"的项目目标，尤其在模型规模（如 MiniMax-H3 这类大文本编码器）持续增长的背景下，这类内存修复对维持框架的"轻量"口碑至关重要。

## 详细提交记录

### [77bb43d](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightX2V/commit/77bb43dd18987f4f9740961c773956068d9d7edd)

- **作者**: zhengxinwei
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T11:57:05Z
- **提交信息**: fix(minimax-h3): release the resident text encoder's host copy (#1666)

Fixes #1664.

## What

When the MiniMax-H3 Qwen3-VL text encoder is resident on the accelerator
(`text_encoder_cpu_offload: false`), `load_text_encoder` moves it to the
device with `to_cuda()` but keeps the host copies (`storage.pin_*`).
Nothing reads them again.

This PR adds `_Qwen3VLTextBackboneWeights.release_host_weights()`, which
drops every host `pin_*` tensor of the backbone's weight modules, and
calls it right after `to_cuda()` in the resident branch. The released
size is logged.

- `to_cpu()` keeps working: a module without a host copy falls back to
`module.to_cpu()` and is copied back from the device.
- Offloaded configurations (`text_encoder_cpu_offload: true`, model or
block granularity) read the host copy on every request and are
unchanged.

## Why

The host copy is the full backbone, ~47 GiB:

- with `text_encoder_host_pinned: true` (default) it is pinned and
unswappable;
- with `text_encoder_host_pinned: false` it is a private mapping of the
checkpoint, and the host-to-device copy dirties its pages. On our
platform all of it ends up `Private_Dirty`/`Anonymous`, so it is not
reclaimable either (details in #1664).

## Test

Single MTT S5000 (80 GB), `PLATFORM=musa`. Config: MiniMax-H3 fl2av,
8-step turbo LoRA (dynamic), BF16, `cpu_offload: true` with
`offload_granularity: block`, `text_encoder_cpu_offload: false`,
`text_encoder_host_pinned: false`, `parallel: {}`. Request: t2av
768x1344, 5 s.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| load log | — | `Released 46.9 GiB of host text-encoder weights now
resident on the device` |
| process Rss after warmup | ~120 GiB | 75.7 GiB |
| checkpoint mappings (`Private_Dirty`) | 46.9 GiB | 0 |
| load models | 133.6 s | 136.9 s |
| 5 s request, pipeline | 106.6 s | 106.1 s |
| text encoding | 0.07 s | 0.07 s |
| GPU memory peak | 70.2 GiB | 70.2 GiB |

Known limitation: the peak *during* loading is still ~118 GiB (`VmHWM`),
because the host and device copies coexist until the release. Loading
layer by layer straight to the device would remove that peak too. This
PR does not attempt that.

## AI分析总结

# FlashInfer 昨日 128 个提交综合分析

## 一、主要更新类型
昨日提交以**性能优化为绝对主体**（约七八成），其余为 Bug 修复、功能新增与工程基建。新增能力包括 DSA 索引器 FP8 可选形式、FP8 分页上下文注意力的 AOT 程序、`light_akk` 显存/速度权衡开关、Selective MQA TopK prefill、CSF 块尺度编解码、`mm_bf16`/`bmm_fp8` 的 bias 支持及 Mamba 因果卷积推理 API 等。

## 二、关键变更
**硬件代际精细化调优**：几乎全部改动按 sm_100a（B200）、sm_103a（GB300）、sm_107a（R200）、sm_120（RTX PRO 6000）做 per-(架构, SM 数, 形状, token 区间) 路由，覆盖注意力、GEMM、MoE、KDA、RMSNorm、GDN 等热路径。典型手段有四级 K ring 流水线、TMA 与计算重叠、L2 预取行上限、makespan 驱动的尾部 tile 排序、per-board override 表驱动的免重编译程序切换。单项提速多在 1%–30%，部分达 1.17x–4.8x。

**训练侧与系统级扩展**：Cake 训练内核（RMSNorm、KDA、LM-head loss、投影 GEMM 的 wgrad/dgrad、上下文并行）密集完善，确定性与非确定性双轨并行维护；MoE GEMM 编译产物跨进程持久化并设计多维失效机制，消除多 rank 冷启动开销；split-KV 按实际 split 数分配，单工作区从 16 GiB 降至 4.65 MiB；FP8 分页注意力由 JIT 迁至 45 个 AOT 程序，提速最高约 3.94 倍且逐位一致。

**正确性与生产健壮性**：系统修复"不报错但输出错误"的静默故障（MXFP4xMXFP8 隐藏维度异常、非连续输入全错、共享内存越界、FA2 rescaling NaN、KDA 屏障死锁、CUDA graph 重放写已释放内存、多进程缓存挂死等），并统一以显式 `ValueError` 或 pad-and-declare 契约拒绝非法输入；部署侧小 query 长度自动回退 fa2，解决 MTP 投机解码约 10 倍浪费。

**工程基建**：CODEOWNERS 分层、多 GPU CI 汇总、autotuner 可复现性、sccache 回退加固、CUTLASS 对齐校验与 vLLM/Megatron 依赖行为的测试固化。

## 三、项目影响
性能收益普遍附带 A/B、ABBA 基准与置信区间，多数优化位级一致、API 不变，用户零迁移成本。稳定性方面消除 illegal memory access、NaN 与挂死，下游隐蔽风险显著下降。FlashInfer 正从"推理内核库"演进为 Blackwell 时代覆盖训练+推理的一体化内核平台，并为 DeepSeek-V4、Kimi-K3 等模型在 Blackwell/Rubin 世代的部署奠定基础；同时生态契约显性化，为 1.x 接口稳定性铺路。风险在于形状/硬件路由逻辑日趋复杂，维护成本上升。

## 四、值得关注的技术点
- **精度-性能权衡工程化**：以 guarded FP32 two-sum、Kahan 补偿累加替代 FP64 折叠，在预算内换速度；按 atol/rtol 精度预算验收，按预算切换程序而非盲目追速。
- **缓存键分层设计**：rank 偏移仅入内存 `__hash__`、不入持久化键，兼得同进程隔离与跨进程共享。
- **编译器与运行时陷阱**：ptxas 版本差异是隐性性能变量；272 KB 超大共享内存依赖 CUDA 13.4 oversized 模式；CUDA 句柄须在参数存活期拷贝。
- **严谨基准文化**：冷 L2、几何均值、噪声带、bitwise 校验，并诚实披露回退幅度与同 SOTA 的差距。

综上，昨日工作以"性能冲刺与正确性加固并重"的节奏，沿多硬件覆盖、训练内核成熟化、系统级优化与工程基建三线并进，持续巩固其作为 LLM 推理与训练内核基础设施的核心竞争力。

### [c51a754](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c51a7540f042d7607f23bc29417147ca7a921828)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T23:53:31Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm): blocked FP32 dw sums for the large-T B200 backward windows (#8848)

Related issue: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/8066

`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_train` is RMSNorm for training. The forward
returns y (BF16) and rstd (FP32), and the backward returns dx (BF16) and
dw (FP32). The two modes, `deterministic=True` and
`deterministic=False`, share the forward and differ only in the
backward. Both modes support:

- [T, H] rows with BF16 or FP32 weight
- a fused residual add (H6144)
- per-head views [T,24,256] (strided) and [T,4,256] (contiguous), with a
shared w[256]

This PR follows #8577, #8626, #8655, #8704, #8810 and #8827. It is the
follow-up that #8827 announced for the B200 top windows. It changes only
the `deterministic=False` backward on sm_100a (B200), in the 12 windows
below. Since #8827, FlashInfer main runs the TwoSum twin program in
these windows. With this PR, the backward there runs a single kernel
with blocked FP32 dw sums, which is the kernel kind that #8655 ships on
GB300 and R200. Above T 131072, the TwoSum twin stays.

- H1536: T 78785 to 131072 with BF16 weight, T 75777 to 131072 with FP32
weight
- H2048, H4096, H6144 and residual H6144: T 65537 to 131072, both weight
dtypes
- H5120: T 56257 to 131072, both weight dtypes

Against the TwoSum twin it replaces (main), the new backward is 1.029x
to 1.266x faster on every bwd row (det-anchored, see Measurement).
Against det, bwd ranges from 0.99x to 1.23x. Against the strongest
in-budget non-Cake SOTA, bwd ranges from 1.01x to 2.29x. Wherever
SOTA/new is below 1 on bwd or 2xfwd+bwd, the candidate shown exceeds the
dw budget (!).

On 9 rows (marked -), det is faster than new in all 4 sessions, each
time by more than the row's A/A floor in that session. On these rows
det/new is 0.9876 to 0.9982 before rounding. They are:

- bwd with FP32 weight at H4096 T 130304 and 131072, and at H5120 T
56257, 98304 and 122304
- bwd with BF16 weight at H4096 T 131072 and H5120 T 98304
- 2xfwd+bwd with FP32 weight at H4096 T 130304 and 131072

These rows come from one measurement run and are shown as measured. A
follow-up PR re-checks them.

**Summary over all rows (39 workloads x 3 ops)**

|op|det/new geomean [min, max]|det/new < 1|SOTA/new geomean [min,
max]|SOTA/new < 1|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fwd|1.000x [0.99, 1.00]|18 of 39|1.001x [0.97, 1.05]|20 of 39|
|bwd|1.037x [0.99, 1.23]|13 of 39|1.186x [1.01, 2.29]|0 of 29|
|2xfwd+bwd|1.014x [0.99, 1.08]|15 of 39|1.091x [1.00, 1.47]|0 of 29|

The "< 1" counts use unrounded ratios, so a row printed as 1.00x can
count as < 1. SOTA/new covers only rows with an in-budget SOTA, so the
20 rows marked ! are left out. This PR does not change the forward: det,
new and main run the same forward programs, and the fwd ratios are
measured values.

**Measurement**

- Latency: the median of the CUPTI span of one CUDA-graph replay with L2
flushed (cold L2).
- 4 sessions run in parallel, one per GPU: s1 and s3 in forward order,
s2 and s4 in reverse order.
- Each session times 201 replays per implementation and op, split over 3
interleaved rounds. The median pools the 4 sessions.
- Each implementation's own setup, reduction, cast and copy kernels are
inside the span.
  - The p10-p90 ranges are omitted here.
- Process: each row group runs in one process that holds det, new and
every non-Cake candidate. The implementation order rotates, so each
implementation takes each position about equally often over sessions x
rounds.
- Context (measured on GB300 and B200): on small rows, Cake gains
somewhat more than the other non-compile libraries from sharing the
process with torch.compile. SOTA/new vs the non-compile candidates is up
to about 1.10x higher (GB300) / 1.14x higher (B200) in the one-process
measurement than in a process without torch.compile; on large rows the
difference is <= 1.02x. Every row here is a large row (T >= 56257).
Ratios vs det are unaffected.
- main/new is det-anchored. main was timed in its own process with only
det and main, so main/new = (main / det of that process) / (new / det of
this PR's process). det runs byte-identical code in both processes, so
this removes the drift between processes. The raw ratio, main us / new
us, is shown in parentheses.
- Workload: eps 1e-6. For every implementation, y, dx and h_new are
BF16, and rstd and dw are FP32.
- det = deterministic Cake (`deterministic=True`), which this PR does
not change. new = this PR's non-deterministic Cake
(`deterministic=False`).
- SOTA = the fastest non-Cake candidate that has these outputs and meets
the accuracy budget, taking the worst of 5 seeds. The budget is dx atol
= rtol = 1e-2, and dw per element atol 1e-4 + rtol 1e-4 vs FP64. new and
det meet it on every row.
- Candidates: QuACK 0.6.5 (heuristic config and per-shape autotuned),
torch.compile (max-autotune-no-cudagraphs and default mode),
Liger-Kernel 0.8.5, and Transformer Engine 2.20.2 (run as the FP32
problem).
- Not candidates: PyTorch's fused rms_norm (dtype error), Apex (not
installed) and FlashInfer's inference rmsnorm (forward only).
- Accuracy: in every changed window, no measured point of new's dw
exceeds the dw budget (per element atol 1e-4 + rtol 1e-4 vs FP64), and
with FP32 weight no point exceeds the dw error of FP32 eager on the same
inputs. The worst point, 0.9988 of the budget (FP32-weight H5120, T
113536, 120 seeds), is confirmed <= 1 with 240 seeds. The seed sets are:
  - 3 x 120 seeds (three input families) in all 12 windows
- fresh seeds 120..239 in the H4096, H5120, H6144 and residual H6144
windows
- 3 x 240 seeds in all 12 windows: 8 T per window, and in the
FP32-weight H5120 window the 32 T of the dense every-64 grid (112512,
114560] around the worst point
- Speedup = baseline latency / new latency (> 1: new is faster). Ratios
are computed from unrounded medians, so a few differ in the last digit
from the ratio of the printed latencies.
- Rows: for each window, the first T above its lower edge, T 98304 and T
131072. Three more rows come from an earlier screen that showed det
faster: H5120 T 128576 (BF16 weight), and H4096 T 130304 and H5120 T
122304 (FP32 weight).

Key:

- form: plain, or res = fused residual add (h_new = BF16(h + u),
combined grad). op 2xfwd+bwd = checkpointed step (forward, forward
recompute, backward).
- main = this backend on FlashInfer main before this PR, which is the
program this PR replaces. Its `deterministic=False` backward runs the
TwoSum twin in these windows (#8827), and its forward is the same
program as new's.
- + / - after det/new: in each of the 4 sessions, det/new differs from 1
by more than the row's A/A floor in that session, and all 4 sessions
agree that new (+) or det (-) is faster. Unmarked rows are within the
floor in at least one session, or the sessions disagree on which is
faster.
- Each session also times a second copy of det and of new. A row's A/A
floor in a session is the larger |1 - A/A| of its det and new copies in
that session.
- The largest A/A deviation of any row in a session was 0.0125 (s1),
0.0117 (s2), 0.0119 (s3) and 0.0078 (s4).
- ! = no non-Cake candidate meets the dw budget. The table shows the
fastest matched candidate, with its dw err/tol in parentheses, and
computes SOTA/new against it.
- SOTA names:
- TC = torch.compile (torch 2.14.1+cu130, inductor mode
max-autotune-no-cudagraphs, emulate_precision_casts=True) of the
explicit FP32-statistics reference
  - TCd = the same with torch.compile inductor default mode
- Q = QuACK 0.6.5 (quack-kernels, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.1), heuristic
config
- QA = QuACK 0.6.5 rmsnorm_fwd_tuned / rmsnorm_bwd_tuned (exhaustive
per-shape autotune, cached before timing)
- Liger = Liger-Kernel 0.8.5 (Triton 3.8.0), casting_mode gemma (FP32
math), offset 0
  - QA+add = torch add + QA (residual form)

**B200 (sm_100a): new non-deterministic Cake vs deterministic Cake,
strongest non-Cake SOTA and main. Every measured row**

- GPU: B200 sm_100a, 148 SMs, compute capability 10.0; driver 580.82.07;
one 8-GPU node used exclusively.
- Software: CUDA toolkit Build cuda_13.4.r13.4/compiler.38855100_0;
torch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA runtime 13.0).
- Builds: new was timed on an earlier build of this branch that runs the
same programs on these routes as this PR's head. main was timed on a
pre-merge build of #8827 that runs the same programs on these routes as
its merged head.

- **提交信息**: fix(attention): preserve FA2 history when the running maximum is unchanged (#6908)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Fix FA2 history rescaling for large, unchanged finite maxima. The
synthetic reproducer returns 128 NaNs before this change and the
expected unit output afterward.

Update only the regular FP32 and VO-split history-rescaling sites in
`prefill.cuh`:
```cpp
m_prev == -math::inf ? 0.f : math::ptx_exp2((m_prev - m_new) * sm_scale)
```
Subtracting before scaling prevents FMA/rounding from corrupting the
equal-maximum invariant; the guard retains empty-state handling. Score
exponentials, FP16 QK accumulation and other backends are unchanged. Add
targeted regression tests.

Fixes #6907

### [1c38099](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/1c380998cd9a59042a9df5565f7ff03f03931b38)

- **作者**: Ka-Hyun Nam
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T23:19:58Z
- **提交信息**: fix(experimental/b12x): deterministic pivot-tie fill in persistent top-k2048 (#8561)

## 📌 Description

The standalone persistent top-k2048 selector
(`flashinfer/experimental/b12x/attention/dsa_indexer/persistent_topk.py`,
`run_persistent_topk2048`) still fills the pivot-equal slots by
`atomic_add_global_i32` on the group output counter, so when more
candidates tie at the pivot than there are slots left, the selected set
depends on which CTA and thread reaches the atomic first. The same input
can return a different index set on every launch. This is the
persistent-kernel counterpart of the tie-fill fixed in #6736 for the
fused and tiled indexers; #6736 does not touch this file.

Fix: the group-wide radix round is factored into a `_radix_round`
helper, and after the four score rounds every CTA derives the number of
pivot ties (`s_suffix[bucket] - s_suffix[bucket + 1]`) and the slots
left from the same global histogram. Only when ties exceed slots does
the kernel run a second four-round radix select over the complemented
logical column (`~col`) of the pivot-equal candidates and store those
with `~col >= index_floor`, so the slots go to the lowest logical
columns regardless of CTA timing. The decision is group-uniform because
it is computed from the shared histogram, and the common no-tie path
pays one shared-memory read pair and a compare.

The histogram triple buffering now follows a running `hist_round`
counter instead of `iter_idx * 4 + round_idx`. This also fixes a latent
bug in the rotation: the old index advanced by four (one buffer modulo
three) across an iteration whose row has `seq_len <= topk`, where no
round runs and nothing is zeroed, so when a group processed a long row,
then a short row, then another long row, the first round of the second
long row accumulated into the buffer still holding the first long row's
round-2 histogram. The stale counts could move the round-0 bucket,
leaving the pivot above every real key and part of the output row
unwritten. Counting only the rounds that actually run keeps the current
buffer freshly zeroed whether an iteration runs zero, four or eight
rounds.

Contract matches #6736: the selected set is deterministic; output order
within the pivot slots (and above the pivot) is still arrival order.
`_fallback_topk2048` (`max_seq_len <= 32768` or unsupported devices)
still relies on `torch.topk` tie choice and is unchanged. The tie path
(four extra group barriers plus chunk scans) was not benchmarked; it
only runs when ties exceed slots.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Refs #6735 (item: standalone persistent top-k2048 tie fill). Companion
to #6736.

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.

justify below).

New
`test_persistent_topk_pivot_ties_select_lowest_columns_gpu[{all_tied,quantized,fp16_rounded}-{1,3}]`
in `tests/experimental/b12x/attention/test_persistent_topk_gpu.py`:
width 33792 (persistent kernel path, 5 CTAs per group), topk 512,
per-row lengths and rolled page tables; asserts the precondition per
pattern (ties straddle the boundary for `all_tied`/`quantized`, ties
exactly fill the slots for `fp16_rounded`, which exercises the skip
branch), compares the selected set against a stable index-ascending
reference through the page table, and requires the sorted output to be
bitwise equal across 8 launches.

New `test_persistent_topk_one_group_rotation_with_skipped_rows_gpu`:
forces `num_groups=1` (the launch config is monkeypatched, which the
test checks through the scratch size) and runs eight rows through one
group, alternating long rows with straddling pivot ties (two all-tied at
a score whose radix key has byte 2 == 0xFF, one all-zero, one quantized)
with rows at `seq_len == topk`, `seq_len == 37` and `seq_len == 300`.
Every row is compared with the lowest-column reference over four
launches, and the output is pre-filled with -1 so an unwritten slot is
visible. The high-byte score makes a stale round-2 histogram land in
bucket 255, so with the old rotation the long rows after a short row
pick a pivot above every real key and stay unwritten.

On RTX 5090 (SM120, CUDA 13.0): `pytest
tests/experimental/b12x/attention/test_persistent_topk_gpu.py -v` passes
11/11 with this change; the same test file on unpatched main fails 5 and
passes 6: `all_tied-1/3` and `quantized-1/3` because the selected set
differs from the lowest-column set, and the rotation case with `long
rows left unwritten: [2, 6]`. Not run on RTX PRO 6000 (same CC 12.0
silicon).

### [adf6add](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/adf6addac9006420fda1a3ba89aa54ae1c56d220)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T23:08:37Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_moe_finalize_allreduce_fusion): shared-expert prefetch programs at world sizes 8 and 2 (#8864)

This PR adds 7 shared-expert programs to
`cake_moe_finalize_allreduce_fusion`: 3 deferred two-shot shared
programs at world size 8 and 4 large-token shared programs at world size
2. Each new program uses the same protocol, workspace, cross-rank
exchange and summation order as the program it replaces. It produces the
same outputs. In each token step, it prefetches the shared-expert row
into L2 before the route loop. It then reads that row through the
read-only non-coherent path. At world size 8, a batch of 768 tokens or
more runs the deferred two-shot program. When the call has a shared
expert and top-k is 8, that batch now runs the deferred two-shot shared
program, except fp16 with FP16 output, which keeps the deferred two-shot
program. At world size 2, a batch of more than 1280 tokens with top-k 4
and a shared expert runs the large-token program. It now runs the
large-token shared program. The choice depends only on the token count,
the world size, top-k and whether the call has a shared expert.
`small_token_max` does not change it. World size 4, and calls without a
shared expert, do not change.

The kernel fuses MoE finalize, the all-reduce across the ranks of one
NVLink node, the residual add and RMSNorm at hidden size 7168. MoE
finalize uses the top-k expert rows with their routing scale, plus an
optional shared-expert row. The entry point is
`flashinfer.comm.allreduce_fusion(..., moe_finalize_backend="cake")`.
The kernel has no other Cake variants. It ships only in this fused form
and covers sm_100a and sm_103a. With this PR, it has 63 programs per
architecture (56 before) in 16 program kinds. Each kind has 2 data types
(fp16, bf16) x 2 epilogues (BF16/FP16 output, packed NVFP4 output),
except the world size 8 deferred two-shot shared kind, which has no fp16
program with FP16 output. World size 2 has small-token, persistent,
quad-route, large-token and large-token shared programs. World size 4
has small-token, persistent, two-shot, two-shot early, deferred two-shot
and deferred two-shot shared programs. World size 8 has small-token,
two-shot, two-shot early, deferred two-shot and deferred two-shot shared
programs.

The baseline is the previous Cake version on FlashInfer main (PR #8697).
In the tables, this PR changes the program of 14 shapes, which show the
token count in bold: 6 shapes with 2048 tokens at world size 8, top-k 8
and a shared expert (of the 8 such shapes, all but the 2 fp16 shapes
with FP16 output), and 8 shapes with 2048 tokens at world size 2 and a
shared expert. Their geomean speedup is 1.025x on B300 (min 1.014x, max
1.034x) and 1.024x on B200 (min 1.013x, max 1.035x). The other 706
shapes run the same program in both versions. Their geomean is 1.000x on
B300 (min 0.981x, max 1.021x) and 1.000x on B200 (min 0.974x, max
1.020x). Over all 720 shapes in the tables, the geomean is 1.000x on
B300 and 1.000x on B200.

In the owner shape list, 2048 is the only token count at world size 8
that is 768 or more, and the only token count at world size 2 above
1280. The data also include a second, independent measurement of each of
the 6 changed world size 8 shapes, and the 8 shapes with 1281 tokens at
world size 2 and a shared expert, the smallest batch that runs a
large-token shared program. On those 8 shapes, the previous version
takes 53.22-55.54 us on B300 and 53.26-55.84 us on B200, and this PR
takes 51.70-54.59 us and 51.74-55.09 us; the geomean speedup is 1.021x
on B300 (min 1.012x) and 1.021x on B200 (min 1.013x). Over all 28
measurements of changed shapes, the geomean speedup is 1.023x on B300
(min 1.012x) and 1.023x on B200 (min 1.013x). None of them measures
below 1.000 on either GPU. Per program, the geomean speedup on B300 /
B200 is 1.026x / 1.028x for world size 8 bf16 with BF16 output, 1.022x /
1.022x for world size 8 bf16 with NVFP4 output, 1.014x / 1.013x for
world size 8 fp16 with NVFP4 output, 1.032x / 1.033x for world size 2
bf16 with BF16 output, 1.023x / 1.020x for world size 2 bf16 with NVFP4
output, 1.024x / 1.025x for world size 2 fp16 with FP16 output and
1.020x / 1.018x for world size 2 fp16 with NVFP4 output.

The tables below give one row per shape of the owner shape list. The
measurements ran on NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (sm_103a) and NVIDIA B200
(sm_100a) with CUDA 13.4 and the default `small_token_max` of 64. The
previous and this-PR columns give the median CUPTI kernel time in
microseconds, taking the minimum over ranks. Speedup is the median of
paired previous/this-PR ratios from interleaved runs, with its 95%
bootstrap confidence interval. So the speedup of some rows differs
slightly from the ratio of the two median times. Values above 1 mean
this PR is faster. In the flag columns (PDL, NVFP4 out, shared expert),
1 means yes and 0 means no. A token count in bold marks a shape whose
program this PR changes.

### [f2c5a23](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/f2c5a23c415a1e6faa8f75d5c6bbf1a841b6a49e)

- **作者**: Jimmy Zhou
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T23:05:24Z
- **提交信息**: fix(prims-ts): recover four MoE perf regressions from #6832 (#7833)

## 📌 Description

#6832 (prims-TS Rubin support) made the prims-TS MoE backend slower in
four cases on Blackwell. On GB300, measured before vs after #6832 (below
1 = slower):

| # | Case | GB300, #6832 vs before |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | FP8 DeepSeek block-scale, autotuned prefill (DeepSeek-R1 / GLM
shapes) | 0.74-0.84x |
| 2 | Kimi-K3 MXFP4×MXFP8, expert parallel (56 of 896 experts local),
untuned, 2048 tokens | 0.33x |
| 3 | MXFP8×MXFP8, untuned, 2048 tokens | 0.88x |
| 4 | MXFP4×BF16, autotuned, 1 token | 0.88x |

Outputs were correct throughout; this PR only affects speed. Each case
has its own cause and its own small fix:

1. **DeepSeek FP8 epilogue spills at 128-token tiles**
(`batched_gemm_config.py`). The rewrite capped how many registers one
tensor-memory read (`tcgen05.ld`) may return. That split the DeepSeek
swap-AB epilogue's per-slice accumulator read into two half-width reads
plus a repack. This epilogue re-reads the accumulator every 128-wide K
block. At `epi_tile_n=128` the extra live registers spill to local
memory inside the hot loop. ptxas also drops the per-warp-role
`setmaxnreg` on these kernels, so the epilogue warps stay at the
128-register default. The fix exempts the DeepSeek epilogue from the
cap, as the non-swap path already was, so it issues one full-width read
per slice again.
2. **Expert-parallel untuned default launches a 16x grid**
(`config_mapper.py`). #6832's estimate of rows per local expert, which
divides by the global expert count, is correct. The problem is the
default it leads to. The untuned default (`[-1, -1]`) takes config 0 of
the lowest tile in the window. On the SM100 menu that config uses the
static tile scheduler, which sizes its grid for every routed row: 16x
the local work at 56/896. Under expert parallelism only, the default now
uses two rules. The tile is the smallest one that covers the average
rows per local expert. The config pair is the first one where both GEMMs
use the persistent scheduler. Default resolution for all-local (non-EP)
cases is unchanged: 150/150 resolutions are identical.
3. **64-wide MXFP8 FC1 gets one loader warp instead of four** (two JSON
menus). The menu field `num_load_b_warps: 1` used to mean "automatic" (4
routed-token loader warps for a 64-wide tile). After the rewrite it
means literally one warp, so the 64-wide FC1 kernel runs with 512
instead of 640 threads. Three stale rows change from 1 to 0
("automatic"). These rows feed the sm100 MXFP8×MXFP8 / MXFP4×MXFP8 FC1
configs and one sm107 MXFP8 FC1 config. Resolving every menu row on
SM100 and SM107 shows that only those 64-wide FC1 configs change.
4. **Two blocks per SM, one of them waiting** (`batched_gemm_config.py`,
`batched_gemm_kernel.py`). The 32-wide MXFP4×BF16 FC1 allocates all 512
tensor-memory (TMEM) columns, so only one block (CTA) can run per SM.
#6832 shrank its 16-bit epilogue staging buffer, which dropped the
shared memory request just below half the SM. The hardware scheduler
does not account for TMEM, so it now places a second block on the SM.
That block spins in `tcgen05.alloc` until the first one finishes. When a
TMEM allocation leaves no room for a second block, the dynamic SMEM
request is now padded to just over half the SM. That makes the scheduler
see the same one-block limit. Kernel code is unchanged (identical SASS),
and only the affected tactics change their SMEM request.

### Measured

Each ratio is the time on `main` (with #6832) divided by the time with
this PR, so above 1 means faster. Arms ran back to back on the same GPU.
The measurements were taken on the `release-v0.7.2` tree carrying #6832;
its `flashinfer/prims_ts/` is byte-identical to current `main`.

| # | Case | B200 | GR100 (SM107) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | DeepSeek-R1 FP8 block-scale, autotuned (7168/2048/256/top-8) |
1.15x (tile-128 kernels 1.28x) | 1.17x (tile-128 kernels 1.23x) |
| 1 | second DeepSeek-FP8 shape, autotuned | 1.13x | 1.09x |
| 2 | Kimi-K3 EP, untuned, 2048 tokens | 2.74x | 1.29x |
| 3 | MXFP8×MXFP8 untuned, 2048 tokens | 1.03x (64-wide kernels 1.07x) |
1.11x |
| 4 | MXFP4×BF16 autotuned / untuned, 1 token | 1.19x / 1.20x | 1.00x
(not affected) |

- Compared with the build before #6832, the fixed tree is level on case
1 (0.98-1.00x) and on case 4 on B200, faster on case 2 (B200 1.09x,
GR100 1.57x), and on case 3 faster on GR100 (1.04x) but about 5% slower
on B200. That B200 gap comes from extra code in all of the rewritten
kernels and is not addressed here.
- MXFP4×MXFP8 untuned, which shares the case-3 menu row, is 1.10x faster
on B200.
- No change elsewhere (0.98-1.02x on both GPUs): BF16, NVFP4, MXFP8 at 1
token, MXFP4×BF16 at 8192 tokens, Kimi-K3 at 1 token, an all-local
DeepSeek-V4-Pro control, and the trtllm-gen MoE backend.

### [5262bbb](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/5262bbb15937d8abdcd167a19297721ed8351761)

- **作者**: Vivian Chen NV
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T23:05:16Z
- **提交信息**: fix(prims_ts): index split-KV partials by the runtime split count (#8078)

## 📌 Description
Fixes #8077. Since #6925, PrimTS decode picks the number of KV splits at
run time, but the partial-O workspace is still sized for sm_count splits
(148 on B300). Most plans use far fewer splits, so most of that memory
is never used. For a head_dim 512 decode plan set (batch 1..1024 × q_len
1..4) the workspaces add up to 16 GiB.

This PR changes how partial-O is laid out:

- partial-O is sized by the number of splits the launch actually uses.
The kernel now uses that number, not sm_count, to compute where each
split writes its partial result. A plan that splits the KV 74 ways
reserves 74 entries per KV head instead of 148. The fused reducer and
the separate reduction kernel use the same offset, and the split count
is a runtime value, so no new kernels are compiled.

- The split counters move to the end of the workspace. Each counter
tracks how many splits of one (batch, KV head) have finished, so the
last one can do the reduction. They used to come right after partial-O,
so their position changed with the plan size. Now they are always in the
last bytes of the buffer. Because of that, plans on one device can share
a single zeroed workspace sized for the largest plan.

- Other paths are unchanged: cluster-SMEM reduction, launches that don’t
use the compact grid, plans without split-KV, and MLA decode keep their
current layout.

Measured on B300, 16/2 heads, head_dim 512, FP8 Q, NVFP4 KV, 4,096 plans
(batch 1..1024 × q_len 1..4):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Scratch, one workspace per plan (summed) | 16,376 MiB | 402 MiB |
| One shared workspace for all plans | not supported | 4.65 MiB |
| Compiled kernels | 10 | 10 |
| Cold pre-plan time | 82.5 s | 82.1 s |

Latency on B300: warm-L2 CUDA graphs, attention + reduction, median of
interleaved main / this PR / main trials (ABBA). The last column is main
itself with all its allocations shifted by 1.5 MB, to show how much
buffer placement alone moves a point.

| case | main (µs) | this PR (µs) | this PR / main | main shifted / main
|
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D128 FP8, 16/1 heads, page 32, batch 8, q_len 4, KV 32K | 16.22 |
16.19 | 0.998 | 0.998 |
| D128 FP8, 16/8 heads, page 32, batch 1, q_len 4, KV 32K | 13.31 |
13.38 | 1.005 | 0.996 |
| D128 FP8, 16/8 heads, page 64, batch 1, q_len 4, KV 32K | 13.34 |
13.27 | 0.995 | 0.997 |
| D128 FP8, 16/8 heads, page 32, batch 2, q_len 4, KV 8K | 9.22 | 9.18 |
0.997 | 1.000 |
| D128 FP8, 16/8 heads, page 64, batch 2, q_len 4, KV 32K | 21.98 |

The first row is the case from #6925. All differences are within noise:

For example, the D512 batch 1, q_len 1, KV 8K case was 0.989× here and

Over 101 cases around these shapes, this PR averages 0.999× of main.

Outputs are bit-identical to main in 564 test cases (head_dim 64–512,
FP8 / BF16 / NVFP4 KV, q_len 1–6, all reduction paths).

### [ac51da6](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/ac51da6185c93bc231cb7abdc009ce6de88fbb97)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T22:53:28Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_indexer_det): an FP8 wide scan program on sm_103a (#8841)

The deterministic DSA indexer top-k,
`flashinfer.dsa_indexer.dsa_indexer_det_topk(..., backend="cake")`, has
two Cake variants: the default BF16 form and the opt-in FP8 form, which
#8749 added and #8781 improved. This PR changes only the FP8 form, and
only on sm_103a (measured on NVIDIA GB300). The FP8 form had no 8-query
wide program. As a result, calls planned as an unsplit wide unit ran the
6-query l6 program. On sm_103a they now run a new FP8 wide program. B200
(sm_100a) and sm_107a keep their FP8 dispatch, because this PR registers
no FP8 wide program there. Of the five shapes, only s1_8k_on_64k is
planned as wide on GB300. It runs 1.13x faster than the previous Cake
FP8 form and 1.32x faster than DeepGEMM + FlashInfer top-k. The other
four rows keep their program, so their 1.00x against the previous Cake
FP8 form is parity, not a speedup.

**NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), CUDA 13.4, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.**
All rows use top-k 2048, key ratio 1 and causal queries (each segment's
queries are its last positions). P1 is a recorded packed training call.
s2_4x2k_packed is 4 x 2048 queries over 18432 / 43008 / 67584 / 100352
keys. Previous Cake FP8 is the FP8 form on main before this PR (the
#8781 dispatch), reproduced in the same process. DeepGEMM + FlashInfer
top-k runs DeepGEMM `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` (branch `nv_dev`, commit
`b64107f2`) with FP32 per-key K scales and FP32 logits. FlashInfer
`top_k_ragged_transform(deterministic=True, tie_break=LARGE)` then runs
over each row's visible keys. Two DeepGEMM arms were measured on every
row, and the table reports the faster one (the ragged top-k arm, which
reads the row-padded logits in place). Each time is the CUPTI GPU
interval over every kernel that the call launches, with cold L2 and
eager launch. Cake arms time a prepared runner into caller-owned outputs
and workspace. Each value is the median over three arm orders (A then B,
B then A, interleaved). s1_8k_on_64k was measured on three GPUs, and its
value is the median of the three (spread: this PR 2.801 to 2.804 ms,
previous 3.166 to 3.168 ms). "vs previous" = previous time / this PR
time. "vs DeepGEMM" = DeepGEMM time / this PR time. A value above 1
means this PR is faster. All arms return bit-identical scores and ids on
every row.

| Shape | Queries T | Keys Tkv | Segments | Previous Cake FP8 (ms) |
This PR (ms) | vs previous | DeepGEMM + FlashInfer top-k (ms) | vs
DeepGEMM |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| P1 | 16231 | 268757 | 8 | 3.173 | 3.173 | 1.00x | 3.996 | 1.26x |
| glm2k_16k | 2048 | 16384 | 1 | 0.320 | 0.319 | 1.00x | 0.347 | 1.09x |
| s1_8k_on_64k | 8192 | 73728 | 1 | 3.167 | 2.803 | 1.13x | 3.692 |
1.32x |
| s2_4x2k_packed | 8192 | 229376 | 4 | 2.700 | 2.703 | 1.00x | 3.406 |
1.26x |
| s3_cold16k | 16384 | 16384 | 1 | 1.176 | 1.175 | 1.00x | 1.706 | 1.45x

The other Cake variant, the default BF16 form, is unchanged; the kernel

### [b461888](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/b461888c9ff06c71ffd8617caecfd9414dfe4c1e)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T22:25:59Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_rmsnorm_train): twosum dw sums for the largest token counts of the sm_103a H4096 / H5120 backward (#8849)

Related issue: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/8066

`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_train` is RMSNorm for training. The forward
returns y (BF16) and rstd (FP32), and the backward returns dx (BF16) and
dw (FP32). The two modes, `deterministic=True` and
`deterministic=False`, share the forward and differ only in the
backward. Both modes support:

- [T, H] rows with BF16 or FP32 weight
- a fused residual add (H6144)
- per-head views [T,24,256] (strided) and [T,4,256] (contiguous), with a
shared w[256]

This PR follows #8577, #8626, #8655, #8704, #8810 and #8827. On sm_103a
(GB300), it changes only the `deterministic=False` backward of plain [T,
H] rows with H4096 and H5120 at the largest token counts. At those token
counts, FlashInfer main runs the single kernel from #8655. That kernel
exceeds the dw budget at every sampled grid T above a cut set for each
route. Above the cut, this PR runs the TwoSum single kernels that these
routes ran before #8655 (as of #8626). At and below the cut, FlashInfer
main's kernel is unchanged.

This is an accuracy fix, so the backward is slower on these rows. On
every bwd and 2xfwd+bwd row, new is slower than det, than SOTA and than
FlashInfer main's program. FlashInfer main's program was timed in
separate runs. The bwd ranges are:

- Against FlashInfer main's program, bwd is 0.9904x to 0.9971x on H4096
and 0.8426x to 0.8576x on H5120.
- Against det, bwd is 0.9767x to 0.9796x on H4096 and 0.8526x to 0.8741x
on H5120.
- Against SOTA, bwd is 0.9391x to 0.9718x on H4096 and 0.8079x to
0.8301x on H5120. No non-Cake candidate meets the accuracy budget on any
bwd or 2xfwd+bwd row. On those rows, SOTA is therefore the fastest
out-of-budget candidate (marked !).

**Changed windows**

The dw budget is per element atol 1e-4 + rtol 1e-4 vs FP64. In the
table, (a, b] means a < T <= b. A breach value is the worst dw error
divided by the budget.

|route (sm_103a, `deterministic=False` backward)|FlashInfer main's

- Budget breach: above each cut, FlashInfer main's kernel exceeds the dw
budget at every sampled grid T. Each grid T was sampled with 120 inputs
from each of three input families. H5120 with FP32 weight at T 262144
and T 393216 was also sampled with 240 inputs per family. Where a T has
two runs, the worse run counts.
- Above each cut, the `deterministic=True` backward's programs also
exceed the dw budget at every sampled grid T. Of the measured
candidates, only the TwoSum kernel stays within the budget there.
- Cut rule: each cut is the largest grid T (131072, 196608, 262144,
393216, 524288, 786432, 1048576) at or below which FlashInfer main's
kernel stays within the dw budget at every sampled point. Two of those
points are above 0.95 of the budget: H5120 with BF16 weight at T 262144
and T 393216 (worst 0.993). Both stayed within the budget on a rerun
with 240 inputs per family.
- Accuracy: every changed window meets the dw budget (per element atol
1e-4 + rtol 1e-4 vs FP64). In each window, the TwoSum kernel's worst dw
error is 0.0006 of the budget at every sampled T, from the first T above
the cut up to T 1048576. Each T was sampled with 120 inputs from each of
three input families.

weight dtypes, 3 T each). The "! rows" column counts the rows where no
non-Cake candidate meets the accuracy budget. On bwd and 2xfwd+bwd, that
is every row, so those SOTA/new ranges are against out-of-budget
candidates.

**Measurement**

- Latency: the median CUPTI span of a CUDA-graph replay with L2 flushed.
Each median pools 4 sessions, one per GPU of a 4-GPU GB300 node. Each
session times 201 replays per implementation and op, split over 3
interleaved rounds. Each implementation's own setup, reduction, cast and
copy kernels are inside the span.
- det, new and the non-Cake candidates of a row group run in one
process. Their order follows a balanced design over the 4 sessions x 3
rounds, so each implementation takes each position about equally often.
- det = deterministic Cake (`deterministic=True`). This PR does not
change it, and on these rows it runs the same programs as on FlashInfer
main.
- new = this PR's `deterministic=False`.
- FI main = FlashInfer main's `deterministic=False`. In bwd, this is the
kernel this PR replaces.
- FI main was timed with the same harness, but in separate runs on other
nodes, so FI main/new compares two runs. FI main was timed on an earlier
FlashInfer main that runs the same programs on these routes.
- det/new and SOTA/new compare implementations timed in the same
process.
- SOTA = the fastest non-Cake candidate that has these outputs and meets
the accuracy budget. The budget is dx atol = rtol = 1e-2 and dw per
element atol 1e-4 + rtol 1e-4 vs FP64, taking the worst of 5 seeds.
- Candidates: QuACK 0.6.5 (quack-kernels, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.1) with
its heuristic config, and QuACK 0.6.5 rmsnorm_fwd_tuned /
rmsnorm_bwd_tuned (exhaustive per-shape autotune, cached before timing);
torch.compile (torch 2.14.1+cu130, inductor mode
max-autotune-no-cudagraphs, emulate_precision_casts=True) and
torch.compile (inductor default mode, emulate_precision_casts=True) of
the explicit FP32-statistics reference; Liger-Kernel 0.8.5 (Triton
3.8.0), casting_mode gemma (FP32 math), offset 0; Transformer Engine
2.20.2 (transformer_engine_torch 2.20.2 built against torch
2.14.1+cu130), run as the FP32 problem.
  - PyTorch's fused rms_norm has no result on these rows (dtype error).
- On BF16-weight rows, library APIs that return dw in BF16 are not
matched outputs and are never chosen as SOTA.
- A/A: each process also times a second copy of det and of new.
  - Over every session, row and op, the largest |1 - A/A| is 0.0060.
- A row's A/A noise is the larger |1 - A/A| of its det and new copies.
On every bwd and 2xfwd+bwd row, det/new differs from 1 by more than the
row's A/A noise in each of the 4 sessions. No fwd row does so in all 4
sessions.
- Speedup = baseline latency / new latency (> 1: new is faster). Ratios
are computed from unrounded medians, so a few differ in the last digit
from the ratio of the printed latencies.
- Builds: det, new and SOTA were timed on an earlier build of this
branch. At the timed rows, that build runs the same programs as this
PR's head in both modes.
- Rows: for each changed route, the first T above its cut and two larger
T. Each row has fwd, bwd and 2xfwd+bwd.

Key:

- form: plain = no residual add.
- op 2xfwd+bwd = checkpointed step (forward, forward recompute,
backward).
- [rerun] = row timed in a second record run of the same harness on
another GB300 node. At these shapes, Transformer Engine fails with a
CUDA illegal memory access, also when run alone. Its failing
configurations were therefore not run, and SOTA is chosen from the
remaining candidates.
- ! (x) = no non-Cake candidate meets the accuracy budget on this row
and op. The SOTA column shows the fastest matched candidate with its dw
err/tol (dw error divided by the dw budget) in parentheses, and SOTA/new
is computed against that candidate.
- SOTA names:
  - QA = QuACK, per-shape tuned configuration
  - Q = QuACK, heuristic configuration
  - TC = torch.compile, max-autotune-no-cudagraphs mode
  - TCd = torch.compile, default mode

### [096ca39](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/096ca39406ef58a89f016a37b861e48786daa1c1)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T22:05:12Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_det_gemm): launch the K1 entry points from a binding of their key (#8843)

This PR changes the Cake `dense_projection_det_gemm` package in
`flashinfer.experimental`, the deterministic dense projection GEMM. It
is a host-side change to the BF16 entry points `projection_det_forward`,
`projection_det_dgrad`, `projection_det_wgrad` and
`dense_projection_det_gemm`. Each entry point now binds its launch once
for each key of its own tensors. The key is the device, the stream, the
entry point with its flags, the PDL flag and the tensor geometry. A
later call with the same key only rebuilds the per-call tensor views and
launches. It does no planning, no view derivation and no allocation.
Tensors that alias keep the previous path. Plans, programs and launch
arguments are unchanged, so outputs are bitwise identical to the
previous version. CUDA graph replay is also unchanged. There are no
kernel source or compiled library changes. The baseline is the previous
Cake version of the package on main. Eager sequences with more than one
call get faster. On GB200, dgrad + wgrad is 1.08-1.60x faster, and the
checkpointed step is up to 1.66x faster. On B200 the gains are up to
1.77x for dgrad + wgrad and 1.98x for the checkpointed step. On R200
they are up to 1.63x and 1.78x. The gain is largest for small and medium
shapes, where host time between launches dominates. Single-call
sequences (forward alone and wgrad alone) and all CUDA graph rows are
within noise of the previous version, at about 0.99-1.01x. This is
expected, because a single call has no host gap inside the timed span
and graph replay does not run the host path. Two rows are measurably
slower. B200 6144→32 dgrad + wgrad eager goes from 75.5 to 76.2 µs
(0.992x). R200 4096→128 forward CUDA graph goes from 11.47 to 11.61 µs
(0.988x).

**Speedup of this PR over the previous Cake version on main.** GB200
(`sm_100a`, 152 SMs), B200 (`sm_100a`, 148 SMs) and R200 (`sm_107a`, 216
SMs); CUDA 13.4, cold L2 (memset flush before each sequence). Each cell
times one sequence of entry-point calls: forward; wgrad; dgrad + wgrad;
or 2×forward + dgrad + wgrad (a checkpointed step). Each sequence runs
as eager calls and as replay of a CUDA graph of the sequence. The timed
span runs from the first kernel start to the last kernel end, so it
includes host gaps between the sequence's kernels. Shapes are layer
in→out with T tokens. 5120→64 T16231 and 6144→32 T16231 use BF16 wgrad
output, and the other shapes use FP32 wgrad output. There are 168 rows:
7 shapes × 4 sequences × 2 modes × 3 GPUs. Speedup = previous time /
this PR time, and values above 1 mean this PR is faster.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Performance**
* Eligible dense projection GEMM, forward, input-gradient, and

setup work.

convenience path. Cached workspace views are refreshed when the

affects associated workspace resources.

### [3985cf9](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3985cf93e2968aa06f2b9447120a60583917bffd)

- **作者**: Adrian
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T22:05:02Z
- **提交信息**: fix(gemm): validate cached GEMV tactics while preserving warmup reuse (#8727)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Nightly pipeline 79161607 on 2026-11-04 failed a BF16 x FP4 GEMM case
with `the gemv tactic requires m == 1, got m=4`. The autotuner's
above-largest-bucket fallback could reuse an M=1 GEMV winner for a
multi-row call.

Validate cached GEMV tactics against the runtime input shape and treat
incompatible entries as cache misses. Keep the original cache key so an
M=128 warmup's M=1 profile remains reusable by later M=1 decode calls.
GEMM tactics retain their existing cross-bucket reuse, and the default
`-1` tactic remains valid.

For repeated warmups, an optional profile-aware validation hook checks
the bucket's M while retaining the original input tensors for other
properties. This avoids rejecting and re-profiling the M=1 bucket merely
because the warmup caller has M=128. Existing validators keep their
current behavior. Bundled package configurations now pass through the
same validation boundary as other cache sources.

CPU regressions exercise the production dispatch caller,
memory/file/bundled cache hits, large-warmup-to-decode reuse, repeated
warmups without input preparation, and invalid tactic indices.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Observed in nightly pipeline 79161607 on 2026-11-04; no separate public
issue.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
* BF16×FP4 operations now select GEMV tactics only for single-row
inputs. Tuning-cache lookups distinguish single-row and larger inputs,
preventing tactics tuned for one shape domain from being reused in the
other. Compatible cached tactics remain available for matching shape
domains.
* Cached tactics are now checked against the relevant input shape before
reuse. Invalid tactics are rejected, while the default fallback remains
supported. This helps avoid applying incompatible tuning results during
both profile reuse and runtime execution.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

### [fc63d8e](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/fc63d8ec43a15b7df0c21bfbdfc8bbb6c74a9499)

- **作者**: Rohith Rachala
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T22:00:47Z
- **提交信息**: feat(autotuner): more reproducible, auditable tactic selection and representative routed-MoE profiling routes (#8451)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

An autotune cache decides which tactic every later process runs (#7884).
This PR makes the cached choice more representative, reproducible and
auditable:

- **Representative routed-MoE profiling routes.** Routed MoE
(`trtllm_*_routed_moe`, Prims-TS) profiles buckets up to the live batch
on the caller's routes. A framework warm-up of identical dummy tokens
sends every row to the same `top_k` experts, so those buckets were tuned
for a load real traffic never has. If the rows a bucket profiles reach
fewer than half the distinct experts that balanced routing would,
`make_repeating_tensor_initializer` now samples balanced routes for that
bucket; real routes, including skewed ones, are still used.
- **Opt-in near-tie settling, `autotune(..., tie_tolerance=t)`.** Dozens
of tactics often measure within noise of the fastest, so the strict
argmin picks a different one in almost every fresh process. With `t >
0`, the tactics within `t` of the fastest that are enumerated before it
(at most 4) are re-timed against it, and the first that stays within `t`
is kept. Enumeration order is the same in every process, so separate
processes agree more often, though not always (see Results). `t = 0`
(default) keeps today's behavior.
- **Selection record.** Entries saved by `autotune(cache=...)` /
`save_configs` gain `{"time_ms", "runner_up_ms", "margin",
"candidates"}` after their policy, so near-ties are visible in the file.
Lookups ignore it; older files load as before, and main still loads
files that contain it.
- **Docs** (`docs/autotuning.rst`, "Auditing Tuned Configs"): the
record, the tolerance, `AutoTuner.get().repeat` as the sample budget,
and pre-warming.

### Results

One GB300, CI image `flashinfer/flashinfer-ci-cu130:20260930-b1420f1`,
main `29386274`.

Routed FP4 MoE (`trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe`, DeepSeek-V3 MoE
shape: hidden 7168, intermediate 2048, 256 experts, top-8, NVFP4), tuned
on 640 identical warm-up rows, then each bucket's pick timed on balanced
routes (CUPTI, CUDA graph, cold L2; median over 6 fresh processes):

| bucket | 16 | 32 | 64 | 128 | 256 | 512 | 768 | 1024 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| main (µs) | 381.9 | 608.9 | 808.3 | 904.5 | 914.7 | 931.6 | 938.8 |
951.4 |
| this PR (µs) | 380.8 | 604.4 | 802.1 | 894.3 | 904.9 | 923.7 | 938.7 |
951.7 |

Buckets up to the warm-up size run 0.3-1.1% faster; 768 and 1024 were
already sampled. With balanced live routes, the two trees match within
0.1%.

#7884's reproducer (`trtllm_bf16_moe`, 7 buckets from 16 to 1024, 5
fresh processes per arm):

| shape | `tie_tolerance` | buckets whose pick differs | process pairs
with the same pick | kept vs. fastest tactic | tuning time per process |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-V3 | 0 (default, as main) | 7 / 7 | 20% | +0.02% | 120.8 s |
| DeepSeek-V3 | 0.005 | 3 / 7 | 79% | +0.21% | 122.4 s |
| Mixtral-8x7B | 0 (default, as main) | 6 / 7 | 41% | +0.14% | 24.4 s |
| Mixtral-8x7B | 0.005 | 1 / 7 | 91% | +0.17% | 24.6 s |

"Kept vs. fastest" is the mean slowdown of the kept tactics against the
fastest one, from a separate 12-process survey. For comparison,
`AutoTuner.get().repeat = 50` (5x the samples) changed only one bucket
at 3.7x the tuning time, and pre-warming cut tuning from 431 s to 124 s
without making picks repeat.

<details><summary>Benchmark script (routed MoE table)</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Autotune routed NVFP4 MoE on a warm-up batch, then time the picks on balanced routes.

A serving framework usually autotunes during a warm-up forward on identical
dummy tokens, so every row of the live batch routes to the same top_k experts.
This script reproduces that with trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe: one call on
a live batch whose rows all route to the same experts ("warmup" source), or on
balanced routes ("balanced" source, what real traffic looks like), inside
autotune(True). Each tune runs in a fresh process with its own cache file.
The same process then times, on balanced routes, the tactic each bucket picked
(CUPTI, cold L2).

Run it once with each FlashInfer build, then compare:

  python bench_routed_moe_autotune_routes.py --out-dir out-main
  python bench_routed_moe_autotune_routes.py --out-dir out-pr
  python bench_routed_moe_autotune_routes.py --compare out-main out-pr

Default shape: DeepSeek-V3 MoE (hidden 7168, intermediate 2048, 256 experts,
top-8), one GPU holding all experts. Weights are random NVFP4 bytes: kernel
time does not depend on their values.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

OP = "flashinfer::trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe"


def parse_args(argv=None):
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    p.add_argument("--out-dir", help="fresh directory for caches and results")
    p.add_argument("--compare", nargs=2, metavar=("BEFORE", "AFTER"))
    p.add_argument("--labels", default="main,PR")
    p.add_argument("--sources", default="warmup,balanced")
    p.add_argument("--runs", type=int, default=3, help="fresh processes per source")
    p.add_argument("--live-rows", type=int, default=640)
    p.add_argument("--tune-max", type=int, default=1024)
    p.add_argument("--buckets", default="16,32,64,128,256,512,768,1024")
    p.add_argument("--hidden", type=int, default=7168)
    p.add_argument("--intermediate", type=int, default=2048)
    p.add_argument("--experts", type=int, default=256)
    p.add_argument("--top-k", type=int, default=8)
    p.add_argument("--iters", type=int, default=100)
    p.add_argument("--dry-run-iters", type=int, default=10)
    p.add_argument("--worker", action="store_true", help=argparse.SUPPRESS)
    p.add_argument("--source", help=argparse.SUPPRESS)
    p.add_argument("--cache", help=argparse.SUPPRESS)
    p.add_argument("--result", help=argparse.SUPPRESS)
    return p.parse_args(argv)


def picks_from_cache(path: Path, hidden: int) -> dict[int, list]:
    """Bucket (rows) -> tactic of every routed FP4 MoE entry in a cache file."""
    out = {}
    width = re.compile(r"\((\d+), %d\)" % (hidden // 2))  # FP4 hidden_states
    for key, value in json.loads(path.read_text()).items():
        if key.startswith("_") or OP not in key:
            continue
        m = width.search(key)
        if m and isinstance(value, list) and len(value) > 1:
            out[int(m.group(1))] = value[1]
    return out


def worker(a) -> int:
    import torch
    from flashinfer import ActivationType, RoutingMethodType, fp4_quantize
    from flashinfer.autotuner import AutoTuner, autotune
    from flashinfer.fused_moe import trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe
    from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time
    from flashinfer.utils import device_support_pdl

    dev = torch.device("cuda")
    E, K, H, I = a.experts, a.top_k, a.hidden, a.intermediate
    g = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(1)
    w13 = torch.randint(0, 256, (E, 2 * I, H // 2), dtype=torch.uint8, device=dev, generator=g)
    w2 = torch.randint(0, 256, (E, H, I // 2), dtype=torch.uint8, device=dev, generator=g)
    w13_sf = (torch.rand(E, 2 * I, H // 16, device=dev, generator=g) + 0.5).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
    w2_sf = (torch.rand(E, H, I // 16, device=dev, generator=g) + 0.5).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
    scale = torch.full((E,), (1.0 / 448.0 / 6.0) ** 2, device=dev)
    pdl = device_support_pdl(dev)

    def hidden(rows: int, seed: int):
        gh = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(seed)
        x = torch.randn(rows, H, device=dev, generator=gh).to(torch.bfloat16) * 0.1
        xq, xsf = fp4_quantize(
            x, torch.tensor([448.0 * 6.0], device=dev), sf_vec_size=16,
            sf_use_ue8m0=False, is_sf_swizzled_layout=False,
        )
        return xq, xsf.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).reshape(rows, -1)

    def packed(expert_ids):
        weights = torch.full(expert_ids.shape, 1.0 / K, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
        return (expert_ids.to(torch.int32) << 16) | weights.view(torch.int16)

    def balanced(rows: int, seed: int):
        gr = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(seed)
        return packed(torch.rand(rows, E, device=dev, generator=gr).topk(K, dim=1).indices)

    def op(topk_ids, xq, xsf):
        return trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe(
            topk_ids, None, xq, xsf, w13, w13_sf, None, None, None, None,
            w2, w2_sf, None, scale, scale, scale, E, K, None, None, I, 0, E, None,
            RoutingMethodType.Renormalize.value, True, pdl, ActivationType.Swiglu.value,
            tune_max_num_tokens=a.tune_max,
        )

    rows = a.live_rows
    if a.source == "warmup":  # identical dummy tokens: every row picks the same experts
        same = torch.randperm(E, device=dev, generator=g)[:K].to(torch.int32)
        live = packed(same.expand(rows, K).contiguous())
    else:
        live = balanced(rows, seed=7)
    with autotune(True, cache=a.cache):
        op(live, *hidden(rows, seed=2))
    torch.cuda.synchronize()

    picks = picks_from_cache(Path(a.cache), H)
    tuner = AutoTuner.get()
    misses_before = tuner.stats.cache_misses
    times = {}
    for b in [int(x) for x in a.buckets.split(",")]:
        ms = bench_gpu_time(
            op, input_args=(balanced(b, seed=1000 + b), *hidden(b, seed=3000 + b)),
            enable_cupti=True, use_cuda_graph=True, cold_l2_cache=True,
            dry_run_iters=a.dry_run_iters, repeat_iters=a.iters,
        )
        times[b] = statistics.median(ms)
    result = {
        "source": a.source, "live_rows": rows, "gpu": torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
        "picks": {str(b): t for b, t in sorted(picks.items())},
        "median_ms": {str(b): t for b, t in times.items()},
        "cache_misses_while_timing": tuner.stats.cache_misses - misses_before,
    }
    Path(a.result).write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=1))
    return 0


def drive(a) -> int:
    out = Path(a.out_dir)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for run in range(1, a.runs + 1):
        for src in a.sources.split(","):
            cache, result = out / f"{src}-{run}.cache.json", out / f"{src}-{run}.json"
            if cache.exists() or result.exists():
                sys.exit(f"{cache} or {result} exists; use a fresh --out-dir")
            cmd = [sys.executable, os.path.abspath(__file__), "--worker", "--source", src,
                   "--cache", str(cache), "--result", str(result)]
            cmd += [f"--{k.replace('_', '-')}={v}" for k, v in vars(a).items()
                    if k in ("live_rows", "tune_max", "buckets", "hidden", "intermediate",
                             "experts", "top_k", "iters", "dry_run_iters")]
            print(f"[{src} run {run}/{a.runs}]", flush=True)
            subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)
    print(summary(out, a.labels.split(",")[0]))
    return 0


def load(out: Path) -> dict[str, list[dict]]:
    runs: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
    for f in sorted(out.glob("*-[0-9]*.json")):
        if not f.name.endswith(".cache.json"):
            r = json.loads(f.read_text())
            runs.setdefault(r["source"], []).append(r)
    return runs


def cell(rs: list[dict], b: str) -> tuple[str, float]:
    tactics = " / ".join(str(r["picks"].get(b)) for r in rs)
    return tactics, statistics.median(r["median_ms"][b] for r in rs)


def summary(out: Path, label: str) -> str:
    runs = load(out)
    lines = [f"{label}: GPU {next(iter(runs.values()))[0]['gpu']}"]
    for src, rs in runs.items():
        lines.append(f"source={src}  runs={len(rs)}  cache misses while timing="
                     f"{sum(r['cache_misses_while_timing'] for r in rs)}")
        for b in rs[0]["median_ms"]:
            tactics, ms = cell(rs, b)
            lines.append(f"  bucket {int(b):5d}: {tactics:40s} {ms * 1e3:9.1f} us")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def compare(a) -> int:
    before, after = load(Path(a.compare[0])), load(Path(a.compare[1]))
    lb, la = a.labels.split(",")
    gpu = before["warmup"][0]["gpu"]
    print(f"GPU: {gpu}. Tactic = [tile_N, config]; one entry per fresh process.\n")
    print(f"| bucket | {lb} pick | {lb} us | {la} pick | {la} us | {lb} / {la} "
          f"| balanced-source pick | us |")
    print("|---:|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---|---:|")
    for b in before["warmup"][0]["median_ms"]:
        tb, mb = cell(before["warmup"], b)
        ta, ma = cell(after["warmup"], b)
        ref = after.get("balanced") or before.get("balanced")
        tr, mr = cell(ref, b) if ref else ("-", float("nan"))
        print(f"| {b} | {tb} | {mb * 1e3:.1f} | {ta} | {ma * 1e3:.1f} | {mb / ma:.2f}x "
              f"| {tr} | {mr * 1e3:.1f} |")
    return 0


def main() -> int:
    a = parse_args()
    if a.worker:
        return worker(a)
    if a.compare:
        return compare(a)
    if not a.out_dir:
        sys.exit("--out-dir or --compare is required")
    return drive(a)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

Run with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0`, alternating builds: `--out-dir
main-1` on main, `--out-dir pr-1` with the route change, then `main-2`
and `pr-2` (each run is 3 warm-up and 3 balanced processes). `--compare
main-1 pr-1` prints one round's picks per process.

## Reviewer Notes

- `tie_tolerance` is opt-in because the kept tactic can be up to `t`
slower than the fastest (about 0.2% on average at `t = 0.005`). It runs
only in `choose_one`. Ranks of a tune process group see the same reduced
times, so they re-time the same candidates, and a failed re-timing (out
of memory included) only drops that candidate. With `race_default`,
near-ties that include the default tactic resolve to it.
- Naming: draft #6289 adds `TuningConfig.tie_tolerance` for a different
rule (keep the previous bucket's winner); one of the two should be
renamed if both land.
- Route check: the rows a bucket profiles are replaced when they reach
fewer than half of `E * (1 - (1 - k/E)^T)` distinct experts; identical
rows are caught from 3 rows, balanced and Zipf(1)-skewed routes are not.
Earlier caches keep their picks until re-tuned, and a degenerate warm-up
now tunes as long as real routes do (175 s vs. 118 s per process).
- The `tie_tolerance` numbers were measured with an earlier revision of
this PR that implemented the same rule.

### [f16f4ec](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/f16f4ec95af5bbfcb5b2211aea9124f5f27144ef)

- **作者**: leonardHONG
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T21:41:00Z
- **提交信息**: feat(mamba): add inference causal conv1d prefill and state update (#8273)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Add CuTe DSL inference causal-conv1d APIs for packed prefill and indexed
state updates:

- `causal_conv1d_fn`: packed variable-length prefill with `cu_seqlens`,
optional initial history, and final-state writeback through
`cache_indices`.
- `causal_conv1d_update`: ordinary decoding and speculative verification
with `state_indices` and accepted-prefix history selection.
- BF16 inputs, outputs and state; width-4 convolution; fused SiLU;
optional bias; FP32/BF16 weights.
- SD/DS state layouts, strided token rows, caller-provided output
buffers, and CUDA graph replay with changing device metadata.

State pools store raw input history. Slot -1 skips a row; slot 0 is
valid. Device metadata is read without host synchronization.

Single-sequence prefill honors the live device offsets, leaves trailing
output rows untouched, and writes history from the actual sequence end.
Speculative updates bound state accesses while computing all output
tokens; callers must still provision at least `T_max + 2` history
entries for subsequent accepted-prefix selection. Tests cover changing
lengths, slots and accepted counts during graph replay.

For batches above 32 sequences, a GPU-built chunk map replaces repeated
sequence searches. Short speculative updates use a bounded token tile
followed by an overflow tail. The FP32 FMA order, SiLU division and BF16
rounding are unchanged.

### Performance

NVIDIA B300, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0 and CuTe DSL 4.8.0.
CUPTI CUDA graph timing with cold L2, 10 warmup iterations and 20
samples, one round per backend. Times are full-call GPU latency,
including state I/O and output-layout adaptation; compilation, fixture
construction and state resets are excluded.

The prefill and speculative tables were collected in separate experiment
batches, not one rerun of every case on the final commit. The prefill
results measure the retained chunk-map path; the speculative results
measure the subsequently integrated bounded-prefix optimization.

| Prefill shape | Before fixes (us) | Retained implementation (us) |
Triton (us) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 32 x 512, C4096 | 90.497 | 90.496 | 91.137 |
| 33 sequences / 16384 tokens, C4096 | 99.905 | 88.721 | 91.329 |
| 64 x 256, C4096 | 101.057 | 88.225 | 91.185 |
| 128 x 128, C8192 | 200.562 | 171.906 | 175.554 |
| 256 x 64, C8192 | 261.443 | 179.761 | 176.786 |

The 33-sequence case uses 32 sequences of length 497 and one of length
480. The 256-sequence case improves by 31.2% over the previous
implementation but remains approximately 1.7% slower than Triton; Triton
is preferable for that measured shape. Its scratch workspace increases
from 1,028 to 10,244 bytes.

| Speculative shape | Bounds-fixed baseline (us) | Integrated
optimization (us) | Triton (us) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 x 5, C4096 | 3.392 | 2.864 | 3.600 |
| 32 x 5, C4096 | 4.368 | 3.936 | 4.000 |
| 32 x 16, C4096 | 6.976 | 6.785 | 7.760 |

These speculative rows use BF16 inputs/state, FP32 weights, no bias, SD
state layout and accepted counts of 1. Their baseline already includes
the state-bounds fixes; it is not the earlier unsafe implementation. The
Triton reference includes the state synchronization fixes isolated in
this PR.

Additional controls from the prefill experiment batch: initial-history
prefill at 1 x 8480 / C4608 takes 49.840 us versus Triton's 56.352 us;
ordinary decode at B32 / C4096 takes 2.880 us versus 3.952 us.

The benchmark, sample cases and CPU parser tests are included in this
PR. Reproduce the comparison cases with:

```bash
python benchmarks/flashinfer_benchmark.py \
    --testlist benchmarks/samples/causal_conv1d.txt \
    --output_path causal_conv1d.csv

python benchmarks/flashinfer_benchmark.py \
    --testlist benchmarks/samples/causal_conv1d_prefill.txt \
    --output_path causal_conv1d_prefill.csv
```

The samples also include shapes outside the tables above. Host
submission time and workspace are reported separately; optional
`--profile_launches` collects launch counts in a separate process to
avoid contaminating subsequent timings.

- Bounds and chunk-map changes: 40 GPU test cases passed across the
implementation/fix runs.
- Integrated speculative optimization: 18 targeted cases and 4
prefill/decode compatibility cases passed.
- Five benchmark parser/sample cases passed.
- Five targeted Compute Sanitizer memcheck cases passed with zero
device-memory errors. CUDA driver API probing reports were suppressed
with `--report-api-errors no`; memory checking and a nonzero error exit
code remained enabled.
- Ruff check and format checks passed for the updated Python files.

Coverage includes FP64 and Triton references, complete state-pool
checks, chunked-prefill/decode equivalence, shortened single-sequence
offsets, state-capacity overflow, invalid accepted counts, SD/DS
layouts, strided buffers, and graph replay with changing lengths, empty
sequences and slots. Output checks retain the original tolerances; state
comparisons and per-backend eager/graph checks are exact. These local
results do not claim that internal CI or the full repository suite has
passed.

### [824a58c](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/824a58c1dc52bcb4ea7082de431310dfe52bd587)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T21:40:28Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train): FP32 two-sum fold on SM100 from 800 rows per SM (#8840)

This PR speeds up the backward of the non-deterministic package of
Cake's SiLU-gated RMSNorm training kernel
(`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train` with `deterministic=False`)
on B200 (sm_100a), for both weight-gradient outputs, BF16 dw and FP32
dw. From 800 up to 12000 rows per SM, the backward now runs the bulk
long backward that folds its per-run dw partial sums with a guarded FP32
two-sum pair and uses FP64 only for the final column sum. This is the
same program FlashInfer already ships on sm_103a from 700 rows per SM
(#8785). Before this PR, sm_100a ran the long backward with the FP64
fold from 1280 rows per SM and a different backward below that. From
12000 rows per SM the FP64-fold long backward still runs. Below 800 rows
per SM nothing changes. The forward, every sm_103a and sm_107a route,
and the deterministic package run the same code as before.

The kernel has two Cake variants: the deterministic package
`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train` (the same API with
`deterministic=True`) and this non-deterministic package, which has a
BF16 and an FP32 weight-gradient output. Both packages ship on sm_100a,
sm_103a and sm_107a. This PR changes only the non-deterministic backward
on sm_100a.

A speedup is baseline us / new us, so a value above 1 means this PR is
faster. The previous Cake version is this package on FlashInfer main
before this PR. Summary on B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs, CUDA 13.4), as ranges
over the 14 shapes of Table 1:

| comparison (Table 1) | backward, CUDA graph (BF16 dw) | checkpointed
step, CUDA graph (BF16 dw) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| det Cake / new | 1.105-1.251 | 1.081-1.136 |
| strongest non-Cake / new | 1.101-1.218 | 1.052-1.122 |
| previous Cake / new | 0.991-1.038 | 0.994-1.023 |

The previous-vs-new comparison is carried by two A/Bs:

- **Backward A/B (Table 2).** Every in-route instance is GAIN or
NEUTRAL, and none is LOSS. FP32 dw is GAIN in all 56 instances. BF16 dw
is GAIN in 54 and NEUTRAL in 2 (2471x48 and 2476x48, both just above 800
rows per SM).
- **Full-step A/B (Table 3).**
- [800, 3200) rows per SM: 144 of 152 cells are faster, 8 are not
faster, and none is slower.
- [3200, 12000) rows per SM: the gain is backward-only. The backward is
faster in every instance of Table 2, but the full-step A/B shows no
whole-step gain there: 26 of 72 cells are faster, 46 are not faster, and
previous / new spans 0.991..1.014.

The strongest non-Cake kernel beats new in 3 cells. All three are
forward cells, which this PR does not change:

- 2476x48 fwd: torch.compile max-autotune-no-cudagraphs (best of 5)
19.296 us vs new 21.248 us (0.908)
- 2476x48 fwdg: torch.compile default (best of 5) 19.200 us vs new
21.440 us (0.896)
- 4824x32 fwdg: torch.compile default (best of 5) 23.936 us vs new
24.352 us (0.983)

In every backward and checkpointed-step row of Table 1, new is faster
than both the deterministic Cake kernel and the strongest non-Cake
kernel. "Cells below 1x" lists every cell below 1.

## How the tables were measured

- Inputs are BF16 x / z / dy of shape [T, H, 128]. dw is BF16 unless an
op says FP32 dw. All times are in us. rows/SM = T x H / 148.
- **Table 1:** CUPTI kernel time with a cold L2, the median of 10 round
medians. The det, strongest non-Cake, new and previous columns come from
the same run.
- **Table 2:** previous vs new backward on the same GPU. The reported
times are rotating buffers, eager. Each instance's verdict (GAIN /
NEUTRAL / LOSS) combines four orders: rotating or same-shape buffers,
each eager and from a CUDA graph.
- **Table 3:** previous vs new through the public API, in interleaved
processes on the same GPU, as medians over the timed sequences.
- **Strongest non-Cake kernel per row:** the fastest of FLA 0.6.0 fused
gated RMSNorm, Mamba v2.3.2 `layernorm_gated` (Triton), torch.compile
default and max-autotune-no-cudagraphs (best of 5 fresh compiles each),
and inductor's generated Triton kernel launched directly. Labels: `FLA`,
`tc-def` (torch.compile default), `tc-max` (torch.compile
max-autotune-no-cudagraphs).
- **Stages:**
  - `fwd`: one eager forward call.
  - `fwdg`: the forward replayed from a CUDA graph.
- `bwdg` / `bwdg_f32`: the backward (BF16 / FP32 dw) replayed from a
CUDA graph.
  - `ckptg`: 2 x forward + backward (BF16 dw) in one CUDA graph.
  - `stepg_f32`: forward + backward with FP32 dw in one CUDA graph.

## Cells below 1x

- **Against the strongest non-Cake kernel:** the 3 forward cells listed
above.
- **Against the deterministic Cake kernel:** 2 forward cells, both
unchanged code. These are 2476x48 fwd 0.992 (21.088 vs 21.248 us) and
2476x48 fwdg 0.992 (21.264 vs 21.440 us).
- **Previous / new, forward cells of Table 1 (12):** these run the same
forward module in previous and new.
  - 2476x48 fwd 0.995 and fwdg 0.996
  - 4824x32 fwdg 0.999
  - 10088x32 fwdg 0.9996
  - 10896x48 fwd 0.998 and fwdg 0.997
  - 18630x48 fwd 0.999 and fwdg 0.999
  - 42448x32 fwd 0.999
  - 48249x32 fwd 0.9998 and fwdg 0.9999
  - 54050x32 fwd 0.9999
- **Previous / new, backward cells of Table 1 (3):** single
measurements. In the backward A/B (Table 2), each of these shapes is
GAIN.
- 22498x48 ckptg 0.994 (508.000 / 510.960 us; round spread new 2.26 %,
previous 3.63 %)
- 54050x32 bwdg 0.991 (370.974 / 374.262 us; round spread new 3.49 %,
previous 3.41 %)
- 54050x32 ckptg 0.995 (819.676 / 824.036 us; round spread new 4.71 %,
previous 5.71 %)
- **Previous / new, full-step A/B (Table 3), [3200, 12000) rows per SM
(4), all not faster:**
  - 30233x48 ckptg 0.997 (687.353 / 689.130 us)
  - 48249x32 ckptg 0.996 (722.315 / 724.897 us)
  - 54050x32 ckptg 0.999 (817.821 / 818.925 us)
  - 54050x32 stepg_f32 0.991 (824.426 / 831.665 us)
- **Backward A/B (Table 2):** none.

That is 24 cells in all.

### [48903c6](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/48903c68b22d8ef52d6294b5af8f2855928ec355)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T21:31:19Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_hopper_msa): single-pass exact top-k select for the plain 2-chunk program (#8839)

`flashinfer.msa_ops.msa_topk_select` on Hopper (SM90) uses 32 Cake top-k
block-select programs, chosen by route. The routes differ in plain or
masked (non-visible-prefix) selection, 1 / 2 / 8 / 16 / 32 chunks per
block, 4 / 16 / 32 / 128-wide tiles, and 6 / 9 / 11 merge levels. Some
routes are latency-oriented forms for long-query shapes. This PR
regenerates one of the 32: the plain program with 2 chunks per block,
128-wide tiles and 11 merge levels. That program now runs the
single-pass exact select instead of the two-pass block select. The
two-pass form pays an extra pass whenever any column of the score row is
flagged. The selections are identical. The baseline is the previous Cake
version of the same program, already shipped in FlashInfer, timed in the
same process. Only one shape runs the new program. On that shape it is
1.09x faster when 2 of 256 columns are flagged, as in the measured model
inputs. It is about 1-2 % slower when no column is flagged: 0.99x with
no flagged column and 0.98x on random-normal scores. The other 31 top-k
programs and the 57 attention / proxy-score programs are byte-identical.
Their shapes measure 0.99x to 1.01x, which is measurement noise.

**`topk_plain_h1_tiles2048_tq256` by score class.** NVIDIA H100 80GB
HBM3 (132 SMs, sm_90a), CUDA 13.4.92, driver 535.216.03. Median kernel
time (CUPTI, cold L2), both run orders. Speedup = Previous / This PR.

| Scores | Previous (µs) | This PR (µs) | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 of 256 columns flagged (measured model inputs) | 6.080 | 5.583 |
1.09 |
| No flagged column | 5.504 | 5.568 | 0.99 |
| Random normal | 5.472 | 5.568 | 0.98 |

**Shape list, random-normal scores.** NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (132 SMs,
sm_90a), CUDA 13.4.92, driver 535.216.03. Median kernel time (CUPTI,
cold L2). Speedup = Previous / This PR. Only
`topk_plain_h1_tiles2048_tq256` runs the regenerated program.
`nvp_forced` = masked selection with the non-visible prefix forced on.
