### [5a94f96](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/5a94f96ec0d0d4a909fcfefaf23ada0574ef6551)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T21:05:22Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_mla): keep small V block scales in the NVFP4 MLA paged decode wide route (#7163) (#8837)

The experimental Cake dense NVFP4 MLA paged decode,
`flashinfer.mla.cake_mla_nvfp4_paged_decode(...)`, serves the Kimi-K3 /
DeepSeek-V3 geometry (512 latent + 64 rope channels per key). It reads
an NVFP4 query and the NVFP4 paged latent cache. Its package has seven
programs. Requests with at most 48 packed (token, head) rows use the
narrow swapped-AB schedules at 16, 32 and 48 rows (`main_rt16`,
`main_rt32`, `main_rt48`). Larger requests (H96 / H128, MTP with q_len x
heads > 48) use the two-CTA wide schedule (`main_wide`). A BF16-to-NVFP4
query quantizer and two split-KV merge programs (a warp reducer and a
CTA reducer) complete the set. This PR replaces only `main_wide`, for
#7163. The old wide program divided every V block scale by 8. Scales
below 2^-3 flushed to zero, and a stale scale byte 0x97 became an E4M3
NaN. The new program divides each token's V scales by 2^k, where k is
the smallest value in 0..3 that keeps that token's scaled V in E4M3
range. It then multiplies P by 2^(k-3) after the row sums. The baseline
is the previous Cake version of this program, and the fix makes it
slower. On the seven `main_wide` rows, old/new is 0.934–0.993 on GB300
and 0.937–0.981 on GB200, so the new program is 0.7–7.1 % slower. The
other rows use unchanged programs and read 0.990–1.005 (GB300) and
0.991–1.002 (GB200). That is within about ±1 %, the spread this setup
shows between two builds of byte-identical programs. The smallest
wide-row difference, 0.993 on GB300, is also inside that spread.

Latency is in microseconds. Each value is the median of the steady
samples of one complete call. A steady sample is a timed call whose
previous call ran the same version (old or new). A complete call is
attention, plus the split-KV merge when the plan has one. The
complete_call_h12_b8_q1_kv131072 row takes a BF16 query, so its call
also includes the BF16-to-NVFP4 query quantizer. Calls run as CUDA graph
replays, with a cold L2 before every call.

"Old" is FlashInfer main at 79cf0557 (wide program
`..._e7cb458f5e586352cfcb`). "New" is this PR
(`..._32a47bbfa05aebbc97c5`). Both ran in the same process on the same
inputs. An old/new value above 1 means this PR is faster. Ratios are
computed from the unrounded medians. GPUs: NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152
SMs, driver 580.159.03) and NVIDIA GB200 (sm_100a, 152 SMs, driver
580.126.20). Kernels were compiled with CUDA 13.4 (nvcc 13.4) and run
under PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. The shapes come from #6242. In each label, h
is heads, b is batch, q is query tokens per request, and kv is the KV
length of the longest request in the batch. The
long_split_h12_kv65536_lse row also writes the LSE. Page size is 64.

| Shape | Route | GB300 old (µs) | GB300 new (µs) | GB300 old/new |
GB200 old (µs) | GB200 new (µs) | GB200 old/new |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| long_split_h12_kv65536_lse | main_rt16 | 21.70 | 21.92 | 0.990 | 22.24
| 22.43 | 0.991 |
| trace_h12_b1_q1_kv76800 | main_rt16 | 19.52 | 19.42 | 1.005 | 19.87 |
19.87 | 1.000 |
| trace_h12_b2_q1_kv77699 | main_rt16 | 23.84 | 23.78 | 1.003 | 24.05 |
24.00 | 1.002 |

### [8550527](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/8550527512be6b5f1b75b0096ddea50cdcb07f65)

- **作者**: Brian K. Ryu
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T21:02:03Z
- **提交信息**: feat(batch_invariant): bias for `mm_bf16(batch_invariant=True)` (#8535)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

<!-- What does this PR do? Briefly describe the changes and why they’re
needed. -->

Stacked on #8361 and #8453. `flashinfer.mm_bf16(a, b, bias=bias,
backend="auto", batch_invariant=True)` accepts the operator's bias, a
bf16 vector of shape `(n,)`, with the same guarantee as the unbiased
call: an output row's bits depend on the input values, the weight shape
and the bias alone, not on the batch size, the row's position, the
configuration the dispatcher or the autotuner picks, the chunk count's
implementation or the SM count.

**Numerics.** The biased output element is `cvt_bf16(add_f32(acc,
bias[n]))`: the bias of the output column, widened from bf16 to binary32
(exact: every bf16 value is a binary32 value, a bit movement rather than
a rounding step), is added once with `add.rn.f32` to the fully reduced
fp32 accumulator, and the result is rounded once to bf16.

### Performance

**Ours with the bias against the best backend with the bias** (geomean
speedup, untuned / autotuned; decode M <= 16, mid 64 .. 1024,
prefill >= 4096):

| part | layout | cells | decode | mid | prefill | all | cells >= 0.95
(untuned) | winner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rubin NVL8 (SM107) | k | 42 | 0.72 / 0.75 | 0.97 / 0.99 | 1.05 / 1.08
| 0.92 / 0.94 | 48 % | CuTe-DSL at decode (12), cuBLASLt elsewhere (30)
|
| Rubin NVL8 (SM107) | n | 42 | 0.74 / 0.78 | 1.01 / 1.02 | 1.08 / 1.11
| 0.94 / 0.97 | 67 % | CuTe-DSL at decode (12), cuBLASLt elsewhere (30)
|
| B200 (SM100) | k | 42 | 0.72 / 0.73 | 0.90 / 0.93 | 0.96 / 1.01 | 0.86
/ 0.89 | 36 % | CuTe-DSL / tinygemm at decode (10 / 2), cuBLASLt
elsewhere (27), cuDNN (3) |
| B200 (SM100) | n | 42 | 0.72 / 0.75 | 0.95 / 0.98 | 1.00 / 1.02 | 0.89
/ 0.92 | 48 % | CuTe-DSL / tinygemm at decode (10 / 2), cuBLASLt
elsewhere (28), cuDNN (2) |

**The cost of the bias** (time with the bias / time without, geomean and
worst cell; ours = the pick, baseline = the best
backend with the bias over the best without):

| part | layout | ours, geomean | ours, worst | backends, geomean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rubin NVL8 (SM107) | k | 1.03 | 1.10 | 1.03 |
| Rubin NVL8 (SM107) | n | 1.03 | 1.10 | 1.03 |
| B200 (SM100) | k | 1.05 | 1.22 | 1.04 |
| B200 (SM100) | n | 1.04 | 1.21 | 1.04 |

### [887514e](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/887514eb356dc065cf1bc0884515f5211af59511)

- **作者**: Jimmy Zhou
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T21:01:49Z
- **提交信息**: fix(norm): cap the RMSNorm cluster at the device's largest launchable size (#8752)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

RMSNorm (and fused-add RMSNorm) split a large row across a cluster of up
to 16 thread blocks. 16-block clusters are non-portable: some GPUs
launch them and others reject them with `cudaErrorInvalidClusterSize`.
The cluster-size choice never checked which kind of GPU it was running
on.

Since #5729 halved the shared-memory target used to pick the cluster
size, fp32 RMSNorm at hidden size 131072 / 163840 picks 16 instead of 8.
On GPUs with too few SMs per GPC for a 16-block cluster it now fails to
launch. The nightly hit this on DGX Spark (GB10, SM121). fp16/bf16 at
hidden size >= 524288 already picked 16 before #5729.

This PR asks the driver for the largest cluster the current device can
launch, and caps the cluster size there. It uses
`cuOccupancyMaxPotentialClusterSize` on a tiny probe kernel with
non-portable sizes allowed, cached per device. The same pattern is used
in `cake_kda_tf32_runtime.py`. If the driver cannot answer, the cap is
the portable 8 on SM12x and 16 elsewhere.

GPUs that can launch 16-block clusters keep today's cluster sizes, so
their behavior and performance do not change.

Measured (CuTe-DSL path; "old" = pre-PR code):

| GPU | SMs | driver's max cluster | cap | old code at the 16-cluster
shapes | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RTX PRO 2000 Blackwell (SM120) | 34 | 12 | 8 | `CUDADialectError`
(invalid cluster size) on all 5 | pass |
| RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell WS (SM120) | — | 16 | 16 | pass | pass, same
cluster sizes, same kernel time |
| B200 (SM100) | 148 | 16 | 16 | pass | pass, same cluster sizes |

Shapes: rmsnorm fp32 H=131072/163840, fp16 H=524288; fused_add_rmsnorm
fp32 H=131072/163840.

A blanket "cap SM12x at 8" was tried first and dropped. On the RTX PRO
6000 it slowed `rmsnorm` fp32 H=131072 (64 rows) from 45.5 to 55.1 us
and bf16 H=1048576 from 1858 to 2603 us. `fused_add_rmsnorm` fp32
H=131072 fell back to one block per row, going from 8.6 to 248 us at 1
row.

Not changed here: `flashinfer/cute_dsl/rmsnorm_fp4quant.py` and
`add_rmsnorm_fp4quant.py` have the same 1-16 cluster loop and can also
pick 16. They are a separate module; happy to extend the cap to them
here or in a follow-up.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Fixes #8745. Regression introduced by #5729.

### [f53e200](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/f53e2001fe6c1d1fbf7de1251fe87c1f81f67e5c)

- **作者**: Ka-Hyun Nam
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T21:01:26Z
- **提交信息**: perf(gemm): avoid constructing a Stream in _get_stream_cache_buf (#8696)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

#8221 moved every GEMM workspace to `_get_stream_cache_buf`, which keys
on `torch.cuda.current_stream(device).cuda_stream`. That call constructs
a Python `Stream` object on every GEMM call, about 3 µs of host time,
and small-M GEMMs are launch-bound enough for it to show up as a perf
regression (reported on Rubin NVL72 for `group_gemm_fp8_nt_groupwise` at
M=16 and `mm_fp4` cudnn / cudnn_autotune at M=64 to 512).

This PR keys on `torch._C._cuda_getCurrentRawStream(index)` instead,
which returns the same handle without building the object. The key is
unchanged, so per-stream isolation and capture-stream behaviour from
#8221 are unchanged.

B200, host-side only:

| | before #8221 | #8221 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspace helper, µs per call | 0.34 | 3.35 | 0.53 |
| `bmm_fp8` cublas, M=64 N=7168 K=2304, host enqueue µs per call (two
runs) | 30.1 / 29.3 | 38.4 / 34.2 | 28.9 / 30.2 |

Not verified: Rubin numbers and the three reported cases themselves
(`bmm_fp8` cublas stands in because it goes through the same helper),
and whether other costs from #8221 contribute. The Rubin host is likely
slower at Python than the one measured, so the regression there is
probably larger than shown.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Follow-up to #8221.

### [dcf0753](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/dcf0753fac6d691cb46b6034d6d82e0410972613)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T20:44:18Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_gdn_det): key the chunk-table cache on the dhu_scan pin (#8834)

`_chunk_meta` in `flashinfer/experimental/cake_gdn_det_train` caches
host-built chunk tables, keyed on the layout and the plan pins. That key
never included `dhu_scan`. Since #8820, the table depends on `dhu_scan`:
on sm_107a, priced split backward plans for value-head groups of two use
the serial adjoint scan unless the caller pins `dhu_scan`. With
`host_cache=True`, a pinned call could reuse the serial table an
unpinned call had cached for the same layout. The reverse could also
happen, with an unpinned call reusing a pinned call's split table. As a
result, the backward segmentation depended on which calls ran first.
Calls that don't pass `dhu_scan` were not affected. CodeRabbit reported
this on #8820.

This PR adds `dhu_scan` to the cache key. A new test runs an unpinned
call followed by a pinned call, then the reverse order. It covers the
pins `tc` and `reg` on layouts with 8 and 16 key heads, at 216 SMs on
sm_107a. The existing cache test now also covers a 16-head layout.

Performance is unchanged. For both default and pinned calls, the chunk
tables match main on all 23 representative rows at 148, 152, 208, 212
and 216 SMs (115 of 115), so the same kernels are launched.

### [e042ba8](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/e042ba88162266cebdd9b204a3c4a8d2e4dffc50)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T20:07:57Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_vsa_sm120): pack the last partial wave of the SM120 VSA work plan (#8829)

This PR changes the host planner of
`BlockSparseAttentionWrapper(backend="vsa_sm120_blk64")`, the SM120 /
SM121 Cake kernels added by #8799. Two persistent kernels run one host
plan with bitwise-equal outputs: `vsa_sm120_blk64` (two 128-thread CTAs
per SM) and `vsa_sm120_blk64_pair` (one CTA of two 4-warp groups per
SM). Each SM has two virtual CTAs. When a plan has fewer than three rows
((head, query block) pairs) per virtual CTA, the planner can now pack
the last partial wave. The items of every full wave keep their places.
The items of the last partial wave fill all virtual CTAs up to the least
common load. A row is cut where a virtual CTA fills up, so its parts can
be any size. The planner uses the packed plan of either kernel when its
cost model predicts that it beats the previous uniform plan. On some
shapes, the same choice switches to the other kernel and keeps the work
table unchanged. The planner skips packing when the K and V of all KV
heads exceed 128 MB in 16 bits, which is the RTX PRO 6000's L2 size. The
limit drops to 32 MB when there are fewer rows than virtual CTAs. Above
these limits, packed plans measured slower. This PR changes only
`flashinfer/cake_vsa_sm120.py` and its tests. The kernels, the API and
the numerics contract stay the same. The parts of a split row still
merge in part order, so outputs stay deterministic from run to run.

The change is host-only, so it covers every variant of this backend:
BF16 and FP16 inputs, head dim 128, 64 x 64 blocks, optional LSE, and
GQA. The baseline is FlashInfer main at 7729459f (the merge of #8799).
On the 22 shapes from #8799, the geomean speedup is 1.028, and the 7
packed shapes reach 1.078. On 26 additional shapes, the geomean is
1.059. In total I measured 100 shapes: these 48 plus 52 that stress
large K/V footprints and the planner's limits. Across all 100, the
geomean is 1.043, 82 shapes reach 1.0 or more, and the slowest shape
runs at 0.970.

I measured on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120,
188 SMs) with driver 595.84.01, CUDA 13.0 (kernels JIT-built by nvcc
13.0.88) and torch 2.14.1+cu130. `flashinfer.testing.bench_gpu_time`
timed `wrapper.run` with CUPTI and a cold L2. Each value is the median
over 3 interleaved rounds x 3 input placements (allocator offsets of 0,
22 and 46 MiB). Speedup = main / this PR, so a value above 1 means this
PR is faster. The Plan column shows whether this PR's plan for a shape
is packed, uses the other kernel with the same work table, or is
unchanged. Unchanged rows show the measurement noise.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Work planning now supports automatic or explicitly enabled packing,
subject to row-count and KV-block limits.
* Packed plans distribute work across execution waves and can reduce the
maximum workload assigned to an individual processing unit.
* Block-mask planning now accepts a packing option. Specifying a fixed
partition continues to disable packing by default.
* Packing selection considers eligible execution plans and chooses the
option with the lowest estimated processing time.

### [5ff6fae](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/5ff6faebcdefbae75935ade11157d6b3a49f4610)

- **作者**: ameynaik-hub
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T20:07:50Z
- **提交信息**: feat(gdn): Rubin (sm_107a) build of the UMMA ReplaySSM MTP u-cache flush kernel, with uGPU localization (#6791)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->


## 📌 Description

Adds a Rubin (`sm_107a`) build of the UMMA ReplaySSM MTP u-cache flush
kernel and **uGPU localization** (each of Rubin's two dies works only on
its own memory). `gated_delta_rule_mtp_ucache_flush` uses it on Rubin
automatically. Results are bitwise equal to the Blackwell kernel
(`gated_delta_rule_mtp_ucache_flush_umma`; stochastic rounding draws the
same noise); other GPUs are unchanged.

On a Rubin VR200 at B = 2048 this runs **2.45× / 2.55× / 2.41× faster
than the best B200 time** at T = 1 / 4 / 8 (Rubin has ~2.5× B200's DRAM
bandwidth), at **91 % / 95 % / 90 %** of Rubin's DRAM peak. Before this
PR the Blackwell kernel reached only 52–57 % of DRAM peak on Rubin.

### Why the Blackwell kernel is slow on Rubin

1. **Only 2 CTAs per SM.** Rubin has 16 named barriers per SM (B200: 64)
and the kernel used ids up to 5. → Use ids 1–3: 4 CTAs per SM.
2. **Instruction-cache misses.** Flush and verify CTAs on one SM run
different code, and together it does not fit the instruction cache
(steps with flush rows were 10–17 % slower). → Smaller code: rolled
loops.
3. **Idle time between CTAs.** Every CTA re-does its set-up (tensor
memory, ~60 barriers); a CTA slot sat empty ~13 % of the time. →
Persistent kernel (T = 2–8): set up once, loop over work items.
4. **Traffic between the two dies.** Normal allocations spread memory
over both dies, so half the bytes cross the die-to-die link. → uGPU:
each die reads only its own memory.
5. **Split key heads at mid batch sizes.** The B200 heads-per-CTA rule
kept each key head's 4 value heads in 2 CTAs up to B = 212 per die;
every CTA repeats the per-key-head prologue, which Rubin hides less well
(1.6× B200's DRAM bytes per SM). → On sm_107a `auto_heads_per_cta` also
takes T, the flush hint and the rounding mode: 4 heads per CTA from B =
40–72 per die (later for Philox with more than 6 rounds). sm_100a keeps
its rule.
6. **Small batches are latency-bound.** At B ≤ ~32 per die a step takes
a few µs and fixed costs dominate: the row-order indirection, a launch
bound sized for 4 CTAs per SM, build options tuned at large B, and on
uGPU a second launch with its fork / join. → On sm_107a with 4 value
heads per key head: no row order on grids of at most 2 CTAs per SM, a
2-CTA/SM launch bound there, cheaper builds for 1–2 heads per CTA, one
launch over both dies' buffers for few rows (B ≤ 12 / 8 / 4 at T = 1–2 /
3–5 / 6–8), and without flush rows the persistent kernel's minimum batch
by T.

### What is in this PR

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `flashinfer/gdn_kernels/gdn_replay_mtp_umma_rubin.py`,
`_umma_helpers_rubin.py` | new: the Rubin kernel (fixes 1–3), persistent
kernel, uGPU launch, `ugpu_ucache_buffers`, heads per CTA (fix 5) and
small-batch dispatch (fix 6) on sm_107a |
| `flashinfer/gdn_kernels/gdn_decode_bf16_wy_ucache_flush.py` |
`backend="auto"` uses the Rubin kernel on SM107 and for uGPU buffers |
| `benchmarks/bench_gdn_ucache_flush.py` | `rubin` arms, `--ugpu`,
`--persistent`, DRAM % |
| `tests/gdn/test_mtp_umma_rubin.py` (new), `tests/gdn/test_mtp_umma.py`
| tests |

### uGPU: how to use it

Allocate the state pool and rings with `ugpu_ucache_buffers`; the call
itself does not change. Each die then runs half of every request's key
heads on its own SMs (one green context per die) against its own memory.

```python
from flashinfer.gdn_kernels import gated_delta_rule_mtp_ucache_flush, ugpu_ucache_buffers

state, k_cache, u_cache, g_cache = ugpu_ucache_buffers(num_slots, H, HV, u_dtype=torch.float16)

out = gated_delta_rule_mtp_ucache_flush(
    A_log, a, dt_bias, q=q, k=k, v=v, b=b,
    initial_state_source=state, initial_state_indices=slot_idx,
    k_cache=k_cache, u_cache=u_cache, g_cache=g_cache,
    hist_len=hist_len, cache_base=cache_base, restart_hist_on_flush=False,
)
```

Buffer layout: `[pool, 2, heads / 2, ...]`; element `[s, t, j, ...]` is
element `[s, t * heads / 2 + j, ...]` of the usual buffer. Make one
eager call before CUDA graph capture (creates the per-die streams).

### Performance

Rubin VR200 (212 SMs), clocks locked (SM 2376 MHz, memory 4752 MHz), H =
16, HV = 64, K = V = 128, fp16 state, bf16 rings, uGPU buffers. DRAM % =
ncu `dram__bytes.sum` ÷ time ÷ 19.15 TB/s.
B200: the best time per cell of the Blackwell kernel and this PR's
kernel (one launch, or uGPU where the driver exposes B200's two dies),
same benchmark, same shapes.
Both: CUDA graph replay, CUPTI median of 200, warm L2. **Speed-up = best
B200 time ÷ Rubin time.**

```
python benchmarks/bench_gdn_ucache_flush.py --arm rubin --ugpu --T $T --batches $B --rates 0 30 --l2 warm --no-commit   # Rubin
python benchmarks/bench_gdn_ucache_flush.py --arm {umma,rubin} [--ugpu] --T $T --batches $B --rates 0 30 --l2 warm --no-commit   # B200, best of
# stochastic rounding: --arm rubin_ph5 / rubin_lcg (umma_ph5 / umma_lcg); flush rows first: --row-order flush_first
```

## Reviewer Notes

- **Who allocates the buffers.** uGPU needs the state pool and rings
from `ugpu_ucache_buffers` (memory placement is fixed at allocation).
Serving frameworks that own the GDN state (vLLM, SGLang) would allocate
it this way on Rubin; everything else is automatic.
- **Why split heads, not V rows like #6604.** The tensor-core tiles here
cover all 128 V rows, so a V split would need M = 64 tiles. Key heads
are independent: splitting them needs only head-slice input views (the
kernel takes the full tensors' strides) and a head offset for the
stochastic-rounding counters, which keeps the results bitwise equal.
- **Launch delay between the dies (explained).** In some timed runs the
second die's kernel started 2–7 µs late (B = 128, T = 4: 28.5 instead of
25.0 µs; ≤ 1 % from B = 2048). Both per-die launches are root nodes of
the captured graph and go through the device's shared hardware work
queues; when they land on queues of the same parity, die 1 waits. It
shows only in CUPTI-timed graphs whose die kernels are root nodes: with
a predecessor node (as in a model's graph) or with CUDA-event timing it
does not occur. Pinning each green context's work queue
(`CU_DEV_RESOURCE_TYPE_WORKQUEUE_CONFIG`) removes it but relies on
undocumented driver behaviour, so it is not in this PR.
- AI-assisted (Claude Code).

### [1ba70b8](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/1ba70b81b209234419088b4131a5ee4809cc1dcb)

- **作者**: Bo Li
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T19:59:43Z
- **提交信息**: fix(prims_ts): persist compiled MoE GEMMs and fix the large-batch LDGSTS TensorMap abort (#7585)

## 📌 Description

This PR fixes three problems in the Prims-TS MoE. Each fix is its own
commit. It is rebased onto current `main`.

### 1. Persist compiled Prims-TS MoE GEMMs across processes

**Problem.** `get_compiled_gemm()` kept the compiled batched GEMMs only
in an in-process dict. As a result:

- every process recompiled every GEMM it used;
- this held even when the tactics came from a tactic file;
- autotuning profiles every FC1 × FC2 config pair of the offered tile_N
candidates, so a new FC1 or FC2 config costs a CuTe DSL compile of about
4 s.

**Fix.** The GEMMs are now also written to the FlashInfer JIT directory,
as module `prims_ts_moe_gemm` through `JitSpecCuteDsl`. Later processes
load them from there.

**Invalidation.** The module is invalidated as a whole when any of these
change:

- the batched GEMM sources (`batched_gemm/`, `cutlass_dsl.py`, and the
FP4 conversion helpers in `cute_dsl/fp4_common.py` that the GEMM
epilogue uses);
- the CuTe DSL stack;
- the compile architecture.

Within the module, a GEMM is named after:

- its config;
- the compile-time types of its launch arguments (pointer element type,
address space, alignment);
- the compile options;
- the `FLASHINFER_PRIMS_TS_DEBUG_CHECKS` setting;
- the device capability.

**Concurrency.** A cache miss compiles outside the module lock, so the
threads of a parallel tactic precompile, and the ranks of an EP job,
keep compiling concurrently.

**JIT layer change.** The MoE GEMMs are compiled without TVM-FFI and
take CuTe pointers. `JitSpecCuteDsl` and
`build_and_load_cute_dsl_kernel` therefore gain `enable_tvm_ffi=False`:

- the kernel is written as a plain object file (`dump_to_object`),
because `export_to_c` would also generate a C header, which needs every
argument annotated;
- it is reloaded with `load_module(enable_tvm_ffi=False)`;
- the default path (`enable_tvm_ffi=True`) is unchanged.

**Autotuning wall time.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash experts (hidden 5120, 384
experts, top-6, MXFP4 weights × MXFP8 activations), EP8 on 8× B300,
Prims-TS compute, 1..4096 tokens per rank (13 batch sizes):

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Empty GEMM cache, new tactic file | 1960 s (144 GEMMs compiled) | — |
| GEMMs on disk, new tactic file | — | 1509 s (all of it profiling) |
| Tactic file present | 111 s (recompiles the 26 chosen GEMMs) | 4 s |

### 2. Describe LDGSTS-gathered activations by their compact storage

**Problem.** Autotuning the MXFP4 × MXFP8 MoE on 8192 expert rows (1024
tokens per rank at EP8, hidden 5120, 48 local experts, top-6) aborted
the process with `CUDA Dialect Assertion failed on CUDA error:
cudaErrorInvalidValue`.

**Root cause.**

- The failing launch is the FC1 GEMM of tactic `[128, 8]`
(`MxFp4xMxFp8_FC1_HighThroughputFusedLdgsts`), which gathers its
activations with LDGSTS.
- `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled` returns `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE` in the
host launch code. The activation descriptor has dims `[5120, 55168, 48]`
and an expert stride of `-254410752` bytes.
- The activations were described as a padded `(K, N, L)` tensor. Its
expert stride, N·K = 55168 × 5120 FP8 elements (2^28.07), overflows when
the TensorMap encoding scales it to bits in 32-bit arithmetic.
- At 4096 rows, N·K is 2^27.2, which is why smaller batches tuned and
ran.

**Fix.**

- An LDGSTS-gathered operand is never read through that TensorMap: the
gather loads it with `cp.async`, and the descriptor is only prefetched.
- The operand is now described by its compact `(K, num_tokens)` storage,
as the TMA gather4 path already does.
- This applies to both the swap-AB (B) and non-swap-AB (A) layouts.
- All 73 MXFP4 × MXFP8 tactics of the 8192-row shape now launch.

### 3. Resolve the compile target on the launch device

**Problem.** `get_compiled_gemm()` takes the launch device from the IO
tensors, which need not be the current device, but resolved parts of the
compile target from the current device:

- the CuTe DSL architecture in the in-process cache key;
- the `JitSpecCuteDsl` module directory and `meta.json` arch
(`_get_compile_arch()`);
- the device capability in the persisted kernel name;
- with the persistent cache disabled, the `cute.compile` call itself.

On a host mixing GPU architectures, a GEMM compiled for the launch
device could be stored under the other device's architecture and name.

**Fix.** All of them are now resolved with the launch device made
current.

## 🔍 Related Issues

None.

## 🧪 Tests

- the persisted name changes with the config, FC1/FC2, pointer alignment
and dtype, compile options, debug checks and capability;

shape);

### [ba976cb](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/ba976cb8ac6c75d61ebc213e900714bd9e26f4c8)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T19:57:10Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsv4): SM107 four-stage FP8 64-head M64 program issues QK(t) without waiting for PV(t-1) (#8828)

The Cake backend of `trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4` has 50
programs: BF16 and FP8 programs for 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128 query heads
(several bodies per head count, picked per shape by the host route) and
an NVFP4-KV decode family. On sm_107a it ships seven FP8 programs for
the DeepSeek-V4 decode route. One of them is the four-stage K/V ring
sibling of the 64-head M64 multi-tile program, added in #8818, and this
PR updates it.

In a single-wave launch, on work items with at least four K/V tiles, the
program made the QK MMA of tile t wait until the PV MMA of tile t - 1
had been issued. That ordering frees a K/V stage early in the two-stage
ring. With four stages it only makes QK, softmax and PV run one after
another, so the four-stage program now drops it. The program keeps its
arguments, host route and output bits.

Speedups are measured against the previous Cake version, the four-stage
program as shipped by #8818. The 64-head top-k 4x decode shapes of width
640 with 120, 132 and 192 rows run 1.0907x-1.1141x faster. The
width-1152 shape with 192 rows runs 1.0486x-1.0488x faster. The other 24
shapes read 0.9955x-1.0274x, including the five SWA-only shapes, whose
program this PR does not change. The slowest are the 32- and 16-head
2048-row prefill shapes, at 0.9955x-0.9958x and 0.9969x-0.9979x.

NVIDIA R200 (208 SMs), sm_107a, CUDA 13.4, two boards. Each time is per
call, from eight back-to-back calls with PDL in one CUDA graph with one

### [28d5a3d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/28d5a3dc86651f5cf9a8d9c03ad5a5bbc94fdabd)

- **作者**: Alex Yang
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T19:40:32Z
- **提交信息**: fix(comm): warn on the deprecated UlyssesCommunicator max_elems alias (#8583)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

#4876 (merged 2026-10-24) renamed the keyword-only capacity argument of
`UlyssesCommunicator.__init__` from `max_elems` to `max_bytes`;
v0.7.2.post1
callers raised `TypeError` (#8000, reported by Kangbin Tu in Slack
`#swdl-flashinfer-dev` on 2026-10-28). #4924 (merged 2026-11-03) brought
the
keyword back on `main` as a silent "legacy" alias, which is why #8107,
the
standalone fix by 0z5a that adds the alias *with* a
`DeprecationWarning`, now
conflicts with `main`. #8107 is being picked onto `release-v0.7.3`
instead
(squashed, with the author's credit), and this PR brings `main` to the
same
contract:

- `max_elems=` emits a `DeprecationWarning` pointing at
  `max_bytes=max_elems * dtype.itemsize` (same text as #8107);
- passing both keywords or neither is rejected through the joint rank
  validation with #8107's messages ("pass max_bytes or the deprecated
max_elems, not both"; "max_bytes is required"), so the release branch
and
  `main` behave and read the same;
- docstrings and `docs/api/comm.rst` describe the alias as deprecated
since
v0.7.3 and scheduled for removal in a future release (`CONTRIBUTING.md`
  deprecation window);
- CPU-only tests (signature, `_normalize_capacity` conversion and every
invalid alias form) and gloo constructor tests asserting the warning for
  fp16/bf16/fp32 and its absence for `max_bytes=`.

The alias mechanics (conversion, mutual exclusion, joint validation,
`comm.max_elems` property) are unchanged from #4924. One remaining
difference from the release pick: `main` keeps #4924's explicit
`max_elems <= 2**31 - 1` check (the v0.7.2 element limit), while #8107
relies
on the converted byte capacity staying under `_MAX_CAPACITY_BYTES`.

**Release notes line:** `UlyssesCommunicator(max_elems=...)` now emits a
`DeprecationWarning`; use `max_bytes` (scheduled for removal in a future
release).

## What actually ships in v0.7.3

The `v0.7.3` label on this PR tracks the `main` side of #8000; the
release branch is already fixed, so the two lines diverge until this
merges:

- **`release-v0.7.3`** carries #8107 by @0z5a as a squashed pick
(1825f0dde, author credited) plus a follow-up (daa3d3c35) that restores
the v0.7.2 `comm.max_elems` attribute and documents the alias in
`docs/api/comm.rst`. So in the 0.7.3 wheels
`UlyssesCommunicator(max_elems=...)` works, emits a `DeprecationWarning`
pointing at `max_bytes=max_elems * dtype.itemsize`, and passing both
keywords or neither raises through the joint rank validation.
- **`main`** got the alias silently from #4924 (merged 2026-11-03),
without the warning or those two error messages, which is why #8107 now
conflicts with `main` and why this PR exists: it brings `main` to the
same contract as the release branch, so the next release does not
regress the deprecation signal that 0.7.3 ships.
- Once this merges, #8000 can close and #8107 can be closed as
superseded (its content shipped in 0.7.3 via the release-branch pick).

## 🔍 Related Issues

Closes #8000. Related: #4876 (rename), #4924 (silent alias on main),
#8107 (the fix picked onto release-v0.7.3).

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
* CUTLASS BF16 matrix and batched-matrix operations now enforce
alignment requirements: K must be divisible by 8, and N must meet the
alignment required by the output data type. When an output tensor is
supplied, its data type determines the requirement.
* Automatic backend selection now excludes unsupported CUTLASS shapes
during tuning, helping it select a valid option for unaligned output
widths.
* Batched matrix operations now handle layouts with a unit-stride batch
dimension more reliably.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
* Tuning now stops with an error identifying the operation, runner,
tactic, input shapes, and CUDA error when a failure leaves the CUDA
context unusable.
* Failed tactics can still be skipped when the CUDA context remains
usable. Tuning no longer profiles later tactics after a persistent CUDA
error.
* In distributed tuning, affected members stop participating; peers
encounter an error at a later collective or process-group timeout.

### [6ff4162](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/6ff41626ee40fc1021504f163d7e9d8c6880e4ee)

- **作者**: Brian K. Ryu
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T19:16:06Z
- **提交信息**: feat(batch_invariant): bmm_fp8(batch_invariant=True); the dispatcher becomes a ranking heuristic (#8453)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

<!-- What does this PR do? Briefly describe the changes and why they’re
needed. -->

This PR adds the second operator of the batch-invariant mode (#8361): a
keyword-only `batch_invariant: bool = False` on `flashinfer.bmm_fp8`,
backed by two fp8 classes next to the bf16 one in
`flashinfer/gemm/batch_invariant/`. It also replaces the dispatcher of
#8361 for both classes: the fitted cost model and its constants file
give way to one ranking heuristic that needs no per-part data, and the
persistent grid is sized from the device's co-resident cluster count
(see Dispatcher).

### API

```python
out = flashinfer.bmm_fp8(A, B, A_scale, B_scale, dtype, backend="auto", batch_invariant=True)
```

* `batch_invariant=True` requires `backend="auto"` (the class replaces
the backends; the autotuner is never free to pick a batch-variant
kernel). Without the flag nothing changes and the default `"cublas"`
stays.
* Supported: `A (b, M, K)` and `B (b, K, N)` both e4m3 or both e5m2 (two
classes; a mixed pair raises), `B` column-major (the transpose of a
row-major `(b, N, K)` weight, the documented layout) or row-major, `K` a
multiple of 16 and `N` of 8 (16 for a row-major `B`), 16-byte-aligned
operand bases, any `b` and `M` including 0 (`K` and `N` not empty);
`A_scale`, `B_scale` 1-element fp32 tensors; bf16 or fp16 output.
* Autotuning: under `flashinfer.autotune(True)` the autotuner profiles
the class's top configurations for the shape (op
`fp8_bmm_batch_invariant`); all of them compute the same bits.
* Batch: the unsplit class runs as one launch over the kernel's batch
mode (a dynamic third operand mode); the split classes run the batch
elements one after another. Both are the class by construction.
* Never falls back: an unsupported dtype pair, layout, alignment, scale,
output dtype, device or architecture raises
`flashinfer.batch_invariant.BatchInvariantUnsupportedError` (a
`ValueError`) naming the class and the limit.
* Accuracy: not bit-equal to any default backend. The max norm-relative
error against the exact scaled product is within 10 % of the better of
`bmm_fp8`'s cuBLAS and cuDNN backends at every tested shape (a test
asserts it, for the unsplit and the split class); the scaled output
equals `cvt_rn(mul_rn(acc, mul_rn(A_scale, B_scale)))` of the kernel's
own fp32 accumulator bit for bit (a test computes it on the CPU).

### Dispatcher

The dispatcher is a ranking heuristic shared by the bf16 and the fp8
classes (`flashinfer/gemm/batch_invariant/heuristic.py`; it replaces the
fitted cost model of #8361 for the bf16 class too). For a shape, layout,
format and part it orders the records of the class's enumerated space by
a per-tile roofline estimate and takes the first; the autotuner profiles
the first ten. The estimate uses the part's nominal numbers (SM count,
co-resident cluster capacity per cluster size from the driver's
occupancy query, MMA rate and the L2 and HBM bandwidths per SM) and a
dozen shape constants shared by every part and format: per-CTA row
efficiency, the transaction efficiency of narrow B boxes, the multicast
benefit, the fixup and per-step floors, the swizzle overrun, the 2-CTA
factor. The format enters through its structure only (element width, MMA
K step, the 8-bit kind's doubled rate). No fitted constants, no per-part
tables, no file to ship: the same code ranks a part it has never seen
from its SM count and its cluster capacity. Every record it ranks
computes the class (R3), so the heuristic only moves time.

The persistent grid is sized from the same occupancy query
(`api.persistent_clusters`): the compiled grid is the number of clusters
the device hosts at once for the configuration's cluster shape, keyed
into the kernel, instead of SMs // cluster size, which left a serial
tail of clusters wherever a GPC cannot hold a whole cluster of every SM.
A placement: the bits never depend on the grid.

### [7060fbe](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7060fbe05df12b8541376c4ab99da9e66ea98a64)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T19:14:47Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_det): split the fused forward scan and output over the value halves on R200 (#8805)

`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_det_train` is FlashInfer's
deterministic Gated DeltaNet chunked training kernel, and its outputs
and gradients are bitwise reproducible. Its variants include beta/dbeta
precision forms, head-group ratios, several scan plans, wavefront forms
and the five-CTA forward WY program. This PR adds one new program, for
sm_107a (R200) only. It splits the forward fused scan + output stage
("fwd_ho") over the two value halves. Each CTA computes one half of the
value dimension, so the grid doubles (for example, from 96 to 192 CTAs
on 1 x 16384, H 8 / HV 16). The planner uses the new program only for
single-round forward plans whose doubled grid still fits in one wave (2
x CTAs <= SMs). Of the 15 shapes below, only 1 x 16384, H 8 / HV 16 uses
it, on all three boards. Every other row launches exactly the same
kernels as main. Outputs and gradients are bitwise identical to the
previous version. The baseline is the previous version of this kernel on
FlashInfer main (speedup = main ms / PR ms, so >1 is faster; median of
interleaved clean-process cells). On the 1 x 16384, H 8 / HV 16 row,
forward + backward is 1.053x to 1.091x faster and the forward pass is
1.128x to 1.218x faster across the three boards.

**NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a) and NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a)**: unchanged; they
get no new library, the compiled programs and the launch trace are
identical to FlashInfer main, and outputs are bitwise equal.

This PR leaves the kernel's other variants unchanged (FP32 and BF16
beta/dbeta forms, HV = H, 2H and 3H head groups, split scan plans,
serial-scan tail_g3 plans, the w2/e4/e8 wavefront forms and the five-CTA
forward WY program), and the kernel ships on sm_100a (B200), sm_103a
(GB300) and sm_107a (R200).

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Performance**
* Added an optimized forward scan path for compatible newer GPUs and

---------

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [9c2158c](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/9c2158ceb7518d58b07a130d2b75ed6225c37d52)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T19:08:42Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_det): FP32-fold column-task backward for small token counts on SM103 and SM107 (#8813)

The deterministic Cake RMSNorm training package
(`cake_rmsnorm_det_train`) covers BF16 and FP32 weights, residual and
non-residual inputs, row widths H 256 (contiguous and per-head views),
512, 1536, 2048, 4096, 5120 and 6144, and the forward and backward
passes. This PR changes the backward pass on sm_103a and sm_107a, mainly
for small token counts. For H 512 to 6144 and T up to a per-width limit,
backward now runs as a single column-task kernel whose dw fold uses FP32
compensated (triple-word) arithmetic with one final rounding, replacing
the FP64 fold. dw stays fixed-order and bitwise reproducible from run to
run, and dx is unchanged. On sm_103a, the previous kernel is kept for H
512 at T <= 4, H 1536 at T <= 31 and H 2048 at T <= 2. On sm_107a, H 256
backward (contiguous and per-head views, all row counts) moves to the
two-kernel form that sm_100a already uses, which accumulates with TwoSum
in the main kernel and in the dw column reduction. On sm_107a, the PR
also raises the forward launch grid for FP32-weight H 5120 above 49152
rows from 48 to 64 CTAs per SM, with the same kernel. sm_100a is
unchanged.

Compared with the previous Cake release:
- **GB300 (sm_103a) backward:** 1.032-1.534x faster on all 92 changed
rows. Against torch.compile it is 0.657-2.177x: Cake is faster on 40 of
the 92 rows and at most 1.528 us slower on the rest.
- **R200 (sm_107a) backward:** 0.887-1.808x. It is slower on 17 of 216
rows, by at most 0.800 us. 14 of those rows are at the upper end of a
width's changed T range; the other 3 are H 256 at T 1 (BF16 and FP32)
and H 256 FP32 at T 64. Against torch.compile it is 0.285-2.339x: Cake
is faster on 173 of the 216 rows and at most 3.752 us slower on the
rest.
- **R200 (sm_107a) forward grid change:** 1.014-1.025x on 4 rows, and
1.176-1.226x against torch.compile.

**NVIDIA R200 (212 SMs), sm_107a, forward: FP32-weight H 5120 above
49152 rows (launch grid change only, 48 -> 64 CTAs per SM).** CUDA 13.4
(kernels built with nvcc 13.4), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0.
Latency is CUPTI kernel-active time per call with a cold L2. Previous
Cake is the previously shipped Cake package. Both Cake versions run
through the package's public forward entry point in the same processes,
in counterbalanced order. Each Cake value is the fastest valid process:
the lowest per-process median among processes where a repeated timing of
the new call lands within 1%. torch.compile is
`torch.compile(dynamic=False)` of the FP32 RMSNorm formula, fastest
process.

| H | weight | T | previous Cake us | Cake us | previous Cake / Cake |
torch.compile us | torch.compile / Cake |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5120 | FP32 | 49153 | 97.160 | 95.384 | 1.019 | 116.976 | 1.226 |
| 5120 | FP32 | 65536 | 130.320 | 127.152 | 1.025 | 152.376 | 1.198 |
| 5120 | FP32 | 98304 | 193.503 | 189.983 | 1.019 | 224.384 | 1.181 |
| 5120 | FP32 | 131072 | 256.471 | 253.047 | 1.014 | 297.464 | 1.176 |

All other variants of the package keep their previously shipped kernels:
the forward pass apart from the R200 grid change above, backward rows
above each width's T limit, and every sm_100a path; this family ships on
sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

### [4e417de](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/4e417deb1adf5a44ad636dc1e43d146977246c3a)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T19:06:06Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_det): serial backward state scan for priced split plans on R200 (#8820)

`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_det_train` is FlashInfer's
deterministic Gated DeltaNet chunked training kernel. Its outputs and
gradients are bitwise reproducible run to run. The kernel has beta/dbeta
precision forms, head-group ratios, split and serial scan plans,
wavefront forms and the five-CTA forward WY program. This PR changes
only the host planner of the backward pass, and only on sm_107a (R200).
Some split backward plans have a priced serial cost that favors one
serial pass. For those plans, the backward state scan (dhu_tc2) now runs
as one serial pass instead of the split form. There are no CUDA source
changes and no new library. Of the 15 shapes below, the rule engages
only 8 x 4096, H 8 / HV 16 and 4 x 4096, H 16 / HV 32, on all three
boards. Every other row launches the same kernels as main. On the two
engaged shapes, dk, dv, dg and dbeta can differ from the previous
version in the last bits; they stay deterministic run to run and well
inside the kernel's accuracy budget, and forward outputs are unchanged.
The baseline is the previous version of this kernel on FlashInfer main
(speedup = main ms / PR ms, so >1 is faster; median of interleaved
clean-process cells). On the two engaged shapes, forward + backward is
1.011x to 1.035x faster across the three boards.

- **提交信息**: perf(cake_batch_deepgemm_fp8): per-cell sm_107a routes for N=4096 K=7168 (#8824)

`cake_batch_deepgemm_fp8` is Cake's masked batch DeepGEMM FP8 kernel. It
has one route chain per architecture: sm_100a (148 SMs), sm_103a (152
SMs) and sm_107a (216 SMs). This PR changes only the host routing table
of the 216-SM sm_107a chain, and only for the N=4096, K=7168 geometry.
For that geometry, 22 (B, em4) cells now pick a different program, where
em4 is expected_m in quarter-octave bins. Every program they pick is
already shipped: bn64 in 1 cell, bn112 in 1, bn144 in 4 and bn240_k128
in 16. The PR adds and removes no programs. Keys outside these cells
keep the geometry's CTA bands. Those bands, as shipped today, are the
baseline here: the previous Cake version of this route. Over all 388
gated row-seeds, the geomean of new/previous is 0.9063 (min 0.8128, max
0.9869). All 388 are faster and none is slower.

NVIDIA R200 board class (sm_107a, 216 SMs), CUDA 13.4. Latency in µs,
from kernel-level timings of programs that are byte-identical to the
shipped ones. The two routes are measured in paired ABBA order, with 3
hot ABBA blocks per row-seed. Each timing window is warmed up and
L2-flushed. A row-seed's ratio is the median over blocks of B/A. Noise
is the maximum over blocks of |A1/A2 - 1| and |B1/B2 - 1|. Each row
shows medians over its seeds: seeds 16-18 for sets s1, s2 and s3, and
seeds 16-25 for the sweep set. The Min-max column is the range of ratios
across those seeds.

### [ae3e5a5](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/ae3e5a508407ecff7167bdf809a5667c72a8aff5)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T18:46:38Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_rmsnorm): sm_100a and sm_107a dw-accuracy backward routes (#8827)

Related issue: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/8066

`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_train` is RMSNorm for training. The forward
returns y (BF16) and rstd (FP32), and the backward returns dx (BF16) and
dw (FP32). The two modes, `deterministic=True` and
`deterministic=False`, share the forward and differ only in the
backward. Both modes support:

- [T, H] rows with BF16 or FP32 weight
- a fused residual add (H6144)
- per-head views [T,24,256] (strided) and [T,4,256] (contiguous), with a
shared w[256]

This PR follows #8577, #8626, #8655, #8704 and #8810. It changes only
the `deterministic=False` backward routes on sm_100a (B200) and sm_107a
(R200). The changed windows are listed below by reason. Rows where new
is slower than det are shown as measured.

Against det, bwd ranges from 0.77x to 1.36x on B200 and from 0.57x to
1.10x on R200. new is slower than det on 56 of 93 B200 bwd rows and on
69 of 86 R200 bwd rows. Against the strongest in-budget non-Cake SOTA,
bwd ranges from 0.43x to 1.58x on B200 and from 0.23x to 1.58x on R200.
These ranges and counts cover the rows whose program this PR changes.
They leave out the [kept] rows and include rows marked ~.

**Changed windows by reason**

The dw budget is per element atol 1e-4 + rtol 1e-4 vs FP64. The FP32
eager reference is the dw error of the FP32 eager computation on the
same inputs. A program fails it when its worst dw error exceeds the
reference's (FP32 weight) or its median dw error exceeds the reference's
median (either weight dtype). Accuracy data from 60 inputs of each of
three input families are not yet qualifying evidence.

B200 (sm_100a):

- Budget breach:
- H1536 above T 78784 with BF16 weight and above T 75776 with FP32
weight ([fix]): FlashInfer main's program is faster but exceeds the dw
budget at a larger T. Below each cut, that program has qualifying dw
evidence. The TwoSum twin runs above the cut.
- H5120 above T 56256 ([twin]): the deterministic=True backward's pair
that this PR replaces up to T 65536 exceeds the dw budget. The
FP32-weight pair computes the same dw. Above T 65536, the replaced
program exceeds the budget (measured with FP32 weight; the BF16-weight
program computes the same dw).
- H6144 above T 65536: the replaced program exceeds the dw budget
(measured with FP32 weight; the BF16-weight program computes the same
dw).
- Eager-reference failure ([route], FP32 weight): H1536 T 1025 to 4096,
H2048 T 337 to 4096, H4096 T 1793 to 3584 and H5120 T 65 to 6144. The
pair this PR replaces exceeds the FP32 eager reference's dw error at
some T of each window. det runs the same pair there (H5120: from T 122;
at T 65 to 121, det runs new's kernel with the same launch).
- H1536 T 65 to 384 ([edge], [cell]) runs a column-task kernel that is
faster than the kernels it replaces. With FP32 weight, the pair it
replaces exceeds the FP32 eager reference's dw error at T 64, and at T
65 to 109 det runs the same column-task kernel, so det and new run the
same backward program at T 65. With BF16 weight, at T 65 to 109 det runs
its own column-task kernel; the one slower row there (2xfwd+bwd at T 65,
0.98x) is marked ~.
- Neutral re-routes:
- H2048 T 45057 to 58880 ([neutral], both weight dtypes) runs the single
kernel of the windows on either side, within 2 % of the time of the
deterministic=True backward's pair that FlashInfer main ran there. The
pair's worst dw element reached 0.969 (BF16 weight) and 0.900 (FP32
weight) of the dw budget, the single kernel's 0.800 and 0.777 (every
64th T, 120 inputs per family).
- H4096 and residual H6144 above T 65536 run the TwoSum program at 1.00x
to 1.01x the time of the replaced program. The replaced program's worst
dw element reached 0.987 of the dw budget for H4096 (FP32 weight 0.907)
and 0.903 for residual H6144 (FP32 weight 0.835), on 60 inputs per
family.
- Qualified-evidence choice with a follow-up PR: H2048 above T 65536
(both weight dtypes) runs the TwoSum program at 1.10x to 1.14x the time
of the program it replaces. The TwoSum program's worst dw error is at
most 0.0006 of the budget. The replaced program stays within the dw
budget at every sampled T, but only on 60 inputs per family, so its data
do not yet qualify.
- Where new is slower than det in the H1536, H2048, H4096, H5120 and
H6144 top windows, the program det runs there is faster but exceeds the
dw budget at some measured T.
- A follow-up PR is planned to replace the TwoSum program in the B200
top windows up to T 131072.
- H512 T 1 to 227 runs the deterministic=True backward's column-task
kernel, so det and new run the same backward program there.

R200 (sm_107a):

- Top windows (TwoSum program): H512 above T 49152, H1536 and H4096
above T 65536, H6144 above T 30720 (FP32 weight: T 28672) and residual
H6144 above T 7168.
- Budget breach: the replaced program exceeds the dw budget at some
measured T of the window for H512, H1536 and H4096 (both weight dtypes),
and for H6144 and residual H6144 (measured with FP32 weight; the
BF16-weight program computes the same dw).
- In the H6144 and residual H6144 top windows, new is also faster than
the replaced program.
- Where new is slower than det, the deterministic=True backward's
program is faster there but exceeds the dw budget at some measured T of
the window. Each window keeps its start, and a follow-up PR re-checks
the faster program above it up to its budget edge.
- Eager-reference failure (FP32 weight):
- Windows: H256 T 1297 to 1536, H1536 T 65 to 256 and T 1025 to 16384,
H2048 T 1025 to 16384, H5120 T 4097 to 19968, H6144 T 65 to 28672 and
residual H6144 T 65 to 96. In each, the pair this PR replaces exceeds
the FP32 eager reference's dw error at some T (residual H6144: at T 8,
below the window). The deterministic=True backward runs the same pair
there (H6144: up to T 19456), except on H256, where it runs its own
pair, which also exceeds the reference.
- H6144 T 19457 to 28672 runs the deterministic=True backward's pair of
that range.
- On H6144 T 97 to 2304, the window uses the column-task program, whose
worst and median dw error stay at or below the reference's at every
sampled T. The deterministic=True backward's pair is faster there; its
data on this range come from 60 inputs per family, and a follow-up PR
re-checks it.
- FP32-weight H2048 T 65 to 127 and H4096 T 65 to 256 run column-task
cells that replace FlashInfer main's slower single kernel. The
deterministic=True backward's pair is faster there but exceeds the FP32
eager reference's dw error in these windows.
- H512 T 1 to 77 (FP32 weight: T 1 to 229) runs the TwoSum column-task
kernel of that hidden size, which is faster than the single kernel it
replaces. The deterministic=True backward's pair is faster there, but
its dw error exceeds the FP32 eager reference's: the median at T 77 with
BF16 weight, the worst at T 229 with FP32 weight.
- Neutral re-route: H6144 T 19457 to 30720 with BF16 weight runs the
deterministic=True backward's pair for now. The pair it replaces stays
within the dw budget there and takes 0.97x to 0.99x of the det pair's
time. A follow-up PR moves the range back to it.

**Measurement**

- Latency: the median of the CUPTI span of one CUDA-graph replay with
cold L2. 4 sessions run in parallel, one per GPU; each session times 201
replays per implementation and op, split over 3 interleaved rounds; the
median pools the samples of the 4 sessions. The p10-p90 ranges are
omitted here. Each implementation's own setup, reduction, cast and copy
kernels are inside the span.
- Context (figures measured on GB300 and B200, not on R200): Cake gains
somewhat more from the context than the other non-compile libraries on
small rows: SOTA/new vs the non-compile candidates is up to about 1.10x
higher (GB300) / 1.14x higher (B200) in the one-process measurement than
in a process without torch.compile; large rows <= 1.02x. So small-row
ratios may overstate the new kernel's lead by up to about that much.
Ratios vs det are unaffected.
- GPU, CUDA version and build are given in the caption of each table.
- Workload: eps 1e-6. For every implementation, y, dx and h_new are
BF16, and rstd and dw are FP32.
- det = deterministic Cake: `deterministic=True` of the same tree, which
this PR does not change. new = this PR's non-deterministic Cake
(`deterministic=False`).
- SOTA = the fastest non-Cake candidate that has these outputs and meets
the accuracy budget, so it is the strongest in-budget comparison. The
budget is dx atol = rtol = 1e-2, and dw per element atol 1e-4 + rtol
1e-4 vs FP64, taking the worst of 5 seeds.
- Candidates: QuACK 0.6.5 (heuristic config and per-shape autotuned),
torch.compile (max-autotune-no-cudagraphs and default mode),
Liger-Kernel 0.8.5, and Transformer Engine (run as the FP32 problem).
- Not candidates: PyTorch's fused rms_norm (dtype error), Apex (not
installed) and FlashInfer's inference rmsnorm (forward only).
- In a B200 record, the torch.compile max-autotune candidate failed with
a disk-quota error on 2 rows. The record does not name them. On those
rows, SOTA is the fastest of the remaining candidates.
- Accuracy: new and det pass on every row.
- Speedup = baseline latency / new latency (> 1: new is faster). Ratios
are computed from unrounded medians, so a few differ in the last digit
from the ratio of the printed latencies. Both modes run the same forward
programs, and the printed fwd ratios are measured values.
- Rows: every measured row whose program this PR changes, plus the
[kept] rows. Rows where new is slower than det are shown as measured.

Key:

- form: plain, or res = fused residual add (h_new = BF16(h + u),
combined grad). op 2xfwd+bwd = checkpointed step (forward, forward
recompute, backward).
- Markers (B200):
- [fix] = window where the FlashInfer main program this PR replaces
exceeds the dw budget at a measured T (H1536 above T 78784 with BF16
weight, above T 75776 with FP32 weight). The TwoSum twin program runs
there.
- [neutral] = neutral re-route (H2048 T 45057 to 58880, both weight
dtypes), not a dw-budget fix. det runs the pair this PR replaces, so
det/new compares new with that pair.
- [twin] = the TwoSum twin program takes the top of the T range (H5120
above T 56256, residual H6144 above T 65536)
- [route] = FP32-weight re-route (eager-reference failure of the
replaced pair)
  - [edge] = new T 65 edge (H1536; FP32-weight H5120)
  - [cell] = new (64, 384] H1536 column-task cell
- [kept] = row in a window where this PR keeps FlashInfer main's
program, so the program at that T is unchanged. These rows are shown for
reference and are not counted in the summary or the ranges above.
- [cut] = row from a second record (H5120 T 56256 and 56257, H1536 T
75648)
- [carried] = row from an earlier record (same GPU model and software
stack) of a program that has not changed since
- R200: every row is a route change (at that T, this PR runs a different
program than FlashInfer main). For H6144 with FP32 weight (plain), every
measured T of the (64, 2304] window is shown.
- ! = no non-Cake candidate meets the dw budget. The fastest matched
candidate is shown, with its dw err/tol in parentheses. On B200,
SOTA/new is computed against it. On R200, no SOTA/new is given (-).
- ~ = the ratio fails the spread rule: the session medians of its
baseline (det or SOTA) or of new differ by > 5 % (largest minus smallest
of the 4 per-session medians, divided by the smallest). Session spread
(largest minus smallest of the 4 per-session medians, divided by the
smallest; largest of det / SOTA / new per row): B200 median 1.75 % (min
0.1 %, max 29.7 %), 40 of 300 rows marked ~; R200 median 1.6 % (min 0.2
%, max 18.3 %), 45 of 258 rows marked ~.
- SOTA names:
- TC = torch.compile (torch 2.14.1+cu130, inductor mode
max-autotune-no-cudagraphs, emulate_precision_casts=True) of the
explicit FP32-statistics reference
  - TCd = the same with torch.compile inductor default mode
- Q = QuACK 0.6.5 (quack-kernels, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.1), heuristic
config
- QA = QuACK 0.6.5 rmsnorm_fwd_tuned / rmsnorm_bwd_tuned (exhaustive
per-shape autotune, cached before timing)
- Liger = Liger-Kernel 0.8.5 (Triton 3.8.0), casting_mode gemma (FP32
math)
  - QA+add = torch add + QA (residual form)

**B200 (sm_100a): new non-deterministic Cake vs deterministic Cake vs
strongest non-Cake SOTA. Rows whose program this PR changes, plus [kept]
rows**

- GPU: B200 sm_100a, 148 SMs, compute capability 10.0; driver 580.82.07.
- Software: CUDA toolkit 13.4 (Build
cuda_13.4.r13.4/compiler.38855100_0); torch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA runtime
13.0).
- Sessions: 4 sessions (s1/s3 forward, s2/s4 reverse) run in parallel on
the node's 4 GPUs. Each row group runs in one process with det, all
non-Cake candidates and new, in a balanced implementation order.
- Builds: all rows were timed on earlier builds of this branch. On these
routes, those builds run the same programs as this PR's head in both
modes.

### [1e41e97](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/1e41e970b1f98883d692ffff8283c3d80e8136c0)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T18:46:32Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): exact-FP32 cluster SIMT router forward at 1 to 192 tokens on 152-SM sm_100a / sm_103a (#8807)

The dense projection GEMM ships as two packages: a deterministic one,
`flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_det_gemm`, and a
non-deterministic one, `flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm`.
In the non-deterministic package, the K1 projections (BF16 or FP32
output) and the FP32 router GEMM each have forward, weight-gradient and
input-gradient programs. This PR delivers the FP32 router forward with
`deterministic=False` on 152-SM GB200 (sm_100a) and GB300 (sm_103a),
with 256 experts and hidden 4096/5120/6144. It uses new exact-FP32
cluster SIMT programs for T 1-192, except H4096 on sm_100a, which covers
T 1-160.

Compared with the deterministic Cake package, the forward op is
1.169-4.882x faster on GB200 and 1.185-4.838x faster on GB300. Compared
with the current main route, it is 1.131-4.769x and 1.137-4.734x faster.
For the whole training step the speedup over deterministic Cake is
1.188-4.176x on GB200 and 1.210-4.129x on GB300. For the checkpointed
step it is 1.207-4.734x and 1.225-4.715x.

The cuBLAS baseline is cuBLAS 13.8.0.4 via `torch.mm` in FP32 with TF32
off (`fp32_precision='ieee'`). In every row it was the fastest library
arm within the accuracy budget, ahead of BF16x9-emulated `cublasSgemm`.
Against it the ratios are as follows (GB200 / GB300):

- Op: 0.903-2.709x / 0.871-2.705x
- Step: 0.757-1.901x / 0.759-1.900x
- Checkpointed step: 0.810-2.294x / 0.811-2.295x

cuBLAS is faster at T1 for every H in the step and checkpointed step on
both GPUs, and in the op at H4096 T1 and H6144 T1. It is also faster in
the GB200 op at H4096 T160 and H6144 T176/T192. On GB300 it is faster at
H4096 T176/T192 in the op, step and checkpointed step. All timings are
CUDA-graph replay.

## Router forward speedup tables (FlashInfer PR #8807)

Source: current-main re-measure (FlashInfer main 79cf0557 + this PR's
forward programs). CUDA graph rows only. `us` = microseconds.

per-run medians over 2 nodes x 4 runs (A/AR/B/BR); FP32 router, 256
experts, hidden H, T tokens; current = FlashInfer main non-deterministic
router_forward, deterministic Cake = deterministic package, cuBLAS =
torch.mm FP32 (TF32 off); ratios > 1 = new faster; not shipped and
omitted: H4096 T176, H4096 T192 (these token counts keep the current
route).

### [b90c723](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/b90c723757b8076df583ce61dba178216c7809f8)

- **作者**: zz774ever
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T18:41:29Z
- **提交信息**: prefill: use fa2 backend for small per-request query lengths (#5188)

## 📌 Description

On SM90, `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(backend="auto")` resolves
to the
`fa3` backend, which runs
`PrefillWithKVCacheKernel<SparseCollectiveMainloop<...>>`.
That kernel uses a fixed `CTA_Q=128` query tile, so when each request
only
verifies a few query tokens (MTP / speculative decoding,
`q_len_per_req=2`),
almost the entire tile is padding and the tensor-core work is wasted.
This is
the ~10x gap reported in #3420.

`determine_attention_backend()` selects the backend from device, dtypes
and
head dims only — it never sees the query length — so `auto` has no way
to know
it is being called with an MTP-shaped batch. Notably, `backend="fa3"`
combined
with `q_len_per_req > 1` raises `NotImplementedError: q_len_per_req > 1
is
currently only supported on the fa2 tensor-core backend`, confirming fa3
is not
intended for this case at all.

**What this PR changes.** In
`BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper.plan()`
(`flashinfer/prefill.py`), after `auto` resolves, fall back to `fa2`
when the
maximum query length per request is small:

```python
if (
    self._backend == "fa3"
    and qo_indptr is not None
    and qo_indptr.numel() > 1
    and int((qo_indptr[1:] - qo_indptr[:-1]).max().item()) <= 64
):
    self._backend = "fa2"
```

`fa2` selects an adaptive query tile instead (`CTA_TILE_Q=16` for
`q_len=2`,
`64` for `q_len=8`). The guard is limited to the SM90 `fa3` case, so
other
backends and other architectures are unaffected.

**Performance (H20 / SM90, FP16, NHD paged KV, page_size=16, GQA 32/8,
head_dim=128, KV=8192, 4 warmups + 12 CUDA-event samples, p50):**

| q_len | fa2 (us) | fa3 (us) | fa3/fa2 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 213.0 | 2141.3 | 10.05x |
| 8 | 570.1 | 2142.9 | 3.76x |
| 16 | 570.7 | 2145.1 | 3.76x |
| 32 | 1055.8 | 2144.0 | 2.03x |
| 64 | 2033.7 | 2145.1 | 1.05x |
| 128 | 3483.5 | 2142.9 | 0.62x |
| 256 | 6803.1 | 4180.3 | 0.61x |

fa3's cost is essentially independent of `q_len` (2141-2145 us at
batch=16,
337-343 us at batch=1) while fa2 scales linearly, which is the
fixed-tile
signature and confirms the mechanism above. The crossover is at
`q_len=128`,
which is why the guard uses `max_q_per_req <= 64`.

End to end through `backend="auto"` with `q_len=2, KV=8192, batch=1`:
337 us
before, 56 us after.

**Reproduction.** Each number is one wrapper call timed with CUDA events
after
4 warmup iterations:

```python
wrapper = flashinfer.prefill.BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(
    workspace, "NHD", backend="fa2"   # or "fa3"
)
wrapper.plan(
    qo_indptr=torch.arange(0, (batch + 1) * q_len, q_len, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
    paged_kv_indptr=torch.arange(0, (batch + 1) * pages, pages, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
    paged_kv_indices=torch.arange(pages, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda").repeat(batch),
    paged_kv_last_page_len=torch.full((batch,), 16, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
    num_qo_heads=32,
    num_kv_heads=8,
    head_dim_qk=128,
    page_size=16,
    pos_encoding_mode="NONE",
    causal=True,
    q_data_type=torch.float16,
    kv_data_type=torch.float16,
)
# then time wrapper.run(q, kv) with start/end CUDA events
```

### [2fc021c](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2fc021cfa697175554fe22e0af3180af8c1ff2db)

- **作者**: wuyaole
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T18:38:28Z
- **提交信息**: ci: report failed and cancelled matrix lanes in test summary (#7996)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

The required PR Test summary reports only the aggregate matrix result. A
single failure can therefore hide that other lanes were cancelled before
providing coverage; reviewers must open individual checks to find the
failed lane.

Report outcomes and job links for the planned matrix lanes from the
exact run attempt, with pagination and explicit missing/unfinished
states. The metadata request has a 20-second total timeout and is best
effort: API, timeout or metadata errors produce an unknown-coverage
note. Existing authorization, fail-fast policy and final test verdict
are unchanged.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Related #5261 (diagnostics only; does not change cancellation policy or
address the underlying test failure).

```experimental-tests
#   tests/experimental/test_my_backend.py
#   tests/experimental/my_backend/
#
# Declaring the whole tree (tests/experimental/) is allowed but means every
# experimental PR pays for every other feature's tests, in every matrix cell.
```

## Reviewer Notes

The required check still uses `needs.test.result` for its verdict. Lane
metadata is diagnostic only, and the existing `actions: read` permission
is sufficient. Successful matrix lanes do not imply full-suite coverage;
the existing scoped-run warning remains.

Prepared with Codex assistance.

### [f108f7f](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/f108f7f5ed635d6d46ca864d074957513f516d33)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T18:35:22Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda): compute warps load the first task's entering state in three new bounded direct N32 turnover builds of BF16 KDA prefill for 128-token launches (sm_103a) (#8823)

The Cake chunked KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) prefill behind
`flashinfer.recurrent_kda(..., backend="cake")` has modules with BF16
inputs and modules with TF32 inputs. Both come in fused and split forms.
This PR changes one build of the BF16-input fused module with FP32
state: the bounded direct N32 turnover build. The change applies only on
sm_103a (GB300). On GB300, some launches would end on this build and
have exactly 128 tokens in every sequence. Those launches now use one of
three new builds. In the new builds, the compute warps load the entering
state of a bin's first task, and the loader warp starts at the bin's
second task. Every other launch keeps its build, and no launch changes
build on sm_100a (B200). The tables compare this PR with the previous
Cake version on FlashInfer main, on B200 and GB300. That version already
includes the FP32 state decay after the full state hand-off in the N16
checkpoint-TMA direct build (#8814). The tables report the latency per
call in microseconds. Each table has 56 rows: 12 or 16 heads, no gate
lower bound or -5, and 14 sequence-length shapes. One table covers the
plan-cache fast path and the other covers the serving pattern. TIE means
no difference beyond the measurement band. In each table, two rows are
faster on GB300: shape BS16 x T128 with gate lower bound -5, once with
12 heads and once with 16 heads. With 12 heads, the GB300 latency goes
from 30.75 to 29.54 us (1.04x) on the fast path and from 31.17 to 29.60
us (1.05x) in the serving pattern. With 16 heads, it goes from 31.49 to
30.72 us (1.02x) and from 31.49 to 30.53 us (1.03x). Every other counted
GB300 row is TIE, and none is slower. On the fast path the GB300 speedup
is 1.00x to 1.04x over 55 counted rows, and in the serving pattern it is
1.00x to 1.05x over 56 rows. B200 is unchanged: no launch moves to a new
build on sm_100a, and all 56 rows in both tables are TIE (0.99x to
1.00x). On the GB300 fast path, the row with 16 heads, gate lower bound
-5 and shape 2x(8128+64) is marked † and is not counted. In that row,
the timing of both sides drifted beyond the measurement guard within one
run. This also happens when FlashInfer main is timed against itself. We
also swept the launch shapes outside the tables that this PR moves to
the new builds. On GB300, all 176 of these held-out shapes are faster,
with a latency ratio (this PR / main) of 0.93 to 0.99. We also timed 8
more shapes with 128-token sequences (batch 24 and 48). All 8 are
faster, with a ratio of 0.97 to 0.99. None of the swept shapes is
slower. The family also ships the TF32-input modules and the split forms
on both sm_100a and sm_103a. This PR does not change those variants or
any other program.


B200: NVIDIA B200, sm_100a, 148 SMs, driver 580.82.07. GB300: NVIDIA
GB300, sm_103a, 152 SMs, driver 580.159.03. CUDA 13.4 (nvcc), PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Added a specialized KDA prefill route for workloads where every
sequence contains exactly 128 tokens, on supported hardware and when the
route is available.
* Other sequence lengths and unsupported routes continue to use the
existing turnover path.
* The specialized route supports bounded launches with and without
checkpoint rows, while preserving the existing launch schedule and
results.
* **Documentation**
* Updated generated-program documentation to describe the 128-token
route and eligible launch behavior.

### [e15959b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/e15959b98afbf07abd04494fd726525f397f50ec)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T18:34:01Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_det_kcp): cheaper eager host path for the deterministic KCP package (#8817)

Cake's deterministic context-parallel GDN training kernel has one
data-type variant: BF16 q/k/v/out/dout with FP32 scalar log-decay g and
beta. The grouped Q/K head counts `(H_qk, HV)` are runtime parameters,
with production shape (16, 48). There are three partition layouts:
contiguous (C), whole-buffer zigzag (Z) and per-document zigzag + ragged
(D). This PR delivers the same variant. It brings over the cheaper eager
host path from the non-deterministic twin (#8600). Each launch binds the
current CUDA stream once on a cached device, and registry and
chunk-token lookups are computed once. Kernels and launches do not
change, and outputs and gradients are bitwise equal to main (the current
deterministic package on FlashInfer main). Time per call at CP 1 on B200
is up to 1.53x faster than main. Full CP 8 steps on GB200 are 2–5 %
faster.

**NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a): host time per call, CP 1**

main is the current deterministic package on FlashInfer main, and new is
this PR. Each value is the median of 200 step times in microseconds
(wall time per call, host work included). All runs are CP 1 contiguous
in one process, with interleaved palindromic main/new/new visits: 5
groups x 20 steps per arm after 5 warm-up steps. new/main < 1 is faster.
Workloads: N = 3 documents (2,049 / 3,001 / 3,142 tokens), heads (2, 6);
A = 4 documents (98,304 / 65,536 / 57,344 / 40,960 tokens), heads (16,
48); M = 5 documents (12,000 / 9,000 / 6,000 / 3,768 / 2,000 tokens),
heads (16, 48). Rows vary the in-kernel q/k L2 norm (on/off), the
context ("reused" = one partition + context built once and reused across
steps; "built per step" = partition and context built inside every timed
step) and the op (forward; forward + backward; checkpointed step =
forward + non-reentrant checkpoint replay + backward). With a reused
context, new/main is 0.65–0.95 (A forward 0.655, N forward 0.869,
forward + backward 0.80–0.92). With the context built per step, it is
0.92–0.98 (A forward 0.980). Environment: NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a), CUDA
13.0 runtime / torch 2.14.1+cu130, CUDA 13.4 toolkit.

### [2a9fd47](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2a9fd4718f0e67eb08f613b40b1b6d24b6f13c83)

- **作者**: Mingyang Wang
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T18:33:57Z
- **提交信息**: perf: group tiny-KV GQA context requests on SM103 (#8736)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

For BF16 paged context attention with two query tokens per request, the
Context kernel schedules one CTA per query head even when each request
has only a few KV tokens. This change selects the existing grouped Q32
generation kernel for the measured SM103 region: batch 4–256, maximum KV
length 1–32, Hq/Hkv=16/1, head dimensions 128 and page size 128.

The dispatch retains packed HND/layout and feature restrictions, Context
persistent scheduling and no split-KV workspace. A zero-default runner
flag retains the initial Q32 tile so both query rows share a CTA,
preserving fully masked-row writes. Other workloads keep their existing
selection. Both the native context API and
`BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(backend="trtllm-gen")` benefit.

Observed on one **B300 (SM103)**, CUDA 13.0.88, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130,
BF16 Q/K/V/output, causal Q2, H16/1, D128, page128, PDL enabled. Wrapper
warm-graph medians for KV32:

| Batch | Context baseline (µs) | Grouped Q32 (µs) | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4 | 6.770 | 5.980 | 1.13× |
| 64 | 23.393 | 6.310 | 3.71× |
| 256 | 79.175 | 8.888 | 8.91× |

At the original KV2/B64 shape, native latency falls from 23.446 to 6.317
µs (3.71×); the profiled grid changes from 1,024 CTAs to 64.

Measurements used matched inputs and serialized
baseline/candidate/candidate-reversed/baseline-reversed runs, with 3
rounds of 10 samples per case. Warm timings amortize 100 calls per CUDA
graph. The baseline disables only this dispatch branch on the same
source based on `a02329da80605b823ad64bf053fc5f744abcddf4`. Source,
loaded library, cubin and actual kernel-route identities were checked
before accepting results. Across 48 warm comparisons, observed speedups
are 1.117–8.936×; every baseline round median exceeds every candidate
round median by at least 0.3 µs and 5%.

Cold one-call graph comparisons used an eviction buffer at least twice
L2, excluded eviction work from timing, and checked outputs immediately
after evicted replay. B64/B256 improve 2.325–5.250×; B4 is neutral. All
14 neighboring fallback and 12 mixed/long-KV comparisons remain on
Context and show no material regression by the same 0.3 µs/5% separation
criterion. These are observed-round comparisons, not statistical
confidence intervals.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Related to https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/7965. This
PR covers the validated BF16 subset; exact GB300 and the original FP8
comparison remain open.

<details>
<summary>Warm-shape reproduction using public APIs</summary>

Run this recipe on the base revision above and the PR head in the same
B300/software environment, after the targeted correctness checks on the
PR. It reproduces the shape and warm-graph timing method; it is a
source-checked convenience recipe, not the harness that produced the
table or a new validation result.

```python
from statistics import median

import torch
import flashinfer
from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time

torch.manual_seed(7965)
device, dtype = "cuda", torch.bfloat16
workspace = torch.empty(128 << 20, device=device, dtype=torch.uint8)
print("batch,kv,median_us")
for batch in (4, 8, 64, 256):
    q = torch.randn(batch * 2, 16, 128, device=device, dtype=dtype)
    kv = torch.randn(batch, 2, 1, 128, 128, device=device, dtype=dtype)
    out = torch.empty_like(q)
    qo = torch.arange(batch + 1, device=device, dtype=torch.int32) * 2
    indptr = torch.arange(batch + 1, device=device, dtype=torch.int32)
    indices = torch.arange(batch, device=device, dtype=torch.int32)
    for length in (1, 2, 5, 16, 31, 32):
        lengths = torch.full((batch,), length, device=device, dtype=torch.int32)
        wrapper = flashinfer.BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(
            workspace, "HND", backend="trtllm-gen", use_cuda_graph=True,
            qo_indptr_buf=qo, paged_kv_indptr_buf=indptr,
            paged_kv_indices_buf=indices,
            paged_kv_last_page_len_buf=lengths,
        )
        wrapper.plan(
            qo, indptr, indices, lengths, 16, 1, 128, 128, causal=True,
            q_data_type=dtype, kv_data_type=dtype, o_data_type=dtype,
            block_tables=indices[:, None], seq_lens=lengths,
            max_token_per_sequence=2, max_sequence_kv=length,
        )

        def run():
            return wrapper.run(q, kv, out=out, enable_pdl=True)

        run()  # Compile/initialize before timing.
        samples = []
        for _ in range(3):
            samples.extend(bench_gpu_time(
                run, dry_run_iters=10, repeat_iters=10,
                num_iters_within_graph=100, use_cuda_graph=True,
                enable_cupti=False, cold_l2_cache=False,
            ))
        print(f"{batch},{length},{median(samples) * 1000:.3f}")
```

The repository benchmark CLI can also exercise KV≥2, but currently
rejects Q2/KV1 and uses cold-L2 timing; its numbers should not be
equated with the warm table.

</details>

## Reviewer Notes

- Exact GB300 NVL validation remains open. B300 evidence is preliminary
for the issue's target.
- This is a BF16 optimization; it does not establish FP8/FlashAttention
parity or end-to-end serving benefit.
- Only uniform actual KV equal to the declared maximum is timed.
Shorter/mixed/empty actual lengths receive correctness coverage.
Intermediate eligible batch/KV values are sampled interpolation; B4 has
no demonstrated cold-cache gain.
- Retaining Q32 is a compatibility choice as well as a scheduling
choice: a Q16 experiment left fully masked leading rows unwritten.
- The new runner flag defaults to false; ordinary decode keeps the
existing occupancy model.
- Review focused on dispatch bounds, workspace compatibility,
numerical/masked-write behavior and graph replay. No required findings
remain.
