### [cb41a8d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/cb41a8d3d7f74eb68c5d99ac5917af92661c1451)

- **作者**: Ka-Hyun Nam
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T18:12:09Z
- **提交信息**: docs(moe): document the gated FC1 [X1; X2] layout and clamp/offset mapping, add deinterleave_gated_rows, pin the MXFP8 clamp/offset numerics (#8433)

## 📌 Description

Acceptance criterion, stated up front: the kernel-level test in this PR
compares the MXFP8 block-scale MoE against Megatron-Core's `glu_inputs`
definition at `atol=rtol=1e-2` after rounding the reference through
MXFP8, not bitwise. The kernel feeds GEMM2 the MXFP8-quantized
activation, so a bitwise match against the fp32 trainer definition is
not available on this path: the kernel equals the in-repo
`run_moe_dequant` reference exactly, and both differ from the fp32
formula only by e4m3 rounding of that activation (5.28 -> 5.5, 13.75 ->
14). The unrounded reference fails at that tolerance, so the check is
tight to one e4m3 ulp.

The `trtllm_*_moe` docstrings did not say which half of the gated FC1
weight rows is the linear/up half and which is the gate half, nothing
documented how a trainer-side SwiGLU clamp value and linear offset
(Megatron-Core `activation_func_clamp_value` / `glu_linear_offset`) map
onto `gemm1_clamp_limit` / `gemm1_beta` / `gemm1_alpha` or onto
`cutlass_fused_moe`'s `swiglu_*` parameters, there was no helper for
weights stored with gate and linear rows interleaved in fixed-width
blocks (Megatron-Core `moe_mlp_glu_interleave_size`), and no test showed
that `trtllm_fp8_block_scale_moe` can express the clamp and offset at
all. Megatron-LM #8566 rejects those options on the FlashInfer backend
for that reason.

This PR documents the `[X1; X2]` row order of `gemm1_weights` on
`trtllm_bf16_moe`, `trtllm_bf16_routed_moe`,
`trtllm_fp8_block_scale_moe` and `trtllm_fp8_block_scale_routed_moe`
(rows `[0, I)` are X1 linear/up, rows `[I, 2I)` are X2 gate, in each
expert's logical `[M, hidden_size]` matrix before the
`use_shuffled_weight` preprocessing), adds the clamp/offset parameter
mapping to the `gemm1_clamp_limit` docstrings of the same four entry
points (`gemm1_clamp_limit=v`, `gemm1_beta=o`, `gemm1_alpha=1` with
`ActivationType.Swiglu` is Megatron's `glu_inputs(v, o)` followed by
SwiGLU), and states the `SwigluBias` formula and the same mapping on
`cutlass_fused_moe`'s `swiglu_alpha` / `swiglu_beta` / `swiglu_limit`.

It adds `flashinfer.fused_moe.deinterleave_gated_rows(x, block)`, a
host-side helper that undoes a block interleave of the two FC1 halves
along the row dimension and is the inverse of
`reorder_rows_for_gated_act_gemm` for `block=1`; it is applied per
expert at load time, so no kernel variant is added. The helper is
exported from `flashinfer.fused_moe` and `flashinfer`, next to
`reorder_rows_for_gated_act_gemm`.

It adds `test_mxfp8_block_scale_moe_matches_megatron_glu_clamp_offset`,
which runs the MXFP8 block-scale MoE on the existing sparse-projection
setup (output column 0 is the SwiGLU of input columns 0 and 1) with
`gemm1_alpha=1`, `gemm1_beta=o`, `gemm1_clamp_limit=v` and compares
against a torch transcription of Megatron-Core's `glu_inputs` (`gate =
min(gate, v)`, `linear = clamp(linear, -v, v) + o`, then `silu(gate) *
linear`). `(v, o) = (2, 1)` clamps the gate on three tokens and the
linear half on three tokens with both signs; `(7, 0.5)` leaves every
value unclamped and checks the offset alone. A guard asserts the
reference differs from plain SwiGLU so the case cannot pass trivially,
and a swapped gate/linear assignment fails on most tokens. The setup of
`test_mxfp8_block_scale_moe_swiglu_oa_activation_params` is factored
into `_mxfp8_sparse_swiglu_case` so both tests share it; its assertions
are unchanged.

No kernel or dispatch code changes. The docstring text is a parameter
mapping onto the formulas the docstrings already state; the new test is
what pins the mapping down numerically on the MXFP8 path.

Fixes #7940; the probs-on-input and float64-noise items are tracked
separately in #8591 and #8592.

### [be0985b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/be0985b1ae7a7f480714cc20486004e73029691d)

- **作者**: Anthony Chang
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T17:42:26Z
- **提交信息**: feat(attn_scores): add selective MQA TopK for prefill (indexer-throwaway topk) (#7325)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Collab w/ @yweng0828.

This PR adds **Selective TopK** for single-request prefill through
`flashinfer.FP8MQATopKWrapper` with `backend="cutedsl"`. It reads
continuous K with separate scales and supports FP8, MXFP8 and MXFP4 Q/K,
FP32/FP16/BF16 logits and FP32/BF16 weights. Its **Selective logits**
stage, the Indexer-throwaway kernel, filters scores before writing
candidates and never materializes the full logits matrix.

### 1. Implementation

**Selective TopK** runs four stages:

1. **K1 - Sample:** stratified samples propose per-row thresholds.
2. **K2 - Selective logits:** the Indexer-throwaway kernel computes QK
with Tensor Core GEMM, applies ReLU and weighted head reduction, and
publishes only candidates that pass the threshold.
3. **K3 - Select:** histogram/radix selection produces exact TopK from
the retained candidates, including tied boundary scores.
4. **K4 - Recover:** rows with insufficient candidates or candidate
overflow are rescored and selected exactly. Recovery reuses the
candidate workspace and may materialize scores for queued rows; K2 does
not write the full logits matrix.

Rows with at most TopK visible keys return those keys directly. Eligible
short domains use exhaustive candidates. Kernel and workspace policies
depend on the declared geometry and physical K extent, not capture
identity. K2 uses shared KV tiles, prepared scale layouts and packed
weight loads where supported; K3 uses compact candidates and
shared-memory histograms. K1, K2 and K4 use the same numerical contract.

`logits_dtype` controls rounding before filtering and selection. FP32
head accumulation and explicit `native_bf16` / `native_fp16` arithmetic
are separate choices; native modes require the matching logits dtype.
Native modes use FP32 QK dots followed by rounded native ReLU, weights,
four FMA chains and the final reduction `(c0+c2)+(c1+c3)`. Token-scaled
FP8/native FP16 uses a fixed QK/512 and weightsx512 rebalance to avoid
FP16 conversion overflow. Weights storage is independent of accumulation
precision. BF16 weights are retained during staging; native BF16 kernels
load adjacent weights as packed pairs and reuse them in the epilogue.

MXFP8 accepts the same E4M3FN values and per-32-element UE8M0 scale
bytes produced by official DeepGEMM quantization. Benchmark comparisons
quantize once outside timing and share these inputs. The DeepGEMM and
dense_mqa baseline kernels are unchanged.

### 2. Supported configurations

| Implementation | Q/K encoding | Weights | Logits | Geometry / workload
| KV layout |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Selective TopK** | Token-scaled FP8, MXFP8 E4M3FN, MXFP4 E2M1 | FP32
or BF16 | FP32, FP16, BF16 | H4/H32/H64, D128, TopK 512/1024/2048;
single-request prefill | Continuous |

**Selective TopK** infers model policies from `(num_heads, head_dim,
top_k, compression_ratio)`; an explicit `model_config` must match those
fields. Qwen's numerical contract applies only when
`model_config="Qwen3.8-Flash-Next"` is explicit: it requires
`1/sqrt(128)` weights rounded to the selected storage dtype and unit K
scales for token-scaled FP8, and replay validates these conditions. A
matching shape without the name keeps the general numerical contract.
The default `math_mode=None` resolves to `relu_fast` for FP8 and MXFP4
and to `relu_strict` for MXFP8, which supports strict ReLU only. Fast
mode requires finite active weights that are zero or have magnitude at
least 2**-125, and MXFP4 scale bytes at most 159. The device validates
these bounds on each replay and fails closed with `-1` rows and an error
bit.

### 3. API and CUDA Graph lifecycle

Construct outside capture, prepare each K/scale binding once, plan each
step and run each layer:

```python
import torch
from flashinfer import FP8MQATopKWrapper

wrapper = FP8MQATopKWrapper(
    strategy="selective", backend="cutedsl", qkv_dtype="mxfp8",
    weights_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    logits_dtype=torch.bfloat16, math_mode="native_bf16",
    num_heads=64, head_dim=128, top_k=2048,
    compression_ratio=1, max_context_length=131072,
    max_chunk_size=8192, max_batch_size=1, device="cuda",
)

# Each layer owns one K/scale binding:
#   k: E4M3FN[131072, 128]; k_scale: uint8[131072, 4] (UE8M0 per 32 elements)
for k, k_scale in zip(layer_ks, layer_k_scales):
  wrapper.prepare_pool(k, k_scale=k_scale)  # once per binding, outside capture
for step in steps:
  # qo_indptr, kv_indptr: CUDA int32[2] original-token prefixes for one request
  wrapper.plan(qo_indptr, kv_indptr)  # once per step; capturable after preparation
  for q, q_scale, weights, k, k_scale in layers:
    # q: E4M3FN[8192, 64, 128]; q_scale: uint8[8192, 64, 4]; weights: BF16[8192, 64]
    indices = wrapper.run(q, weights, k, k_scale=k_scale, q_scale=q_scale)
    # indices: int32[8192, 2048], shared across layers; consume it or pass out=
```

The output is request-local int32 TopK indices with `-1` padding.
Equal-score ties may produce different valid indices. The wrapper binds
continuous K directly, with no page table or gather. It accepts only
`strategy="selective"` and `backend="cutedsl"`, and requires an explicit
`num_heads`.

Prepare and warm up every K/scale address pair before capture. Keep
wrappers and bound tensors alive through replay; serialize calls sharing
a wrapper and use separate `out=` tensors when layer outputs must
coexist. Read `error` and `repair_error` outside capture.

Released plans queue their CUDA modules in one process-wide queue.
`plan`, `prepare_pool` and `clear_pools` unload them unless their own
stream is capturing; `run` never does. Do not call those three methods
while any thread is in global capture on another stream.

**Selective TopK does not yet provide one CUDA Graph for every
`kv_length`.** A prepared graph is tied to its capacity, layouts and
K/scale bindings; live prefixes can change within that contract. A
single graph spanning KV lengths is planned follow-up work.

### 4. Current limitations

- **Selective TopK** supports batch-1 prefill at H4/H32/H64 and D128;
H8, batched decode and trace export are unsupported.
- Paged KV is not supported; callers pass continuous K.
- At most 1,048,576 physical keys; query capacity must be divisible by
64/8/4 for H4/H32/H64. Block-scaled K storage requires a multiple of 256
rows and aligned base addresses.
- Compression ratios 1 and 4 describe already-compressed inputs. The
backend does not compress K. Length policies use physical K, including
the current queries' compressed keys.
- FP16/BF16 **Q/K inputs** are not supported. Native FP16/BF16 refers to
head arithmetic, not Q/K storage.
- Measurements cover B200, B1/Q8192/D128 and three captures per
configuration. They do not establish all-shape or end-to-end serving
wins. Recovery cost depends on the score distribution.
- SM103 is accepted but not validated; all tests and measurements ran on
B200 (SM100).
- `max_chunk_size` is checked only for its row alignment. Capacities
whose index offsets exceed int32 are untested.
- `plan` checks `num_query_rows` on the host when it is called or
captured. A replayed plan keeps the captured value, so each layer must
supply that many query rows.
- The API is experimental and emits `ExperimentalWarning`; its contract
may change without deprecation. Its documentation lives in
`flashinfer/experimental/attn_scores/README.md`, not `docs/api/`, until
it graduates.

### [a30888d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/a30888dff9ac38facfbd3b3a25e0a3652a1c988d)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T17:20:46Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): faster K1 forward programs for small-N rows on 152-SM sm_100a and sm_103a parts (#8794)

Cake's dense projection GEMM ships as two packages: the deterministic
`flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_det_gemm` and the
non-deterministic `flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm`. The
non-deterministic package holds two GEMMs: K1, with BF16 or FP32 output,
and an FP32 router GEMM. Each GEMM has forward, input-gradient (dgrad)
and weight-gradient (wgrad) programs. This PR switches the K1 forward on
the `deterministic=False` path to a faster program in five cases, all N
= 512 projections with BF16 input and BF16 output on 152-SM parts:
- GB200 (sm_100a): 4096→512 at T = 2048; 5120→512 at T = 1024 and T =
4096
- GB300 (sm_103a): 4096→512 at T = 2048; 5120→512 at T = 1024

On main, the `deterministic=False` forward for these cases runs the same
program as `deterministic=True`. The other variants also ship for
sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a: the deterministic package, the router
GEMM, K1's dgrad and wgrad programs, and K1's forward for other shapes
and parts. This PR changes only the K1 forward routes listed above.

New non-deterministic Cake is faster than deterministic Cake in every
row. The speedup is 1.20–1.48x in forward, 1.08–1.70x in step and
1.17–1.76x in checkpointed step. For step and checkpointed step, the
speedup is 1.08–1.35x under CUDA graph replay and 1.52–1.76x in eager
mode. In eager mode the deterministic dgrad + wgrad also measure slower
than the `deterministic=False` ones, which this PR does not change.
Non-Cake SOTA is faster than new non-deterministic Cake in every row
(0.44–0.96x). The lowest speedups are for 5120→512 at T = 1024 on both
GPUs: 0.44–0.45x for step and checkpointed step under CUDA graph replay,
and 0.50–0.52x for forward.

memsets the operation launches, measured under CUDA graph replay or

a 2 x L2 buffer. Each value is the median of 12 per-process medians,
from 12 processes on 2 nodes per GPU type. Each per-process median
covers 15 groups x 20 timed iterations. On each node, every GPU ran one
process stream. Two streams timed all measured rows in one process, one
in forward row order and one in reverse. The other two timed each row in
its own process. One node repeated this with the GPUs swapped.
Process-to-process variation (interquartile range / median, worst cell)
was 4.6 % (CUDA graph) and 14.5 % (eager) for the Cake arms, and 3.8 %
and 32.5 % for the library arms. For A/A noise, the previous forward ran
as a second, independent arm in the same processes. Its paired ratios
over forward, step and checkpointed step were 0.993–1.009 (GB200 CUDA
graph), 0.979–1.019 (GB200 eager), 0.993–1.005 (GB300 CUDA graph) and
0.983–1.025 (GB300 eager). Deterministic Cake = `deterministic=True` for
forward, dgrad and wgrad. For these rows, the previous
`deterministic=False` forward ran the same forward program. New = this
PR's forward with the unchanged `deterministic=False` dgrad and wgrad.
Step = forward + dgrad + FP32 wgrad. Checkpointed step = 2 x forward +
dgrad + FP32 wgrad. For forward, non-Cake SOTA is, per process, the
fastest of torch.mm (cuBLAS heuristic) and the cuBLASLt heuristic's
top-8 algorithms; the operation column names the arm. For step and
checkpointed step, SOTA uses the fastest library call per operation:
torch.mm or a cuBLASLt top-8 algorithm, picked per process by CUDA-graph
replay time. The Cake forward arms meet the BF16 budget \|out - ref\| <=
1e-2 + 1e-2 x \|ref\| against FP64. Whether the library arms meet it is
unknown, because the summaries behind this table record no budget result
for them. For forward, cuBLASLt algorithms were admitted only if finite
with relative Frobenius error <= 2e-2, and torch.mm was not filtered.
For step and checkpointed step, every library call, torch.mm included,
was admitted only if finite with relative Frobenius error <= 2e-2 (<=
1e-3 for the FP32 wgrad). The new forward had 0 budget violations and 0
non-finite values in 400 launches per shape and GPU type. Speedup =
baseline latency / new latency (> 1 = new faster), computed from the
printed two-decimal latencies. Measured dgrad + wgrad latency in eager
mode: 70.7–89.9 us for the deterministic programs and 43.5–63.8 us for
the `deterministic=False` ones. Under CUDA graph replay: 20.8–44.0 us
and 20.9–43.5 us.*

### [124ba7c](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/124ba7c9213309bb0cdaeaf69c4cfe9da5b55cfa)

- **作者**: Jonathan Dierksen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T17:09:19Z
- **提交信息**: chore(codeowners): add infra ownership layer for CI, scripts and build files (#8573)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Adds an infra layer to `.github/CODEOWNERS` so CI, build and
test-harness changes can be approved by the infra reviewers without
needing the busy catch-all reviewers. Today PRs such as #7016, #7897,
#7898 and #7899 touch only files that match no rule but the catch-all,
so each needs one of the full approvers.

New rules (owners: the same list as the existing test-runner rules):
- Whole directories: `.github/`, `scripts/`, `ci/`, `docker/`,
`.devcontainer/`, `flashinfer-jit-cache/`,
`flashinfer-jit-cache-provider/`, `flashinfer-cubin/`,
`tests/test_helpers/`
- Files: `build_backend.py`, `pytest.ini`, `tests/conftest.py`,
`CONTRIBUTING.md`
- Infra tests: JIT-cache, cute-DSL cache, build, CI-image, collect-env,
ninja-diagnostics, watchdog and nightly-validation tests,
`tests/test_artifacts.py`
- Docs: `docs/installation.rst` and the JIT-cache-provider and CI-bot
design docs

Deliberately not included: the JIT/build core under `flashinfer/`
(`jit/core.py`, `cpp_ext.py`, `aot.py`, ...), which every kernel author
depends on, and per-feature `tests/cpu/*` files, which stay with their
feature owners. `.github/CODEOWNERS` and the codeowner scripts fall
under the new `.github/`/`scripts/` rules, so infra can change them.

### [b869e63](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/b869e635a98f643a709259d6ded1a0ef1a682f9b)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T17:01:02Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda_det_kcp): v2 affine merge, offset walks and BF16x3 transfer walk, bitwise identical to v1 (#8803)

`flashinfer.experimental.cake_kda_det_train_kcp` holds the deterministic
context-parallel (KCP) training kernels of KDA (Kimi Delta Attention).
This PR replaces four of them with v2 builds. Outputs and gradients are
bitwise identical to v1. The baseline is v1, the previous Cake version
of each kernel, which main ships today. Per-kernel ranges are isolated
kernel times on GB300.

- **Affine merge** (state merge across ranks): register-blocked v2 in
four builds with 8, 16, 32 or 64 columns per CTA. A per-architecture
rule picks the build from T = n_chains * ncols / 128. The 64-column
build ships on sm_100a and sm_103a only. 1.46-2.43x.
- **Forward-state offset walk** (fwd h): v2 split-role schedule for
every head count. 1.02-1.36x.
- **Backward-state offset walk** (dh): v2 overlap schedule for H >= 64.
H <= 63 keeps v1 because v2 is slower at H = 4. 1.01-1.14x.
- **BF16x3 transfer walk** at value width 64: v2 with two compute
warpgroups. 1.26-1.41x.

End to end, the CP4 training step (fwd+bwd) is 1.022-1.026x faster on
GB300 over three runs and 1.023x faster on GB200.

**End-to-end training step**: CP4 (4 ranks), 16384 tokens per rank, H
64, per-document zigzag, Q/K L2 norm in the kernel. Values are ms as v1
(main) → v2 (this PR), with speedup = v1 / v2. v1 and v2 were timed on
the same node. CUDA 13.4, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.

| step | GB300 (sm_103a), run 1 | GB300 (sm_103a), run 2, order reversed
| GB300 (sm_103a), run 3, other node | GB200 (sm_100a) |

3.0371 (1.055x) | 3.3132 → 3.1728 (1.044x) |
| bwd | 5.5708 → 5.5018 (1.013x) | 5.5682 → 5.5258 (1.008x) | 5.5633 →
5.4951 (1.012x) | 5.7604 → 5.6896 (1.012x) |
| fwd+bwd | 8.5019 → 8.2886 (1.026x) | 8.5008 → 8.2966 (1.025x) | 8.4920
→ 8.3086 (1.022x) | 8.7573 → 8.5606 (1.023x) |
| checkpointed (2 x fwd + bwd) | 10.8477 → 10.5967 (1.024x) | 10.8284 →
10.5859 (1.023x) | 10.8089 → 10.5627 (1.023x) | 11.1964 → 10.9391
(1.024x) |

The package's other Cake variants are unchanged here (the full-width and

- **提交信息**: perf(cake_comm): fused multiply-add epilogue defaults on SM100 / SM103 and SM100 eight-rank cross-band plan for QKV exchange (#8800)

Add the fused multiply-add epilogue producer builds of QkvNormRopeExchangeOverlap and make them the SM100 / SM103 defaults; bring the eight-rank cross-band plan to SM100. A default build that is not delivered for the session's tile width falls back to the baseline build; every build checks 16-byte alignment of cos_sin and the norm weights.

### [7e88829](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7e8882906592c1fba598b5683e8e257dff72a21f)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T15:52:36Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_det_gemm): measured split counts for the router weight gradient at H 5120 / 6144 (#8816)

This PR changes the Cake `dense_projection_det_gemm` package in
`flashinfer.experimental`, the deterministic dense projection GEMM. Most
programs in the package are BF16-operand GEMMs (forward, dgrad and
wgrad), and one is an FP32 router GEMM. The router GEMM has three
layouts: forward (`kk`, 4 split-K partitions by default), input gradient
(`kn`, 1) and weight gradient (`nn_t`, 6). Each launch splits the second
operand into BF16x3, runs the program and sums the split-K partials.
This PR adds measured split-K counts for the router weight gradient in
`ROUTER_SPLIT_RULES`. They apply when the caller passes no `splits`. The
default `splits` of `router_det_forward` and `router_det_wgrad` is now
`None`, which means "use the planned count". An explicit `splits` from
the caller still wins. The 8 new entries cover 256 experts (N = 256) and
token counts T 16129 to 16384 on `sm_100a` and `sm_103a`, at 148 and 152
SMs. For hidden size 5120 the count goes from 6 to 9 splits, and for
hidden size 6144 it goes from 6 to 3. These parts are unchanged: the
hidden size 4096 router rows, the forward and input-gradient router
counts, and all other devices and SM counts (including `sm_107a` and
160-SM parts). The BF16 row rules stay at 391. No kernel source or
compiled library changes, and the package still has 277 compiled
libraries. The baseline is the previous Cake version of the package on
main. The timed launch is the whole router launch: the BF16x3 split, the
program and the sum of the partials. Over the T window 16129 to 16384,
hidden size 5120 is 1.10 to 1.13x faster and hidden size 6144 is 1.01 to
1.03x faster. Both were measured at T 16129, 16231 and 16384, and hidden
size 6144 was also measured at T 16172. No changed row is slower on any
of the four GPUs. All other rows of the shape list plan the same
programs as main.

**Speedup of this PR over the previous Cake version on main.** GB200
(`sm_100a`, 152 SMs), GB300 (`sm_103a`, 152 SMs), B200 (`sm_100a`, 148
SMs) and B300 (`sm_103a`, 148 SMs); router weight gradient, 5120->256 at
T 16231 and 6144->256 at T 16172 and 16231; CUDA 13.4, cold L2, FP32
output. Speedup = previous time / this PR time, and values above 1 mean
this PR is faster.

### [d3e8776](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/d3e87763a76e5ac78cfd671e1fc2c27a9924882c)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T15:24:33Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_lm_head_loss): two-slice counted dX for one-slice chunks under the zero-gradient row skip (sm_100a, sm_103a) (#8796)

Cake's chunked LM-head + loss training backend covers cross-entropy
loss, policy loss, log-probability with no temperature, a scalar
temperature or a per-token FP32 `[T]` temperature, support
log-probability and support-KL, on BF16 hidden states and weights. The
backend has a deterministic form and a non-deterministic (ND) form.
`deterministic=False` on the public `flashinfer.chunked_lm_head` entries
(`chunked_lm_head_loss`, `chunked_lm_head_logprob`,
`chunked_lm_head_support_logprob`, `chunked_lm_head_support_kl`) selects
the ND form, implemented in
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_lm_head_loss`.

This PR changes the ND log-probability backward, with or without
temperature, on sm_100a and sm_103a when it skips rows with zero dlogp.
There, a dX chunk that the slice rule gives one K slice now uses two
(the two-slice rule, `DX_COUNTED_MIN_SLICES_BY_ARCH`). The forward, the
other loss modes and sm_107a are unchanged.

Against the previous ND plan (prev: FlashInfer main's planner, timed on
this PR's build with the two-slice rule off), this PR's ND plan (new) is
faster in 36 of 195 cells on B200 (1.0162x-1.2811x) and in 24 on GB300
(1.0147x-1.0542x), and slower in none. The largest gains are p09 bwd on
B200 (21.180 -> 16.533 ms) and p30 bwd on GB300 (51.644 -> 48.991 ms).
Against deterministic Cake (det), new is faster in 124 of 195 cells on
each GPU (B200 1.0570x-1.9421x, GB300 1.0472x-1.9176x) and slower in
none.

On the 90 per-token temperature (LP+tT) and scalar temperature (LP+t0.7)
cells per GPU, SOTA (the fastest non-Cake arm timed in each cell) is
PyTorch chunked + torch.compile (PT), the only non-Cake arm timed there,
and new is faster in all 90 (B200 1.0500x-2.0358x, GB300
1.0615x-2.0357x). On the 105 log-probability (LP) cells, SOTA is Cut
Cross-Entropy 25.1.1 (CCE, torch.compile path), and new is faster than
CCE in 41 on each GPU (B200 1.0493x-1.3119x, GB300 1.0551x-1.2876x). New
is slower than CCE in 58 LP cells on B200 (0.6930x-0.9830x) and 53 on
GB300 (0.6898x-0.9787x), and prev is also slower than CCE in each of
those cells by point estimate.

support log-probability and support-KL modes, plus the deterministic
form of every mode; the ND form ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Performance**
* On supported GPU architectures, eligible counted reductions now use at
least two dX slices when the plan allows it. Explicitly tuned slice
counts and short-K-step cases retain their existing behavior.
* Temperature calculations continue to compute every row for one-slice
chunks on SM107 and when the slice count is explicitly tuned.
* **Documentation**
* Clarified architecture-specific slice-count behavior and zero-gradient
row handling.

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [7d1cc82](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7d1cc828bc42b32f2d77833250c9c500eb578203)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T15:17:57Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda): FP32 state decay after the full state hand-off in the N16 checkpoint-TMA direct build of BF16 KDA prefill (sm_100a + sm_103a) (#8814)

The Cake chunked KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) prefill behind
`flashinfer.recurrent_kda(..., backend="cake")` has modules with BF16
inputs and modules with TF32 inputs. Both come in fused and split forms.
This PR changes one build of the BF16-input fused module with FP32
state: the N16 checkpoint-TMA direct build, on sm_100a (B200) and
sm_103a (GB300). This build now decays the FP32 state after the full
state hand-off, not before it. Every launch that used the old build now
uses the new one. The tables compare this PR with the previous Cake
version on FlashInfer main, on B200 and GB300. That version already
includes the owner/helper hybrid build. The tables report the latency
per call in microseconds. Each table has 56 rows: 12 or 16 heads, no
gate lower bound or -5, and 14 sequence-length shapes. One table covers
the plan-cache fast path and the other covers the serving pattern. TIE
means no difference beyond the measurement band. In each table, one row
is faster on both GPUs: 12 heads, gate lower bound -5, shape
8x(1024+64). On B200 its latency goes from 110.46 to 107.60 us (1.03x)
on the fast path and from 111.74 to 109.12 us (1.02x) in the serving
pattern. On GB300 it goes from 103.14 to 100.70 us (1.02x) and from
103.94 to 101.54 us (1.02x). Every other counted row is TIE, and none is
slower. On the GB300 fast path, the row with 16 heads, gate lower bound
-5 and shape 2x(8128+64) is marked † and is not counted. In that row the
timing of both sides drifted beyond the measurement guard within one
run, and this also happens when FlashInfer main is timed against itself.
We also swept all launch shapes outside the tables that this PR moves to
the new build. On B200, 293 of 294 are faster and 1 is TIE. On GB300,
309 of 310 are faster and 1 is TIE, with a latency ratio (this PR /
main) of 0.97 to 0.99. None is slower on either GPU. The family also
ships the TF32-input modules and the split forms on both sm_100a and
sm_103a, and this PR does not change those variants or any other
program.

B200: NVIDIA B200, sm_100a, 148 SMs, driver 580.82.07. GB300: NVIDIA
GB300, sm_103a, 152 SMs, driver 580.159.03. CUDA 13.4 (nvcc), PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130.

### [3a5b493](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3a5b493e581f01ddec66aa78df930cad1fce0562)

- **作者**: Adrian
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T14:57:33Z
- **提交信息**: fix(jit): remove NVFP4 kernel dependency on the quantization API (#8728)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Nightly pipeline 79161607 on 2026-11-04 failed the strict CuTe-DSL
source-closure guard for the NVFP4 quantization kernel: its dependency
set grew to 84 files, exceeding the existing 50-file limit.

The kernel imported `get_num_sm` from `cute_dsl.utils`. That shared
module now reaches the public FP4 quantization API through a
scale-layout helper, pulling unrelated quantization and batch-invariant
backends into the kernel's cache key.

Use the existing lower-level `utils.get_device_sm_count` helper instead.
Both helpers cache the device's physical multiprocessor count. This
removes the unnecessary dependency while preserving source hashing and
the existing closure limit.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Observed in nightly pipeline 79161607 on 2026-11-04; no separate public
issue.

### [ffdf2a7](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/ffdf2a7618a3e716d091bb460eeb6f2f705d2325)

- **作者**: Ka-Hyun Nam
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T14:41:57Z
- **提交信息**: test: restore flashinfer modules after logging replay tests (#8437)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`tests/utils/test_logging_replay.py` deletes every `flashinfer*` entry
from `sys.modules` before and after its tests and never puts the
originals back. Test files collected earlier keep the classes and enums
they imported at collection time, while lazy imports after the purge
resolve to freshly created modules, so the two disagree on identity. In
one pytest session this fails later tests with `Softmax can only be
applied to LOGITS, got LOGITS` (all of
`tests/utils/test_logits_processor.py` that builds a pipeline) and
`PicklingError: ... it's not the same object as ...NVFP44Over6Config`
(`TestPickleAndDeepcopy` in
`tests/cpu/utils/test_nvfp4_4over6_config.py`). A skipped replay test is
enough to trigger it, because the fixture runs before the skip.

The fix adds an autouse fixture that snapshots the `flashinfer*` modules
before each test in the file and restores them afterwards, including the
submodule attributes on parent packages. The in-test purges stay, so the
replay tests still re-import under their own logging env vars. The
fixture is file-wide rather than on `level10_environment` only, because
the `test_dump_*` / `test_jsonl_format` / `test_safetensors_*` tests
call `_clean_flashinfer_modules()` directly without that fixture.

Verified on B200 (sm_100), pytest in one process each:

| Session | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/cpu/utils/test_nvfp4_4over6_config.py` alone | 162 passed | 162
passed |
| `tests/utils/test_logits_processor.py` alone | 591 passed, 12 skipped
| 591 passed, 12 skipped |
| `test_logging_replay.py::test_mm_fp8_replay`, then NVFP4 config | 12
failed | 163 passed |
| `test_logging_replay.py`, then `test_logits_processor.py` | 591 failed
| 607 passed, 14 skipped |
| replay + NVFP4 config + logits processor + `test_logging.py` | not run
| 798 passed, 14 skipped |

Not verified: other architectures (the defect is pure Python and was not
run anywhere but B200), the full `tests/utils` directory in one session,
and the two safetensors replay tests, which skip because `safetensors`
was not installed in the test image. `tests/utils/test_logging.py` has a
milder form of the same pattern (it purges only
`flashinfer.api_logging`); it is left unchanged here and passed in the
mixed session above.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Found while running the utils tests on Windows/WSL; no public issue.

### [0102aa9](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/0102aa9f9f4689e167a4e5ea9d1c46b2e431e005)

- **作者**: Shuwen Wang
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T14:39:16Z
- **提交信息**: fix(kda): double-buffer update_ready in the CuTe DSL decomp chain kernel (#8684)

## 📌 Description

`kernel_chain_dv2` (the `mode="decomp"` path of the CuTe DSL KDA
prefill) can hang.

Warp 12 commits `stateq_done(c)` before it waits on `update_ready(c)`.
If warp 12 is delayed there, warp 13 and the CG warps can finish chunk
`c + 1` as well, so the single `update_ready` barrier completes twice.
Its phase parity is then back to the value warp 12 is waiting on, and
warp 12 waits forever while the CG warps wait on its `stateq_done(c +
1)`.

This PR gives `update_ready` two slots, indexed by `chunk % 2` with
parity `(chunk // 2) % 2`. The CG warps arrive for `c + 2` only after
`stateq_done(c + 1)`, which warp 12 issues after its wait for `c`, so a
slot cannot complete twice ahead of it. Nothing else changes.

The fused engine kernel is not affected: its only `update_ready` waiter
also issues the update MMA that gates the next chunk's arrivals.

## 🔍 Related Issues

None.

### [2cb4ca4](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2cb4ca4bb50e209a94124c700b0233f43cb182c8)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T14:30:56Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_gdn_det_kcp): make the byte queries of the deterministic KCP package match what the calls bind (#8808)

`gdn_det_workspace_bytes_kcp` / `gdn_det_workspace_layout_kcp` and
`gdn_det_saved_bytes_kcp` / `gdn_det_saved_layout_kcp` did not count the
same pools that the deterministic KCP calls bind. This change applies
the fix the non-deterministic twin received in #8623. The queries now:

- at P > 1, count the M_f tiles in the forward/backward c1 send pool
(`c1_send_mf`) and the `max(n_in, n_out)` extra fused-walk carry slots;
- size the b1 send/recv pools as the larger of the dense and map layouts
the call binds;
- take a `graph=` keyword (`"off"` | `"replay"`): an eager forward no
longer counts the c2 send pool it never binds, a replayed forward does,
and a replayed backward no longer counts a c2 receive pool;
- size the forward as the max of its prep and walk phases, and leave the
b2 receive pool out of the fused adjoint walk, because the c1 send and
b2 receive pools are released before their walks;
- count the forward exchange pools that a backward on a caller-held
workspace sizes, and accept `save_for_backward=False` with a backward as
the replay case;
- at P > 1 without `save_transfer`, count one kept-form staging plane in
the backward and the other in the kept tapes;
- under `boundary_mode="replay"`, leave the ten full-mode tapes out of
the saved layout and report the replay workspace figure even with
`reuse_recompute_tapes=True`;
- range-check `segments` without building a plan.

Only byte queries, docs and tests change: kernels, launches and outputs
are unchanged, so there is no timing change. The README corrects the
S_in (`n_in * s_pad`) and owner-pair (`2 * s_owner * N_out`) cells. It
also drops a claim that the validator refuses an undersized workspace,
notes that a reused workspace binds the `graph="replay"` figure from the
second step, and says what the queries do not cover. This follows up on
the review of #8755 and #8783.

Cake also ships these separately: a non-deterministic variant of this
kernel, single-GPU GDN training packages without context parallelism
(deterministic and non-deterministic), GDN inference kernels for chunked
prefill and decode, and the KDA deterministic context-parallel training
sibling, which covers the per-channel-gate form; this kernel ships on
sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

### [7729459](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7729459ffe1a4248bf07965f4383e50524b60fd5)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T14:30:32Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_vsa_sm120): run vsa_sm120_blk64 backend on Cake kernels (#8799)

This PR replaces the kernel behind the existing
`BlockSparseAttentionWrapper(backend="vsa_sm120_blk64")` backend with
Cake programs. The API stays the same. The PR delivers every variant of
this kernel: BF16 and FP16 inputs, head dim 128, 64 x 64 blocks,
optional LSE and GQA. Two persistent Cake kernels with bitwise-equal
outputs implement the backend. One runs two 128-thread CTAs per SM, and
the other runs one CTA of two 4-warp groups. For each plan, the host
picks the kernel and how to split long rows. The baseline is the
backend's current CuTe-DSL `sm120_blk64` kernel on main `ed5b3885`.
Built with nvcc 13.0, Cake has a geomean speedup of 1.068 over that
baseline, with 20 of 22 shapes >= 1.0; the slowest shape is
`minimaxh3_local_s18752_h56_r14` at 0.992. Built with nvcc 13.4, the
geomean is 1.084, with 22 of 22 shapes >= 1.0; the slowest shape is
`std_s16384_d10_h32` at 1.018.

Measured on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120, 188
SMs) with driver 595.84.01 and CUDA 13.0 (torch 2.14.1+cu130), using
`flashinfer.testing.bench_gpu_time` with CUPTI and cold L2; each value
is the median of 3 interleaved rounds of `wrapper.run`, and speedup =
main / Cake, so > 1 means Cake is faster. The Cake columns are JIT-built
by nvcc 13.0.88 and by nvcc 13.4.92: ptxas 13.4 schedules these kernels'
MMA instructions back to back and ptxas 13.0 does not, so the speedup

This family ships `sm_120a` and `sm_121a` builds; Cake also ships VSA
block-sparse attention for SM100/SM103
(`BlockSparseAttentionWrapper(backend="cake")`, BF16 and a Sage FP8
form), SM90 (`VariableBlockSparseAttentionWrapper(backend="cake")`, BF16
and Sage FP8) and an SM120 Sage form (INT8 QK / FP8 PV).

### [69d69ae](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/69d69ae18debfdd93b87922adb84bfdef99eafdd)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T14:19:08Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_dense_projection_gemm): keep workspace buffers alive for captured CUDA graphs (#8812)

This is a correctness fix for CUDA graph capture on the
`deterministic=False` convenience path of
`flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm`; kernels, plans and
routes are unchanged. The path keeps its split-K and stream-K workspaces
in one arena per (device, stream); on main, growing an arena frees the
buffer it replaces and evicting a cache entry can release its arena, so
a captured graph can replay into memory that the allocator has since
given to other tensors. With this change a growth retires the replaced
buffer instead of freeing it and eviction leaves the arena in place, so
every workspace buffer stays allocated until
`clear_convenience_caches()` or `use_deterministic_backend()`, which are
documented to invalidate captured graphs. The memory cost is bounded: a
growth at least doubles a buffer, so the retired buffers of a kind hold
fewer bytes than its live one, and a kind holds at most four times its
largest requested size (16 elements minimum).


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai
-->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
* CUDA graphs captured through convenience calls now remain safe to
replay after workspace growth or cache eviction, provided their caches
have not been cleared.
* Calls captured on the same stream should be replayed one at a time,
not concurrently with other calls on that stream.
  * K2 split launches now zero the output on the launch stream.

* **Documentation**
* Clarified workspace retention and growth limits, and when clearing
convenience caches invalidates captured graphs.

### [f8bedda](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/f8bedda6038a3eff3b6953664c385c6b9eb0f1a3)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T14:16:08Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): restore the K1 weight-gradient routes on 216-SM sm_107a parts (#8782)

Cake's dense projection GEMM ships as two packages: the deterministic
`flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_det_gemm` and the
non-deterministic `flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm`. The
non-deterministic package holds two GEMMs: K1 (BF16 or FP32 output) and
an FP32 router GEMM. Each has forward, weight-gradient (wgrad) and
input-gradient (dgrad) programs. #8743 restored the faster
non-deterministic K1 wgrad routes on the `deterministic=False` path for
148- and 152-SM sm_100a and sm_103a parts and for 212- and 208-SM R200
parts. This PR restores them on R200 (sm_107a) parts with exactly 216
SMs, in five windows over four shapes. On main, these windows run the
deterministic package's wgrad program. Parts with 217 or more SMs keep
main's routes. The other variants (the deterministic package, the router
GEMM, and K1's forward and dgrad programs) also ship for sm_100a,
sm_103a and sm_107a, and this PR changes K1 wgrad routing on 216-SM
sm_107a parts only.

**216-SM R200 windows (60 rows).** The new route is faster than
deterministic Cake in all 60 rows, and deterministic Cake is main's
route on these rows. Across CUDA graph and eager mode, the new route is
1.06–2.23x faster in wgrad, 1.03–1.71x in bwd and 1.01–1.33x in the
checkpointed 2fwd+bwd step.

Against non-Cake SOTA, the new route is 0.55–1.04x in wgrad, 0.58–0.98x
in bwd and 0.50–0.98x in 2fwd+bwd. Only four rows reach 1.00x or better,
all of them wgrad:
- 4096→512 at T = 16173: 1.01x in both modes.
- 8192→128 at T = 8128: 1.03x under CUDA graph and 1.04x in eager.

The other 56 rows are slower than SOTA. The lowest is 8192→128 at T =
1025, 2fwd+bwd under CUDA graph, at 0.50x. It is unknown whether the
SOTA library launches meet the original FP32 budget (see the caption).

*Min and max speedup over the 60 rows of the per-shape table below. The
rows cover the 5 windows this PR restores on R200 parts with exactly 216
SMs: 4096→512 n128, 1 split (T = 16173–32767 except 16231 and 16384);
4096→1024 n192, 1 split (T = 16173–16383 except 16231); 4096→1024 n256,
1 split (T = 16385–32767); 5120→1024 n256, 1 split (T = 16385–32768);
and 8192→128 n128, 2 splits (T = 1025–8192, odd numbers of 64-token K
blocks only). Each window appears at its first and last token count T,
in CUDA graph and eager mode, and every window edge was timed exactly. T
= 16173 is the first T of both the 4096→512 window and the 4096→1024
(n192) window. T = 16172, 16231 and 16384 lie outside every window and
keep main's route. Parts with more than 216 SMs keep main's routes and
are not in the table. GPU: R200 (sm_107a, 216 SMs), driver 615.71.10
(CUDA driver API 13.4). CUDA 13.4 toolchain (nvcc 13.4.92), cuBLAS /
cuBLASLt 13.8.0.4, torch 2.14.1+cu130. Latency method: the L2 was
flushed before every iteration by zeroing a 2 x L2 buffer (cold L2).
Latency is the CUPTI span of all launches of the operation, using CUDA
graph replay or eager launch. Each value is the median of 4 per-process
medians, from two process layouts x two launch orders. Each process ran
15 rotated groups x 20 timed iterations for wgrad, and 9 groups x 20 for
bwd and 2fwd+bwd. Deterministic Cake = the deterministic package's
program. Main already runs it on these rows for `deterministic=False`,
so it is also the previous route. Non-Cake SOTA = the fastest of
torch.mm (cuBLAS heuristic) and the cuBLASLt heuristic's top-8
algorithms, picked per process and mode, with the same BF16 inputs and
FP32 output, measured in the same processes. cuBLASLt was fastest in 68
of the 80 wgrad cells (20 wgrad rows x 4 processes) and torch.mm in 12.
For bwd and 2fwd+bwd, SOTA uses the fastest library launch per GEMM. It
is unknown whether these library launches meet the original FP32 budget
(rel_fro ≤ 5e-5 and max|err| ≤ 1e-3·max|ref| vs FP64), because that
check is not in the results available for this table. The benchmark
required only rel_fro ≤ 1e-3 vs FP64 for the cuBLASLt algorithms and for
the per-GEMM library picks, or 2e-2 for the BF16-output forward and
dgrad. It did not apply an accuracy filter to torch.mm in wgrad. The new
route's program met the original FP32 budget at all 32 timed (shape, T)
points inside these windows, with 10 input seeds x 20 reruns each.
Speedup = baseline latency / new latency (> 1 means the new route is
faster). bwd = dgrad + wgrad. 2fwd+bwd = checkpointed step (2 x forward
+ dgrad + wgrad). Each Cake arm uses its own package's forward and dgrad
programs. A/A noise: a second, independently prepared launch of the
deterministic wgrad program was timed in the same processes, over all 38
timed (shape, T) groups of the two runs on this part. The ratio of
deterministic to A/A wgrad was 0.951–1.008 under CUDA graph and
0.990–1.015 in eager. When the A/A launch ran with this package's
forward and dgrad, as in the new arm, the bwd and 2fwd+bwd ratios were
0.944–1.046 under CUDA graph and 0.919–1.041 in eager.*

### [f0ec379](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/f0ec379398e0ba6f38a8093415b489405a21fedb)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T14:09:04Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_grouped_fp8_gemm): SM107a single-run BLOCK_N 256 below 32 K blocks (#8809)

`cake_grouped_fp8_gemm` is Cake's prepared contiguous grouped FP8 GEMM.
On sm_100a and sm_103a it ships three variants: FP32-scale (promotion)
programs, block-scaled programs with packed UE8M0 scales, and a fused
gate_up + SwiGLU + FP8 quant form. On sm_107a it ships only the
block-scaled UE8M0 variant, and this PR changes only that variant. This
PR changes how the host picks BLOCK_N for single-run layouts on sm_107a,
which covers the 216-SM R200 class and the 208/212-SM parts. A
single-run layout now uses the BLOCK_N 256 program whenever the K loop
has fewer than 32 K blocks, however many M blocks there are. Otherwise
it uses BLOCK_N 128. Before this PR, BLOCK_N 256 was picked only when
there were few M blocks or few valid blocks. Only the host routing
changes. No new program is added. The baseline is the previous Cake
route, BLOCK_N 128.

Shapes whose route changes (alignment 128, G = 256):

| Shape | M, N, K | GPU (SMs) | before µs (hot) | this PR µs (hot) |
speedup hot (noise) | speedup cooled (noise) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fib_q35b_gate_up_t4096 | 65280, 1024, 2048 | R200 (216) | 89.71 |
81.06 | 1.1070 (0.16%) | 1.1077 (0.18%) |
| fib_q35b_gate_up_t4096 | 65280, 1024, 2048 | R200 (212) | 84.85 |
76.17 | 1.1141 (0.25%) | 1.1137 (0.11%) |
| q35b_gate_up_t4096_a128 | 65280, 1024, 2048 | R200 (216) | 87.36 |
80.74 | 1.0830 (0.33%) | 1.0834 (0.18%) |

76.53 | 1.0688 (1.10%) | 1.0685 (0.16%) |

GPU product NVIDIA R200, architecture sm_107a, CUDA 13.4. Before =
BLOCK_N 128, this PR = BLOCK_N 256. Each value is the median over 3
operand seeds with a cold L2, in hot and cooled windows. Speedup =
before / after; above 1 is faster.

Every other shape of the 63-shape list keeps its route and program on
sm_107a, and sm_100a and sm_103a are unchanged.

### [386275f](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/386275f02fc63a74d27b2c6469deffc07f2e6ea5)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T14:08:55Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_rmsnorm_train): end the sm_103a H2048 det-pair backward windows below their dw budget breach (#8810)

Related issue: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/8066

`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_train` is RMSNorm for training. The forward
returns y (BF16) and rstd (FP32), and the backward returns dx (BF16) and
dw (FP32). It has two modes, `deterministic=True` and
`deterministic=False`. Both use the same forward and differ only in the
backward. Both modes support the forms listed in #8655 on sm_100a
(B200), sm_103a (GB300) and sm_107a (R200):

- [T, H] rows with BF16 or FP32 weight
- fused residual add (H6144)
- per-head views [T,24,256] and [T,4,256] with a shared w[256]

This PR fixes accuracy in one of these variants: the
`deterministic=False` backward of H2048 [T, H] rows on sm_103a, with
BF16 weight and with FP32 weight.

On main, this backward uses a pair of programs from the deterministic
package (the det pair) from T 32769 to 61952. The pair is the
deterministic package's main kernel and its fixed-order dw reduce, which
the deterministic package itself uses only up to T 55296. On GB300, the
pair's worst dw element exceeds the per-element budget (atol 1e-4 + rtol
1e-4 against an FP64 reference) at T 58560. It reaches 1.0622 of the
budget with FP32 weight. With BF16 weight, the pair computes the same dw
as with FP32 weight for equal inputs, so it has the same breach.

With this PR, the pair runs only up to T 58496, the last multiple of 64
below T 58560. From T 58497 to 61952, the backward runs the same program
that `deterministic=True` runs at these token counts. Its worst dw
element is 0.9454 of the budget at the sampled T from 58497 to 61952 on
GB300. Nothing else changes: T up to 58496, T above 61952, the forward,
other forms, other architectures and the deterministic package all stay
as they are.

This is an accuracy-budget fix, and it makes the backward about 1 %
slower than main's `deterministic=False` backward (main ND), which is
the pair this PR replaces at these T. Here new is `deterministic=False`
with this PR, and new/main ND is new latency / main ND latency, so a
value > 1 means new is slower. On all 6 bwd rows, new/main ND ranges
from 1.0074 to 1.0102:

- 1.0074: H2048 T61952 w FP32, new 122.2720 us vs main ND 121.3770 us
- 1.0102: H2048 T60224 w BF16, new 120.3205 us vs main ND 119.1050 us

On 2xfwd+bwd, new/main ND is 1.0050 to 1.0055. The forward is the same
program in both builds, and its new/main ND is 0.9991 to 1.0014.

Against the two baselines, det (Cake `deterministic=True`) and SOTA (the
fastest non-Cake candidate within the accuracy budget), where a ratio >
1 means new is faster:

- det/new is 0.9982 to 1.0013 over all 18 rows. At these T, both modes
run the same forward and the same backward program.
- SOTA/new is 1.1008 to 1.3441 for bwd, 1.0636 to 1.1736 for 2xfwd+bwd
and 1.0000 to 1.0332 for fwd.

**GB300 (sm_103a): this PR (new) vs deterministic Cake (det) vs the
fastest non-Cake candidate (SOTA) vs main's `deterministic=False` (main
ND), H2048, T 58497 to 61952**

- GPU: NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a), one node, all 4 GPUs (aarch64 host).
- Software: NVIDIA driver 580.159.03; CUDA toolkit Build
cuda_13.4.r13.4/compiler.38855100_0; torch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA runtime
13.0).
- Timing:
- 4 sessions run in parallel, one process per GPU, as the node's only
work.
- Each session holds det, new and every non-Cake candidate for all 6
shape rows.
- Implementations are timed in an order set by a balanced design over
the 4 sessions x 3 rounds, so every implementation takes every position
about equally often.
- Each fwd, bwd and 2xfwd+bwd latency is the CUPTI span of one
CUDA-graph replay after an L2 flush.
- Each session runs 201 replays per implementation and op, split over
the 3 rounds.
- Each reported latency is the median of the span samples pooled over
the 4 sessions.
- Each span includes the implementation's own setup, reduction, cast and
copy kernels.
- main ND: measured in a second run on the same node with main's build,
so new/main ND compares two runs.
- Noise: A/A means the same implementation timed as two interleaved
arms, each with its own buffers. The per-session noise floor (max |1 -
A/A| over every row and op, det and new arms) is 0.0061 to 0.0093 in the
run with this PR and 0.0059 to 0.0099 in the run with main. The floor
maxima are on fwd rows. On bwd rows, max |1 - A/A| is 0.0038 in the run
with this PR and 0.0028 in the run with main.
- Measured build: new was measured on an earlier revision of this
branch. That revision differs from this PR only in comments and
commit-message text.
- Workload, the same for every implementation: x BF16 [T, H], no
residual. The effective weight w is BF16 or FP32 (no in-kernel 1 + w).
eps 1e-6. Outputs: y BF16, rstd FP32, dx BF16, dw FP32.
- Baselines:
  - det: Cake `deterministic=True`, measured in the same run as new.
- SOTA: the fastest non-Cake candidate that produces these outputs and
meets the accuracy budget, measured in the same run as new. The budget
is dx atol = rtol = 1e-2, and dw per element atol 1e-4 + rtol 1e-4 vs
FP64, taking the worst of 5 seeds. On the four T60224 bwd and 2xfwd+bwd
rows, QuACK is faster than the listed SOTA, but its dw exceeds the
budget there, so it is not the baseline. Candidates timed:
- QuACK 0.6.5 (nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.1): the low-level API and the
autotuned API
- torch.compile in max-autotune-no-cudagraphs mode and in default mode
    - Transformer Engine 2.20.2
    - Liger-Kernel 0.8.5 (Triton 3.8.0)
- PyTorch fused RMSNorm (`aten._fused_rms_norm`) does not accept BF16 x
with an FP32 weight, so it has no FP32-dw result on these rows.
- On the BF16-weight rows, QuACK, PyTorch, Transformer Engine and
Liger-Kernel are also timed through their APIs as is. These return BF16
dw there, so they are never chosen as the baseline.
  - SOTA winners on these rows:
- compile = torch.compile(mode=max-autotune-no-cudagraphs,
dynamic=False, fullgraph=True) (torch 2.14.1+cu130,
emulate_precision_casts=True) of the explicit FP32-statistics reference
forward and backward, FP32 dw
- quack = QuACK low-level _rmsnorm_fwd / _rmsnorm_bwd, FP32 dw = sum of
its FP32 partials (no narrowing)
- quack_tuned = QuACK rmsnorm_fwd_tuned / rmsnorm_bwd_tuned (exhaustive
autotune per shape), FP32 dw
- main ND: `deterministic=False` at main c5bd9da2, the base of this PR.
On these rows its backward is the det pair described above.
  - new: `deterministic=False` with this PR.
- Context: Cake gains somewhat more from the context than the other
non-compile libraries on small rows: SOTA/new vs the non-compile
candidates is up to about 1.10x higher (GB300) / 1.14x higher (B200) in
the one-process measurement than in a process without torch.compile;
large rows <= 1.02x. So small-row ratios may overstate the new kernel's
lead by up to about that much. Ratios vs det are unaffected.
- Ratios: det/new and SOTA/new = baseline latency / new latency, so a
value > 1 means new is faster. new/main ND = new latency / main ND
latency, so a value > 1 means new is slower.
- op: 2xfwd+bwd (checkpointed) = two forwards and one backward.

Rows: 6 shapes (H2048 at T 58497, 60224 and 61952, each with BF16 and
FP32 weight) x 3 ops = 18 rows. On every row, det and new run the same
programs. The ratios are measured, and none is set to 1.

|row (H / T / weight)|op|det us|SOTA us (impl)|new us|main ND us|det/new

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

### [8baa822](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/8baa822f846eab3b0466742be686a540a84b5025)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T12:46:30Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): plain FP32 SIMT router windows on 148-SM sm_100a / sm_103a parts (#8763)

Cake's dense projection GEMM ships as a deterministic package and a
non-deterministic package
(`flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm`). The non-deterministic
package includes an FP32 router GEMM (E = 256 experts) with forward,
weight-gradient (wgrad) and input-gradient (dgrad) programs. This PR
changes the router wgrad and dgrad routes on the `deterministic=False`
path of 148-SM B200 (sm_100a) and B300 (sm_103a) parts. On these parts
main runs #8707's compensated (Kahan / Dot2) FP32 SIMT programs for
wgrad at T ≤ 160 and for dgrad at T ≤ 32, and the deterministic program
above those token counts. This PR switches both ops to the plain FFMA
SIMT programs of #8730 in measured token windows. wgrad: H = 4096, T =
2–224 (`simt_n128m64s2`); H = 5120, T = 1–256 (`simt_n64m64s2`); H =
6144, T = 1–256 (`simt_n64m64s2`). At H = 4096, T = 1, wgrad keeps the
compensated Dot2 program. dgrad: H = 4096, T = 1–64 (`simt_m32n64s8`); H
= 5120, T = 1–32 (`simt_m32n64s8`); H = 5120, T = 64–128
(`simt_m32n64s4`), B200 only; H = 6144, T = 1–32 (`simt_m32n64s8`). The
forward and all other token counts keep main's route. The new programs
stay inside the router accuracy budget (worst rel_fro 2.1e-7 vs FP64;
budget 2e-6).

Against main's current route, the changed op is 1.24–3.05x faster where
it replaces #8707's compensated programs (89 op rows). Where it replaces
the deterministic program in the widened windows it is 1.10–2.00x faster
(24 op rows: wgrad 1.15–1.62x, dgrad 1.10–2.00x). bwd gains 1.07–2.14x
and 2fwd+bwd gains 1.01–1.19x. No row is slower than main. Five 2fwd+bwd
rows (1.01–1.04x) are inside the A/A noise band. The deterministic Cake
column in the tables below matches main's route only in the 56 rows
where main runs the deterministic program: op rows with wgrad T > 160 or
dgrad T > 32, and bwd and 2fwd+bwd rows at T > 160. In every other row
it overstates the gain over main.

Against deterministic Cake the new route is faster in 263 of 267 rows,
at 1.04–5.37x (wgrad 1.15–5.37x, dgrad 1.10–2.07x, bwd 1.07–3.32x,
2fwd+bwd 1.04–1.33x). The other 4 rows, all 2fwd+bwd at T = 224 and 256
(1.01–1.04x), are inside the A/A noise band. "Non-Cake SOTA" is the
fastest in-budget non-Cake library kernel measured for each cell; the
caption lists the library arms and their accuracy status. Against it the
new route is faster in 100 rows, inside the A/A noise band in 51 and
slower in 116. It is slower:

- at T = 1: wgrad 0.67–0.77x, dgrad 0.77–0.80x, bwd 0.71–0.78x;
- for wgrad in 9 rows at T ≥ 65: 0.92–0.97x;
- for dgrad in 3 rows at T = 2 on B200: 0.87–0.90x;
- for bwd in 14 rows at T = 33–128, where dgrad stays on the
deterministic program: 0.83–0.87x, and in 2 rows at T = 2 on B200, where
both ops run the new programs: 0.93–0.95x.

The checkpointed step never beats SOTA. It is slower in 72 of the 77
2fwd+bwd rows (0.26–0.97x), and the other 5 (0.98–0.99x) are inside the
A/A noise band. Its two forward calls run the deterministic program,
which is 1.1x to more than 5x slower than the fastest library forward.

| GPU | op | rows | vs deterministic Cake, min | vs deterministic Cake,
max | vs non-Cake SOTA, min | vs non-Cake SOTA, max |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| B200 sm_100a | wgrad | 38 | 1.15 | 5.36 | 0.67 | 1.24 |

*Min and max speedup over the 267 rows of the per-shape table below
(FP32 router, E = 256, H = 4096 / 5120 / 6144, T inside the windows this
PR changes, `deterministic=False`). GPUs: NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs)
and NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (sm_103a, 148 SMs). Software: CUDA 13.4
toolchain (nvcc V13.4.92), torch 2.14.1+cu130, cuBLAS / cuBLASLt
13.1.1.3. Some timing runs did not record their container image; for
those runs these versions come from other GPU runs with the same Python
environment. Latency method: CUDA graph replay with L2 flushed before
every iteration (cold L2), measured as the CUPTI op span (first start to
last end of the op's kernel, memset and copy activities). Each cell is
the median of 15 paired groups per process, then the median over run A
(several rows in one process) and run B (one process per row). A/A
noise: the same Cake programs timed as two arms gave paired ratios of
0.968–1.038 on B200 and 0.966–1.029 on B300. One B200 cell is left out
of that band: the current route timed against itself at H = 6144, T = 2,
wgrad, which gave 0.900 in one of its two runs. A row counts as faster
or slower only when its ratio, before rounding, is outside the band of
its own runs and, against non-Cake SOTA, the paired ratio of each run is
on the same side of 1; otherwise it counts as parity. Speedup = baseline
latency / new latency (> 1 means the new program is faster).
Deterministic Cake = the deterministic package's programs. Non-Cake SOTA
= for each cell, the fastest of five library arms measured in the same
runs: cublasSgemm (default math, no TF32), cuBLASLt FP32 (the fastest
in-budget of its top-8 heuristics), torch.mm FP32 with TF32 off, cuBLAS
BF16x9 FP32 emulation, and a per-GEMM mix (each GEMM of the op takes the
fastest of those four in a pre-timing). Every arm was checked against
FP64 in every run and met the router budget (rel_fro ≤ 2e-6). Worst
rel_fro: cublasSgemm 2.9e-7, cuBLASLt 3.0e-7, torch.mm 2.9e-7, BF16x9
3.7e-7, mix 3.0e-7, new programs 2.1e-7. The fastest arm was cublasSgemm
in 54 rows, cuBLASLt in 74, torch.mm in 72 and the mix in 67. BF16x9 was
never the fastest arm. bwd = dgrad + wgrad. 2fwd+bwd = checkpointed step
(2 x forward + dgrad + wgrad); the forward is the deterministic program
in every Cake arm. Where T is inside only one op's window, bwd and
2fwd+bwd run the other op on main's route ("unchanged").*

The kernel's other Cake variants, the deterministic package
(`flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_det_gemm`), the K1 GEMM (BF16
or FP32 output), the router forward and the router backward on parts
other than 148-SM B200 / B300, are unchanged; the family ships for
sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a, and this PR changes only the router
backward routes of 148-SM sm_100a and sm_103a parts.

refreshed the documented measurements and accuracy limits.

### [c3e28f8](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c3e28f87a049f75526367917626e7ef47a339157)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T12:42:01Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_indexer_det): run the FP8 l6 program for wide-unit decisions (#8781)

The deterministic DSA indexer top-k,
`flashinfer.dsa_indexer.dsa_indexer_det_topk(..., backend="cake")`, has
two Cake variants. This PR changes only the opt-in FP8 form (added by
#8749). The FP8 form has no 8-query wide program, so calls planned as an
unsplit wide unit now run the 6-query l6 program instead of the 4-query
narrow program. On NVIDIA B200, s1_8k_on_64k and s2_4x2k_packed change
program and run 1.02x and 1.07x faster than the previous Cake FP8 form.
On NVIDIA GB300 and sm_107a, only s1_8k_on_64k changes program, and it
runs 1.13x and 1.11x faster, respectively. P1, glm2k_16k and s3_cold16k
already ran the l6 program on all three GPUs. s2_4x2k_packed keeps its
program on GB300 and sm_107a. These rows read 0.99x to 1.01x, which is
parity, not a speedup.

**NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), CUDA 13.4, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.** All
rows use top-k 2048, key ratio 1 and causal queries (each segment's
queries are its last positions). P1 is a recorded packed training call.
s2_4x2k_packed is 4 x 2048 queries over 18432 / 43008 / 67584 / 100352
keys. Previous Cake FP8 is the FP8 form on main before this PR, with its
dispatch reproduced in the same process. DeepGEMM + FlashInfer top-k
runs DeepGEMM `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` (branch `nv_dev`, commit `b64107f2`)
with FP32 per-key K scales and FP32 logits. FlashInfer
`top_k_ragged_transform(deterministic=True, tie_break=LARGE)` then runs
over each row's visible keys. This baseline computes the same scores
from the same inputs. Each time is the CUPTI GPU interval over every
kernel that the call launches, with cold L2 and eager launch. Cake arms
time a prepared runner into caller-owned outputs and workspace. Each
value is the median over three arm orders (A then B, B then A,
interleaved). "vs previous" = previous time / this PR time. "vs
DeepGEMM" = DeepGEMM time / this PR time. A value above 1 means this PR
is faster.

DeepGEMM |

| s1_8k_on_64k | 8192 | 73728 | 1 | 3.651 | 3.581 | 1.02x | 4.245 |
1.19x |
| s2_4x2k_packed | 8192 | 229376 | 4 | 3.094 | 2.879 | 1.07x | 3.773 |
1.31x |
| s3_cold16k | 16384 | 16384 | 1 | 1.256 | 1.254 | 1.00x | 1.903 | 1.52x
|

**sm_107a (212 SMs), CUDA 13.4, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.** Same timing
method and previous Cake FP8 baseline as B200. DeepGEMM `nv_dev`
`b64107f2` does not run on sm_107a: its FP8 logits kernel hits a
device-side assert. P1 runs the same program in both arms, and its 0.99x
is parity within the 1.6 % spread (2.142 to 2.176 ms) between separate
arms of that program.

The other Cake variant, the default BF16 form, is unchanged, and the
kernel family covers sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* FP8 dispatch comparisons now include additional options for evaluating
the `l6` and narrow execution paths.
* **Bug Fixes**
* FP8 wide workloads can now use the `l6` fallback, with sampling and
check-period settings adjusted for the selected fallback.
* **Documentation**
* The FP8 workspace requirement for the `l6` fallback is larger than for
the narrow fallback. Buffers sized for the previous fallback may be
rejected; use the workspace-size function to determine the required
capacity.

### [3bab410](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3bab410bc81e469de7fe43091c9c7721a8719952)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T12:37:14Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_indexer_det): split few-query calls so each split holds at most top_k keys on sm_107a (#8802)

`flashinfer.dsa_indexer.dsa_indexer_det_topk` (backend `"cake"`) is the
Cake deterministic DSA indexer top-k scan. It ships in the package
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_dsa_indexer_det`. It uses BF16 queries and
keys, and FP32 head weights and scores. It returns the top-k key ids for
each query. The ids and scores do not depend on partitioning or
chunking. Ties go to the larger id. Cake ships two variants of this
kernel in FlashInfer: the BF16 form, which is the default, and the
opt-in FP8 (e4m3) form. This PR changes the BF16 form on sm_107a only.

The sm_107a host dispatch record now uses the same split-count rule that
#8725 added for sm_100a and sm_103a. This applies to calls with few
queries per segment that the floor rule already splits. For these calls,
the host uses ceil(mean keys per work unit / top_k) splits if that count
fits the split limit and the grid. The count is rounded up to whole
4096-entry merge chunks. Each split then holds at most top_k keys. For
example, 5 splits become 12 (A1), 7 become 16 (A2 and the 32k rows), and
3 become 8 (the 16k rows). Every other call keeps its plan and program.
The kernel code does not change. Only the host policy does. The FP8
form's sm_107a record has no split-count rule, so FP8 plans on sm_107a
do not change. sm_100a and sm_103a are not changed by this PR.

Only two prepared-call rows change their plan. A1 has 4 queries and
22018 keys and goes from 5 to 12 splits (0.0459 -> 0.0385 ms, 1.192x).
A2 has 4 queries and 30466 keys and goes from 7 to 16 splits (0.0496 ->
0.0460 ms, 1.078x). The eager entry shows the same rows at 1.193x (A1)
and 1.080x (A2). Each split-count rule row has 1 to 64 queries over 16k
or 32k keys in one segment. These rows are 1.06x-1.53x faster. The 16k
rows go from 3 to 8 splits and are about 1.43-1.53x faster. The 32k rows
go from 7 to 16 splits and are about 1.06-1.13x faster. All other
prepared, eager and side-stream rows are unchanged within run-to-run
noise. The side-stream rows range from 0.987x to 1.003x. The lowest is
C2 with 32 SMs held (1.8211 -> 1.8453 ms, 0.987x).

The baseline is the previous Cake version, FlashInfer main `dfc8e4d6`.
All measurements were taken on sm_107a (212 SMs) with CUDA 13.4. Speedup
is main time divided by this PR time, so values above 1 mean faster.
Every row is timed in fresh processes, 4 per row, in both arm orders.
Each time is the CUPTI GPU time of one synchronized call, and the
reported value is the median over processes. Output bits match main on
every row of every table.

| sm_107a (212 SMs, CUDA 13.4) | ratios | min | max |
|---|---|---|---|
| prepared calls | 64 (32 shapes x sampling on/off) | 0.992x (S2,
sampling off) | 1.192x (A1) |
| split-count rule rows | 16 (8 shapes x sampling on/off) | 1.059x
(W1_32k) | 1.526x (W4_16k) |
| eager entry | 8 | 0.999x (S1, S2) | 1.193x (A1) |
| side stream | 12 (6 shapes x 1 or 32 SMs held) | 0.987x (C2, 32 SMs
held) | 1.003x (S6, 1 SM held) |

### [79cf055](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/79cf05572cab13a60dda6a055589f40bd1d93b65)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T11:27:53Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_batch_deepgemm_fp8): SM107a (B, expected_m) cell table for three masked geometries (#8798)

`cake_batch_deepgemm_fp8` is Cake's masked batch DeepGEMM FP8 kernel. It
has one route chain per architecture: sm_100a (148 SMs), sm_103a (152
SMs) and sm_107a (216 SMs). Until now, the sm_107a chain picked one of
six programs by CTA band. This PR changes that for three masked
geometries: N=128 K=512, N=512 K=128 and N=7168 K=2048. For these, the
216-SM sm_107a chain picks the program per (B, em4) cell, where em4 is
expected_m in quarter-octave bins. Seven new sm_107a programs back the
cells. For a key that has no cell, 128x512 and 512x128 use the nearest
cell, and 7168x2048 keeps its CTA bands. The BLOCK_N 128 K-tile 256
program was routed only by the N=128 K=512 band, so this PR removes it.
The baseline is the previous Cake version: the shipped sm_107a 216-SM
bands. Geomean speedups over the holdout row-seeds are 1.164x on
128x512, 1.186x on 512x128 and 1.038x on 7168x2048.

bands.

### [74d202d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/74d202d77f051f8f77924c4210d1a791da25da18)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T11:27:26Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): one split of 64-wide tiles for the FP32 K1 weight gradient 4096 -> 32 / 128 on 152-SM parts (#8760)

Cake's dense projection GEMM ships as two packages: the deterministic
`flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_det_gemm` and the
non-deterministic `flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm`. The
non-deterministic package holds two GEMMs: K1 (BF16 or FP32 output) and
an FP32 router GEMM. Each GEMM has forward, weight-gradient (wgrad) and
input-gradient (dgrad) programs.

This PR adds a one-split K1 wgrad route for FP32 output on the
`deterministic=False` path. The route uses block_n 64 and one K split. A
new `K1_ONE_SPLIT_RANGES_BY_SM` table selects it. It applies only to
parts with exactly 152 SMs, in four windows:
- 4096→32 at T = 256–2048 on GB200 (sm_100a) and on GB300 (sm_103a)
- 4096→128 at T = 256–3328 on GB200
- 4096→128 at T = 256–2816 on GB300

Other shapes, token counts and SM counts keep their current routes. At
every timed point in these windows, the route meets the deterministic
package's FP32 budget against an FP64 reference: rel_fro ≤ 5e-5 and
max_abs ≤ 1e-3 · max|ref|.

Under CUDA graph replay, the new route is faster than deterministic Cake
at every timed point: 1.15–2.19x in wgrad, 1.12–1.66x in bwd and
1.03–1.22x in 2fwd+bwd. Non-Cake SOTA is faster than the new route at
every timed point. The speedup vs SOTA is 0.64–0.79x in wgrad,
0.62–0.86x in bwd and 0.42–0.66x in 2fwd+bwd.

| GPU | op | timed points | vs deterministic Cake, min | vs
deterministic Cake, max | vs non-Cake SOTA, min | vs non-Cake SOTA, max
|
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GB200 (sm_100a, 152 SMs) | wgrad | 28 | 1.15 | 2.19 | 0.65 | 0.79 |
| GB200 (sm_100a, 152 SMs) | bwd | 28 | 1.12 | 1.66 | 0.62 | 0.85 |
| GB200 (sm_100a, 152 SMs) | 2fwd+bwd | 28 | 1.03 | 1.22 | 0.42 | 0.66 |
| GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs) | wgrad | 30 | 1.16 | 2.19 | 0.64 | 0.79 |
| GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs) | bwd | 30 | 1.12 | 1.66 | 0.62 | 0.86 |
| GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs) | 2fwd+bwd | 30 | 1.03 | 1.22 | 0.42 | 0.65 |

*Min and max speedup over all 58 timed points inside the four windows
this PR changes (GB200 (sm_100a, 152 SMs) 4096→32 T = 256–2048; GB200
(sm_100a, 152 SMs) 4096→128 T = 256–3328; GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs)
4096→32 T = 256–2048; GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs) 4096→128 T = 256–2816); a
point timed in two runs counts twice. The per-shape table below lists
105 rows at 27 representative points: each window's first and last timed
token count T, T = 1024, and T = 512, 768, 1536, 2048, 2816, 3072 and
3328 where they were timed inside the window; a point timed in two runs
appears twice, the second marked "repeat run". GPUs: GB200 (sm_100a, 152
SMs), driver 580.126.20; GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), driver 580.159.03.
CUDA 13.4 toolchain (nvcc 13.4.92), cuBLAS / cuBLASLt 13.8.0, torch
2.14.1+cu130. Latency: CUDA graph replay, with L2 flushed (a 2 x L2
buffer zeroed) before every iteration, measured as the CUPTI span of all
launches of the operation. Each value is the median over 4 processes
(two launch layouts x two row orders) of the per-process medians (15
groups of 20 iterations for wgrad, 15 groups for bwd and 2fwd+bwd). In
eager mode, in the same processes, wgrad is 1.14–2.20x vs deterministic
Cake and 0.62–0.81x vs non-Cake SOTA. Deterministic Cake = the
deterministic package's wgrad program (for bwd and 2fwd+bwd, also its
forward and dgrad programs). Non-Cake SOTA for wgrad = in each process
and launch mode the fastest of torch.mm (cuBLAS heuristic) and the
cuBLASLt heuristic's top-8 algorithms (CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F), with the
same BF16 inputs and FP32 output, measured in the same processes; each
of these library arms met the original FP32 accuracy budget (against an
FP64 reference: relative Frobenius error ≤ 5e-5 and max abs error ≤ 1e-3
x max|ref|, 3 reruns in each process) at all 58 timed points. Non-Cake
SOTA for bwd and 2fwd+bwd = whichever of two whole-step library arms,
measured in the same processes, has the lower median over the 4
processes: per operation the library call fastest in a CUDA-event
pre-timing, or torch.mm for every operation. For these bwd and 2fwd+bwd
SOTA values (232 cells: all 58 timed points, graph and eager), it is not
known whether the library arms met that budget: the whole-step runs
recorded only each library call's relative Frobenius error (wgrad at
most 3.54e-6), not its max abs error, and the forward and dgrad calls
have BF16 output, to which the FP32 budget does not apply. New = the
non-deterministic package with this PR's wgrad route (block_n 64, one K
split) and its own forward and dgrad programs. bwd = dgrad + wgrad;
2fwd+bwd = checkpointed step (2 x forward + dgrad + wgrad). Speedup =
baseline latency / new latency (> 1 means the new route is faster). In
CUDA graph replay, non-Cake SOTA is faster than the new route at every
timed point, in wgrad, bwd and 2fwd+bwd. A/A noise: a wgrad program
timed against a second, independently prepared instance of itself in the
same processes, over every timed point of these runs, inside and outside
the windows (wgrad, bwd and 2fwd+bwd, eager and graph): 0.974–1.022
(GB200), 0.981–1.027 (GB300). At points where the route before this PR
runs the deterministic wgrad program, one instance runs bwd and 2fwd+bwd
through the deterministic package's forward and dgrad calls and the
other through the non-deterministic package's.*

The kernel's other Cake variants (the deterministic package, K1 with
BF16 output, K1's forward and dgrad programs, and the router GEMM) ship
for sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a, and this PR changes only K1 FP32 wgrad
routing on 152-SM sm_100a and sm_103a parts, with no sm_107a change.

checks, and reported results.

### [92e6998](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/92e6998f891642c3c7293eb9e6d6cb1e8a7b0aff)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T11:21:13Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dcp): run near-grid E4M3 head_dim-128 launches with 4+ query rows on program 0 (#8797)

The E4M3 head_dim-128 family of `flashinfer.cake_dcp` uses BF16 query
and output with an FP8 E4M3 paged KV cache. It has three programs, and
the host picks one from launch metadata:

- Program 0 is the persistent planner program without the idle-CTA
eight-slice fold.
- Program 1 is the same planner program with that fold.
- Program 2 is the plan-free static one-wave program.

Before this PR, launches below the grid ran program 0 only if they had
at least 8 query rows per request and `num_kv_heads * (batch_size + 10)`
was greater than the SM count. Other launches below the grid ran program
1 unless they used the static one-wave program. This PR lowers the
minimum from 8 query rows per request to 4, so launches with 4 to 7
query rows per request in that range now run program 0 instead of
program 1. No request can be split in that range, so the fold never
runs. Every other launch keeps its program. The baseline is the previous
Cake version of the kernel, which is the version on FlashInfer main and
runs program 1 here. The trtllm-gen route (`route="static"`),
FlashInfer's non-Cake implementation of this operation, is shown for
reference. On the measured shape, this PR is 1.0184x to 1.0212x faster
than the baseline and about 4.3x to 4.4x faster than trtllm-gen.

| GPU | Mode | trtllm-gen (µs) | Previous Cake (µs) | This PR (µs) |
Speedup vs previous Cake | Speedup vs trtllm-gen |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs) | Eager | 864.57 | 204.89 | 201.01 |
1.0193x | 4.3011x |
| NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs) | CUDA-graph replay | 864.62 | 204.82 |
201.12 | 1.0184x | 4.2990x |
| NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs) | Eager | 840.26 | 194.50 | 190.75 |
1.0197x | 4.4050x |
| NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs) | CUDA-graph replay | 840.32 | 194.91
| 190.87 | 1.0212x | 4.4026x |

*Shape: 16 requests with 4 query tokens each (speculative decode), 8 KV
heads with 8 query heads per KV head, head_dim 128 and page size 64. The
context-parallel world size is 4 and the measured shard is rank 0.
Context lengths are long and ragged, taken from an agentic trace. This
is the only shape in the benchmark list whose program changes. All other
shapes keep their program. Software: CUDA 13.0 runtime with PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130, and kernels JIT-compiled with nvcc 13.4. Each value is
kernel time from FlashInfer `bench_gpu_time` (CUPTI) with FlashInfer's
L2 flush (cold L2). Each value is the median over 6 independent starts
(fresh processes) of the per-start median of 10 rounds. Speedup =
previous Cake / this PR and trtllm-gen / this PR.*

This module also ships the BF16 head_dim-128 and E4M3 head_dim-256
balanced DCP families from Cake, and these programs ship on sm_100a and
sm_103a.

### [11aa762](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/11aa7628bfa599fa4e929cb107cc11131b0f98fa)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T10:26:27Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kimi_k3_attn_res): L2 first-chunk prefetch programs for three B200, eleven B300 and eleven GB300 shapes (#8791)

This PR changes routes of the Cake AttnRes operator,
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_kimi_k3_attn_res`, which is exposed as
`flashinfer.kimi_k3_attn_res.prepare_kimi_k3_attn_res` and
`kimi_k3_attn_res`. One launch does residual add, an optional snapshot
write, K+1 candidate scoring, softmax, mix and output RMSNorm. It takes
BF16 inputs with hidden size 7168 and K in [0, 8]. It has one data type,
one layout and two fused forms: dense and snapshot write. This PR
changes routes on B200, B300 and GB300, at both PDL modes. Among the
measured shapes, 3 change on B200, 11 on B300 and 11 on GB300. This PR
adds one build option. It is off by default and ships only in programs
that a route uses.

- **New first-chunk L2 prefetch row cap (B300, GB300):** Each of these
shapes moves to a build of its previous program with a first-chunk L2
prefetch row cap that this PR adds. The cap is the suffix `r<R>` after
the existing `_fpl` / `_fpw` options (#8676). With `_fplr<R>`, the
lane-issued first-chunk L2 prefetch covers only the first R rows of the
first chunk instead of all K+2 rows. `_fpwr<R>` does the same for the
warp-issued prefetch. This PR uses R=2 and R=3.
- On B300 (sm_103a, 148 SMs): serving_m256_k7 moves from
`persistent:k7_nc4_d2_f111000000000000_fm` to
`persistent:k7_nc4_d2_f111000000000000_fm_fplr3`.

`persistent:k4_nc3_d2_f111000000000000_fm_rcp` to
`persistent:k4_nc3_d2_f111000000000000_fm_rcp_fplr3`.
