### [8e50827](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/8e508274877835f5d31b91a28d0268bfc75d644e)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T10:09:27Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_gdn_det_kcp): count the full-mode forward tapes without a saved set in the workspace query (#8783)

`gdn_det_workspace_bytes_kcp` / `gdn_det_workspace_layout_kcp`
under-counted the caller-held workspace of a `save_mode="full"` forward
that keeps no saved set (`save_for_backward=False`, or any forward under
`boundary_mode="replay"`). Such a forward binds its tapes in the
workspace arena, as the light split forward does, but the query left
them out whenever `save_mode="full"`. The query now leaves them out only
when the forward keeps a saved set. Only the byte query changes:
kernels, launches and outputs are unchanged, so there is no timing
change. The README's output-walk paragraph now also names the checkpoint
recompute that skips the output program under `recompute_output="auto"`.
This follows up on the review of #8755.

Cake also ships these separately: a non-deterministic variant of this
kernel, single-GPU GDN training packages without context parallelism
(deterministic and non-deterministic), GDN inference kernels for chunked
prefill and decode, and the KDA deterministic context-parallel training
sibling, which covers the per-channel-gate form; this kernel ships on
sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

### [85626c0](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/85626c0d7aa63453c67bd83e076d6d9c6954dfe3)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T10:08:00Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_fmha): plan small-M splits on the launch stream's partition by default, capture-safe (#8641); count profiled launches between sentinels (#8472) (#8789)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

This PR fixes two sets of failures:

- **#8641:** the small-M `cake_fmha` decode hangs on a green-context
stream. This PR also fixes a latent CUDA graph capture bug in the same
partition query.
- **#8472:** three profiler-based launch-count tests fail on GB300
because CUPTI loses their records.

### #8641: small-M decode hangs on a green-context stream

**What breaks**

- On main `267888284c` (GB300, CI image `flashinfer-ci-cu129` = torch
2.13.0+cu129),
`tests/attention/test_cake_fmha_decode_programs.py::test_cake_decode_smallm_in_an_sm_partition_completes[torch_before_import]`
times out (2:00 watchdog) in 2/2 runs.
- Full file on main: 1 failed / 336 passed / 6 skipped.

**Background**

- The BF16 head-dim-256 small-M decode splits each tile's KV over one
resident wave of CTAs. These CTAs wait for each other.
- #8387 made the split count follow the launch stream's SM partition
(green context).
- This happens only after FlashInfer observes a green context:
FlashInfer's own green-context helpers or its wrappers of
`torch.cuda.green_contexts.GreenContext` methods turn the plan on, or
the user sets `FLASHINFER_CAKE_FMHA_SM_PARTITIONS=1`.
- Until then, a launch plans on the whole device.

**Root cause**

- In torch 2.13, `GreenContext.create` returns the C++ base class. So
the Python wrappers never see the green context or its `Stream()`.
- The gate stays off. A 32-SM partition gets the device's 65-/152-way
plan. Its CTAs never all become resident, so the launch never completes.
- Two more cases cannot be observed at all:
- a green context whose stream was taken before FlashInfer was imported;
  - a green context made with the CUDA driver API (or another library).

**Second, latent bug (#8420)**

- The per-stream cache keys streams by `cuStreamGetId`.
- On a stream that is being captured into a CUDA graph, `cuStreamGetId`
returns `CUDA_ERROR_STREAM_CAPTURE_UNSUPPORTED` and invalidates the
capture. This happens with driver 580.159.03, in both global and relaxed
capture modes. It was measured on GB300.
- `cuStreamGetCtx`, `cuCtxGetCurrent`, `cuCtxGetId` and
`cuCtxGetDevResource` are legal during a capture.
- Once the gate is on, a small-M decode captured into a CUDA graph fails
with "operation failed due to a previous error during capture". With the
gate on by default, this caused 2 failures of
`test_cake_decode_smallm_program_is_sync_free_and_replays`.

**Fix: partition-aware plan on by default**

- FlashInfer cannot reliably observe a green context. So the
partition-aware plan is now on by default.
- The torch green-context method wrappers are removed.
- A launch reads its stream only if the small-M route can take it. The
read happens after the route's structural checks.
- A launch with more tiles than the device's SMs reads no stream.
- Opt-out: `FLASHINFER_CAKE_FMHA_SM_PARTITIONS=0` or
`enable_cake_fmha_sm_partitions(False)`. Use it only in a process that
never launches the small-M route on a partition.

**Fix: new host library `csrc/cake_fmha_stream_context.cpp`**

- Each small-M launch makes one FFI call into this library. The call
reads the SM count of the stream's CUDA context.
- The library has no device code. It is JIT-built with the host compiler
on first use (about 3 s) and links with `-lcuda`.
- If it cannot be built or loaded, the module warns once and plans on
the device's SM count. That is main's behaviour.
- The legacy and per-thread default streams read the thread's current
context (`cuCtxGetCurrent`). When a green context is current, as
`torch.cuda.green_contexts` makes it, these streams run on its
partition.
- Any other stream reads its own context (`cuStreamGetCtx`).
- The device's primary context is retained once and recognised by its
handle. A launch on any primary-context stream costs one driver call.
- For any other context (a green context), the SM count is cached per
`cuCtxGetId`. Context IDs are never reused, unlike handles.
- Newer driver entry points are resolved with `cuGetProcAddress`, and
only when the driver has them.
- The library does not call `cuStreamGetId`.
- Before CUDA 13 (R570/R575 drivers), `cuStreamGetCtx` returns
`CUDA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED` for a stream made by
`cuGreenCtxStreamCreate`.
- Main then fell back to the thread's current context, which is the
primary one. So it planned on the whole device again.
- Now the library reads the stream's green context with
`cuStreamGetCtx_v2` and `cuCtxFromGreenCtx`.
- Only a stream with no green context falls back to the current context.

**Scope**

- Only the small-M route changes. Other decode routes keep the device SM
count.
- On the whole device, the selected routes and outputs are unchanged.
- The `CLAUDE.md` env-var table row and a comment in
`flashinfer/green_ctx.py` now describe the new default.

### #8472: profiler-based launch-count tests fail on GB300

**What breaks**

On main (GB300, cu129 image), these tests fail in 40/40 runs:

| File | Test | Assertion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tests/norm/test_cake_rmsnorm_train_api.py` |
`test_a_single_kernel_window_launches_exactly_one_kernel` | `assert 0 ==
1` |
| `tests/msa_ops/test_blackwell_msa_sm100.py` |
`test_uniform_fp8_two_split_eager_calls_are_one_kernel_on_one_counter` |
`0 == 200` |
| `tests/msa_ops/test_blackwell_msa_sm100.py` |
`test_union_decode_eager_calls_without_a_workspace_are_one_kernel` | `0
== 40` |

On GB200 (same image), the msa pair fails intermittently (25/40 runs on
main).

**Root cause**

- On GB300, CUPTI 12.9 in the cu129 image does not initialise:
`cbapi.getCuptiStatus() failed with error CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_DEVICE
(2)`.
- As a result, `torch.profiler` returns 0 CUDA records in 18/18
sessions.
- On the same node, the cu130 (CUPTI 13.0.1) and cu134 (CUPTI 13.4.0)
images return every record.
- On GB200, the cu129 image drops records intermittently:
- In some long single-process file runs, both msa tests lost their
sentinels in 4/4 sessions. Those sessions kept 169 and 9 records instead
of 203 and 43.
  - Single-test runs passed 20/20.
- The tests counted raw profiler events. So a lost record looked like a
wrong launch count.

**Fix**

- The three tests now count launches with the existing
`tests.test_helpers.cake_profiler.cuda_kernel_names(..., exclude=())`
helper (from #7522).
- The helper brackets the window with sentinel kernels and retries a
session that lost them.
- It skips with a `CUPTI-LOST-RECORDS` reason only when no session keeps
the sentinels.
- `exclude=()` keeps every CUDA activity, including memsets and copies.
So "exactly one kernel" keeps its meaning.
- All count, output-reference, bitwise and counter-reset assertions are
unchanged.
- If every session lost its records, the test still runs its
profiler-independent checks before it skips the count: outputs vs
reference, bitwise, counters, carriers, workspace at rest. A lost
profiler never hides a wrong result.

### Test changes

`tests/attention/test_cake_fmha_decode_programs.py` (#8641):

- The partition test now also runs `torch_stream_before_import` and
`driver` (a driver-API green context with no setting).
- Every row is also captured into a CUDA graph on the partition stream
and replayed. The replay must match the eager output bitwise.
- New variant `driver_without_stream_context`: `cuStreamGetCtx` fails
for the driver-API green stream, as before CUDA 13. The launch must
still plan on the partition and complete, and the capture must replay
bitwise.
- The partition test used to skip on any device whose SM count is not
the pinned one (GB200's 152-SM sm_100a). Its plan does not depend on the
device SM count. It now runs on every device with room for a 64-SM
partition.
- Host-only tests (with a fake library):
- the launch plans on the partition when the partition is smaller than
the device, else on the device;
  - an unknown answer plans on the device;
- each launch asks once, with its stream's raw handle and device index;
  - a launch with more tiles than SMs reads no stream;
  - a library that fails to load warns once and plans on the device.
- A GPU test of the library itself:
- the default, legacy, per-thread and torch streams read the device's SM
count;
- a driver-API green context's stream reads its partition, also through
the entry that skips `cuStreamGetCtx`;
- with that green context pushed as the current context, the default
streams read the partition. After it is popped, they read the device
again.

`tests/norm/test_cake_rmsnorm_train_api.py` and
`tests/msa_ops/test_blackwell_msa_sm100.py` (#8472): the three
launch-count tests now count launches between sentinels, as described
above.

| GB300 / cu134 | rmsnorm "exactly one kernel" test x10; the two msa
launch-count tests x10 | all passed |
| GB300 / cu129 | same, x10 | the launch count is skipped
(`CUPTI-LOST-RECORDS`) in every run, after the profiler-independent
checks passed: CUPTI 12.9 does not initialise on GB300 |
| GB300 / cu129 | `tests/norm/test_cake_rmsnorm_train_api.py
tests/msa_ops/test_blackwell_msa_sm100.py`, 2 runs | 114 passed / 6
skipped, both runs (3 of the skips are `CUPTI-LOST-RECORDS`) |
| GB300 / cu134 | same | 117 passed / 3 skipped, both runs |

Most skips are not caused by CUPTI:

- The pinned sm_100a small-M programs are planned for 148 SMs. So 62
small-M GPU tests skip on the 152-SM GB200 ("sm100a with 152 SMs plans
other split counts"). They run on GB300.
- The NVFP4 decode tests need CUDA 13.4 (5 skips with the cu129 image).

Suggested CI test targets (optional; paths under `tests/`,
whitespace-separated — a starting point for `@flashinfer-bot run
<targets>` / `/bot run <targets>`, reviewers may adjust):
`tests/attention/test_cake_fmha_decode_programs.py
tests/norm/test_cake_rmsnorm_train_api.py
tests/msa_ops/test_blackwell_msa_sm100.py`

## 📊 Performance

This measures the host time of the partition query on GB200 (Grace
host), driver 580.126.20, cu129 image, whole device.

Method: one process alternates the setting on and off (ABBA order) over
32 rounds of 50 real small-M decode calls per row. The table gives the
median of the paired (on - off) differences, from three processes on the
default stream and two on a torch side stream. Timing is paired within
one process because cross-process timing on this host varied by 4-8%
between two runs of identical code.

| Row (BF16, head dim 256, 8 query heads per KV head, page 64) | Host
time, setting off (median, us) | Added by this PR, default stream (us, 3
processes) | Added, side stream (us, 2 processes) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `smallm_kv8200_q8_p64` | 63.2-67.5 | 2.69, 2.52, 2.23 | 2.21, 2.31 |
| `smallm_kv60008_q8_p64` | 62.7-67.4 | 3.34, 3.15, 2.33 | 3.40, 2.46 |
| `smallm_kv1032_q8_p64` | 60.5-66.3 | 2.78, 2.39, 2.56 | 2.22, 2.52 |

- The query adds about 2.2-3.4 us (about 4%) per eager small-M launch.
- It is host time only. On the whole device, the selected routes,
programs and outputs are unchanged.
- A launch replayed from a CUDA graph makes no query.
- The same queries through the Python driver bindings cost 5.3-6.6 us
(measured the same way). That is why they moved into the C++ library.
- `FLASHINFER_CAKE_FMHA_SM_PARTITIONS=0` removes the query for a process
that never launches on a partition.

## Reviewer Notes

- **Default change.** The partition-aware plan is now on by default.
- Each eager small-M launch pays about 2.2-3.4 us (about 4%) of host
time.
- Graph replay pays nothing, and launches with more tiles than SMs read
no stream.
  - The first use JIT-builds the host library (about 3 s).
- Opt out with `FLASHINFER_CAKE_FMHA_SM_PARTITIONS=0` or
`enable_cake_fmha_sm_partitions(False)`.
- **Why C++ instead of Python driver bindings.** The bindings cost
5.3-6.6 us of host time per real small-M launch on GB200. That was
paired within one process against the setting turned off. It is about 9%
of the launch's ~62 us host time. Most of that cost was the bindings
call and the Python glue around it, not the driver itself.
- **Pre-CUDA-13 fallback (`cuStreamGetCtx_v2` + `cuCtxFromGreenCtx`).**
No R570/R575 node was available. The fallback was verified through a
test-only library entry that skips `cuStreamGetCtx`. The test used a
real green-context stream on driver 580.
- **#8472 skips.** When CUPTI loses every record, the tests first run
their profiler-independent checks: outputs vs reference, bitwise,
counters, carriers, workspace at rest. Only the count is skipped, with a
`CUPTI-LOST-RECORDS` reason.
- **Files touched:**
  - `csrc/cake_fmha_stream_context.cpp`
  - `flashinfer/cake_fmha.py`
  - `flashinfer/jit/cake_fmha.py`
  - `flashinfer/green_ctx.py`
  - `CLAUDE.md`
  - `tests/attention/test_cake_fmha_decode_programs.py`
  - `tests/msa_ops/test_blackwell_msa_sm100.py`
  - `tests/norm/test_cake_rmsnorm_train_api.py`

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Small-M decode planning now adapts to the launch stream’s available
GPU resources by default, improving partition-aware execution.
* You can disable this behavior with
`FLASHINFER_CAKE_FMHA_SM_PARTITIONS=0` or control it through a Python
API.
* When stream-specific information is unavailable, planning falls back
to the device’s SM count.
* **Bug Fixes**
* Improved handling of CUDA streams and contexts when selecting Small-M
decode plans.

### [a1a1540](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/a1a154096d11fd046a823639b719c9e1db39aacf)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T10:02:25Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate): with grad, FP32 two-sum fold on SM103 from 700 rows per SM (#8785)

This PR speeds up the backward of the non-deterministic package of
Cake's SiLU-gated RMSNorm training kernel
(`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train` with `deterministic=False`)
on GB300 (sm_103a). It applies to both weight-gradient outputs, BF16 dw
and FP32 dw. Inputs from 700 up to 12000 rows per SM now run a new bulk
long backward. That backward folds its per-run dw partial sums with a
guarded FP32 two-sum pair instead of in FP64, and it uses FP64 only for
the final column sum. Before this PR, on sm_103a the long backward (FP64
fold) served from 1280 rows per SM and the base backward below that
(inputs of at most 256 rows run the short backward, as before). From
12000 rows per SM the long backward still runs, as before. Below 700
rows per SM nothing changes. The forward, every sm_100a and sm_107a
route, and the deterministic package run the same code as before.

The kernel has two Cake variants: the deterministic package
`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train` (the same API with
`deterministic=True`) and this non-deterministic package, which has a
BF16 and an FP32 weight-gradient output. Both packages ship on sm_100a,
sm_103a and sm_107a. This PR changes only the non-deterministic backward
on sm_103a.

A speedup is baseline us / new us, so a value above 1 means this PR is
faster. The previous Cake version is this package on FlashInfer main
before this PR. Summary on GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs, CUDA 13.4), as
ranges over the 14 shapes of Table 1 and as A/B medians over every
instance in the route:

| comparison | backward (BF16 dw) | checkpointed step (BF16 dw) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| det Cake / new (Table 1) | 1.142-1.268 | 1.083-1.176 |
| strongest non-Cake / new (Table 1) | 1.110-1.228 | 1.028-1.134 |
| previous Cake / new (Table 1, A/B) | 1.014-1.103 | 1.005-1.045 |
| previous / new, A/B median, [700, 3200) rows/SM | 1.060 (BF16 dw),
1.061 (FP32 dw); n 37 | 1.027 (BF16 dw and FP32 dw); n 37 |
| previous / new, A/B median, [3200, 12000) rows/SM | 1.022 (BF16 dw and
FP32 dw); n 18 | 1.010 (BF16 dw and FP32 dw); n 18 |

All 110 in-route backward instances of the A/B are GAIN, for both BF16
dw and FP32 dw (Table 2).

The strongest non-Cake kernel beats new in 4 cells. All are forward
cells, which this PR does not change. In each, the winner is
torch.compile default (best of 5):

- 2285x48 fwd 0.911 (16.640 vs 18.272 us; new slower by 9.8 %)
- 2285x48 fwdg 0.905 (16.672 vs 18.432 us; new slower by 10.6 %)
- 3045x48 fwd 0.921 (21.888 vs 23.776 us; new slower by 8.6 %)
- 3045x48 fwdg 0.897 (21.408 vs 23.872 us; new slower by 11.5 %)

In every backward and checkpointed-step row, new is faster than both the
deterministic Cake kernel and the strongest non-Cake kernel. "Cells
below 1x" lists each cell below 1.

## How the tables were measured

- Inputs are BF16 x / z / dy with head dimension 128. dw is BF16 unless
an op says FP32 dw. All times are in us.
- Table 1 and the forward table: the det, strongest non-Cake and new
columns are CUPTI kernel time with a cold L2. Each value is the median
of 10 round medians.
- Previous vs new comes from interleaved A/Bs on the same GPU.
- Backward (Table 2 and the bwdg rows of Table 1): both versions in the
same process, rotating buffers, CUDA-graph replay, medians over 8 valid
processes on 2 nodes. GAIN / NEUTRAL / LOSS is the A/B's verdict per
instance.
- Full step (Table 3 and the ckptg rows of Table 1): one process per
version, run in 16 sequences per shape in counterbalanced orders on the
same GPU. Its values are medians over those 16 sequences, and its det
values come from the previous version's processes. Table 3 is reported
without a per-instance verdict.
- Table 1 shows each A/B's previous value next to that A/B's own new
value.
- Strongest non-Cake kernel per row: the fastest of FLA 0.6.0
`rms_norm_gated`, mamba_ssm v2.3.2 `rmsnorm_fn` (gated), torch.compile
default and max-autotune-no-cudagraphs (best of 5 compiles each), and,
on the forward rows, inductor's Triton kernel with a pinned config. The
first four were measured on every row and the inductor kernel on every
forward row. The non-Cake column uses these labels:
  - `FLA`: fla 0.6.0 `rms_norm_gated`.
  - `tc-max`: torch.compile max-autotune-no-cudagraphs, best of 5.
  - `tc-def`: torch.compile default, best of 5.
- Stages:
  - `fwd`: one eager forward call.
  - `fwdg`: the forward replayed from a CUDA graph.
  - `bwdg`: the backward replayed from a CUDA graph.
- `ckptg`: the checkpointed step (2 x forward + backward) in one CUDA
graph.

## Cells below 1x

- Against the strongest non-Cake kernel: the 4 forward cells listed
above.
- Against the deterministic Cake kernel: 4 forward cells, all of them
unchanged code. These are 2285x48 fwd 0.993 (18.144 vs 18.272 us),
2285x48 fwdg 0.993 (18.304 vs 18.432 us), 3045x48 fwd 0.996 (23.680 vs
23.776 us) and 3045x48 fwdg 0.996 (23.776 vs 23.872 us).
- Previous / new at the instances this PR routes (Tables 1, 2 and 3):
none.
- Previous / new at the control instances of Table 2: 4 cells. These
controls force the new backward below 700 rows per SM, where this PR
does not route it:
- BF16 dw: 2462x32 0.979 (23.376 / 23.872 us) and 91257x1 0.972 (26.404
/ 27.172 us).
- FP32 dw: 2462x32 0.980 (23.364 / 23.848 us) and 91257x1 0.972 (26.418
/ 27.172 us).

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Performance**
* Added an intermediate backward path for SM103 GPUs, covering workloads
from 700 to 12,000 rows per SM before routing to the long-workload path.
  * Adjusted backward routing thresholds for SM100 and SM103.

* **Accuracy and behavior**
* SM103’s intermediate backward path uses FP32 two-sum accumulation.
Results may be non-finite if the accumulation exceeds FP32’s range; the
deterministic backward can return finite results in such cases.
  * At 12,000 rows per SM, the existing FP64-fold path applies.

* **Validation**
* Expanded coverage of routing thresholds and deterministic-output
parity for SM103.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

### [e0ba270](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/e0ba270a8d504d52015cf138ace4e73d94515924)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T09:46:58Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_deepgemm): route two SM120 batch-128 64K-context decode steps to faster programs (RTX PRO 6000 h64 p64 n4, h64 p64 n3) (#8786)

The SM120 paged FP8 MQA logits kernel picks its program from a route
catalog. Each heads/page/next_n configuration has a default route, and
device routes pick a tuned variant for each shape. FlashInfer main
(beeb23bc) already ships the previous version of this kernel. This PR
moves two RTX PRO 6000 shapes at batch 128 and context 65536 from their
default route to tuned programs:

- h64/p64/next_n 4 moves to the existing route
`sm120:fp8:h64:p64:n4:a4:mpf_bta_ha_k2q_ef`. Batches 33 to 127 keep the
default route.
- h64/p64/next_n 3 moves to a new route,
`sm120:fp8:h64:p64:n3:a3:mpf_bta_ha_k2q_ef`, which adds one program.

On these two shapes, the geomean speedup over FlashInfer main is 1.030×
(seed 760) and 1.031× (seed 52021). RTX 5090 routes do not change. No
routes or programs are deleted, and every other shape keeps its current
route.

NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (188 SMs, sm_120a), driver
595.84.01, CUDA 13.4.92 toolchain (CUDA 13.0 runtime, PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130). Baseline: FlashInfer main (beeb23bc). Latency: median µs
of the paged FP8 MQA logits call (CUPTI, L2 flushed before each launch,
5 interleaved baseline/new groups). Each seed (760, 52021) runs on its
own GPU. Speedup = baseline µs / new µs. The table covers all 216
shapes. The 2 changed shapes have a geomean speedup of 1.030× (seed 760)
and 1.031× (seed 52021). On unchanged shapes both sides run the same
program.

- **提交信息**: perf(cake_moe_grouped_gemm): use the L2 evict-first 512-wide dgrad tile on sm_100a (#8773)

The Cake MoE grouped BF16 GEMM has deterministic and non-deterministic
variants. This PR changes one program of the non-deterministic variant:
the sm_100a data gradient (`dX = G W`) now takes the L2 evict-first
build of its existing 512-wide tile. The existing host rule, which
sm_107a already uses, selects it when groups average at least 16384 rows
and K >= 4096. In the table below, that is the six gate_up E4 rows and
gate_up E8 balanced. dX stays bitwise equal to the deterministic dX, and
nothing else changes. On the selected rows, dgrad is 1.8-2.4 % faster
than the previous version (1.0197-1.0242x vs deterministic Cake,
1.0392-1.0460x vs non-Cake SOTA). The full-backward gain over the
previous version is small (+0.6-1.2 %) and depends on the GPU. The full
backward is still 0.5-0.6 % slower than the composed cuDNN backward on
E4 m136064 skewed and one_empty, but the gap is smaller than before
(0.9939 / 0.9948, was 0.9848 / 0.9888). The checkpointed step is faster
than every non-Cake arm on every row. The gain is an energy effect:
fewer DRAM reads allow a higher sustained clock, and in cold-cache
single launches the backward gain is within noise.

NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a, 148 SM), driver 580.82.07; torch 2.14.1+cu130
(CUDA 13.0 runtime, bundled cuBLAS); kernels built with CUDA 13.4; cuDNN
9.24.0; Transformer Engine 2.20.2. Sustained mode, 2 nodes x 2 GPUs, all
arms in one run. Speedup = baseline latency / new latency (> 1 = new
faster), reported as the pooled median of paired per-group log ratios
[95 % bootstrap CI]. Ratios are paired medians while ms are pooled
medians, so quotients of the shown ms can differ from the ratio by up to
0.66 pp. Non-Cake SOTA is the fastest of cuDNN grouped GEMM (cudnn),
serial cuBLAS per group (cbl) and TE grouped GEMM (teNN), and cmp_X is
library X's forward and dgrad plus the TE NT wgrad accumulating into
fp32 main_grad. The last column gives the previous non-deterministic
Cake latency in parentheses. Forward is unchanged.

### [e517055](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/e517055fdcb5e9d92509b83299a2b0e40ec1e1d3)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T09:01:28Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): restore the SIMT and head/tail router windows on 152-SM and 212-SM parts (#8730)

Cake's dense projection GEMM ships as two packages: the deterministic
`flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_det_gemm` and the
non-deterministic `flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm`. The
non-deterministic package holds two GEMMs, K1 (BF16 or FP32 output) and
an FP32 router GEMM. Each has forward, weight-gradient (wgrad) and
input-gradient (dgrad) programs. The family ships for sm_100a, sm_103a
and sm_107a. #8707 added compensated (Kahan / Dot2) router programs for
148-SM B200 and B300 parts. This PR restores plain FFMA SIMT router
programs (FP32, E = 256 experts, H = 4096, 5120 and 6144) on the
`deterministic=False` path. They cover 152-SM GB200 (sm_100a), 152-SM
GB300 (sm_103a) and 212-SM R200 (sm_107a) in few-token windows: wgrad up
to T = 192–288 and dgrad up to T = 64 or 128, depending on GPU and H.
The PR also restores large-T head/tail wgrad windows on GB200 (H = 5120,
T = 10240–16384) and GB300 (T = 16172–49152, with bounds that depend on
H). The new programs stay inside the router accuracy budget (rel_fro ≤
2e-6 vs FP64). The forward route is unchanged from main. So is the
router route outside these windows, except that main's `waves` wgrad
route at H = 5120, where it applies on sm_103a parts with SM counts
other than 148 and 152, now runs up to T = 192 (main: 160).

Inside these windows the new programs are never slower than
deterministic Cake. They run at 1.00–5.79x over all 165 rows; the two
1.00x rows are GB300 bwd and 2fwd+bwd at H = 4096, T = 49152. The
largest gains are for wgrad at T = 1 (4.94–5.79x). Non-Cake SOTA is, for
each cell, the fastest of five library arms that meets the router
accuracy budget. The five arms are cublasSgemm, cuBLASLt FP32, torch.mm
with TF32 off, cuBLAS BF16x9 FP32 emulation and a per-GEMM mix. Against
SOTA the result is mixed. The new programs are faster in 71 rows, equal
in 4 and slower in 87, and 32 rows fall inside the A/A noise band (1 ±
the largest A/A deviation from 1 given in the caption for that GPU and T
range). The 3 GB300 rows at H = 6144, T = 20480 have no SOTA value
because no library arm met the budget in every run. At T = 1, wgrad,
dgrad and bwd lose (0.62–0.94x). For T = 17–288 they run at 0.88–1.71x.
In the 18 large-T head/tail rows that have a SOTA value, every op wins
at 1.30–1.63x, including the checkpointed step. In each of those rows
the fastest library arm is BF16x9 emulation or the per-GEMM mix. In the
few-token windows the checkpointed step loses (0.25–0.99x vs SOTA,
1.02–1.32x vs deterministic Cake) because its two forward calls still
run the deterministic program.

At T ≥ 10240 the gain over deterministic Cake is small: 1.05–1.25x for
wgrad, 1.00–1.11x for bwd and 1.00–1.06x for 2fwd+bwd. Ten of these 21
rows fall inside the A/A noise band, as do four 2fwd+bwd rows at the top
of the few-token windows. Read them as parity or a small gain.

Deterministic Cake is also current main's route on these rows, except on
GB200 and GB300 at H = 5120, T ≤ 128, where main runs its `waves` wgrad
route. Against `waves` the new programs are 1.57–2.12x for wgrad,
1.29–1.82x for bwd and 1.07–1.14x for 2fwd+bwd.

*Min and max speedup over the 165 rows of the per-shape table below
(FP32 router, E = 256, H = 4096 / 5120 / 6144, T inside the restored
windows, `deterministic=False`). GPUs: GB200 (sm_100a, 152 SMs), GB300
(sm_103a, 152 SMs) and R200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs). CUDA 13.4 toolchain
(nvcc V13.4.92), torch 2.14.1+cu130; cuBLAS / cuBLASLt 13.1.1.3 on
GB200, 13.1.1.3 and 13.8.0 on GB300 (both measured; the faster counts),
13.8.0.4 on R200. Latency method: CUDA graph replay with L2 flushed
before every iteration (cold L2), measured as the CUPTI op span. Each
cell takes the median of paired groups per process, then the median over
runs: run A (all rows in one process) and run B (one process per row);
on GB300 each layout ran once per cuBLAS build. A/A noise: where the
deterministic, current-main and new arms of one run execute the same
kernel (the forward, and dgrad outside its window), their ratios to the
new arm (deterministic/new and current/new) span 0.986–1.021 at T ≤ 288
and 0.930–1.019 at T ≥ 10240 on GB200, 0.981–1.014 at T ≤ 288 and
0.957–1.000 at T ≥ 10240 on GB300, 0.930–1.011 at T ≤ 288 on R200; a
separate R200 run with both arms on the current main planner gave
per-run paired ratios of 0.896–1.163 over its 160 graph cells. Large-T
rows ran with the software power cap engaged on some samples. Speedup =
baseline latency / new latency (> 1 means the new program is faster).
Deterministic Cake = the deterministic package's program. Non-Cake SOTA
= for each cell, the fastest of five library arms: cublasSgemm, cuBLASLt
FP32 (top-8 heuristics), torch.mm with TF32 off, cuBLAS BF16x9 FP32
emulation, and a per-GEMM mix (each GEMM of the operation uses the
fastest of these libraries that meets the budget), measured in the same
runs. An arm counts only if it met the router accuracy budget for that
shape in every run (rel_fro ≤ 2e-6 vs FP64, finite, and the forward's
top-8 expert selection equal to FP64's), so every value in this column
met the budget. On GB300 at H = 6144, T = 20480 no library arm met the
budget in every run (in the one-process-per-row runs no library's
forward passed: sgemm, torch.mm and BF16x9 chose a different top-8 set
than FP64 on one sampled row, and no cuBLASLt algorithm passed), so its
3 rows show n/a and are left out of the SOTA min and max. bwd = dgrad +
wgrad. 2fwd+bwd = checkpointed step (2 x forward + dgrad + wgrad), where
the forward is the deterministic program in every Cake arm. Where T is
outside the dgrad window, bwd and 2fwd+bwd use the unchanged dgrad
route.*

### [efbdc89](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/efbdc89c69d0374c7b36bb81fee443d3374fe72b)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T08:50:13Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda): one-helper owner/helper hybrid build for equal-length 37-48-task launches in BF16 KDA prefill (sm_100a) (#8764)

The Cake chunked KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) prefill behind
`flashinfer.recurrent_kda(..., backend="cake")` has modules with BF16
inputs and modules with TF32 inputs. Both come in fused and split forms.
This PR changes only the prepared BF16-input path with FP32 state
(`flashinfer.prepare_bf16_kda_prefill`), and only on sm_100a (B200). On
sm_100a, the owner/helper route of the value-split M64 module, where two
value-half owner CTAs per task prepare all chunks (pair share), gains a
hybrid build. One helper CTA per task prepares half of each task's
chunks (chunk c with c % 8 >= 4) and stores them to its packet ring. The
two owners prepare the other chunks and copy the helper's chunks from
the ring. The build launches cooperatively on a (tasks, 3) grid. It is
taken only for equal-length launches of 37 to 48 tasks at 2048 tokens or
more that the pair-share rule already takes. Every other launch keeps
its program, and a refused cooperative launch falls back to the
pair-share program. Outputs are bit-identical to the pair-share and
routed programs, and there are no register spills. The tables compare
this PR with the previous Cake version on FlashInfer main, which already
includes the short-task turnover change, on B200 only. They report the
median latency per call in microseconds, with a cold L2. Each table has
56 rows: 12 or 16 heads, no gate lower bound or -5, and 14
sequence-length shapes. One table covers the fast path and the other
covers the serving pattern. TIE means no difference beyond the
measurement band. One row is faster in each table: 12 heads, gate lower
bound -5, shape 4x4096. Its latency goes from 195.92 to 177.18 us
(1.11x) on the fast path and from 197.95 to 179.01 us (1.11x) in the
serving pattern. On a second B200, the same row went from 192.13 to
179.97 us and from 192.86 to 180.67 us (both 1.07x). The other 55 rows
are TIE, and none is slower. We also swept the 152 launch shapes outside
the tables that take the new build (equal-length batches of 36 to 48
sequences of 2049 to 14000 tokens, 12 and 16 heads, layer and wrapper
calls). On B200 all 152 are faster (latency ratio this PR / main 0.87 to
0.95), and none is slower. The family also ships the TF32-input modules
and the split forms, on both sm_100a and sm_103a (GB300). This PR does
not change those variants or any sm_103a program or route.

B200: NVIDIA B200, sm_100a, 148 SMs, driver 580.82.07. CUDA 13.4 (nvcc),
PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.

### [9cdebfc](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/9cdebfc5c7f654d1e87b9bbe1d94b381689fc294)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T08:39:37Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_dsv4): fall back from the SM107 K=64 program without oversized shared memory (#8777)

On SM107, FP8 H128 decode launches with 48 or more query rows on the
uniform persistent route run the K=64 program
`cake_dsv4_7074d4c5b808db91fcba`. This program needs CUDA 13.4's
oversized shared-memory mode. If the process has a CUDA 13.0 runtime
loaded, the launch fails with `cudaFuncSetAttribute failed: invalid
argument`. This PR adds a host-side runtime check and falls back to
programs that fit in standard shared memory when the K=64 program can't
launch.

## Problem

`cake_dsv4_7074d4c5b808db91fcba` uses 272512 B of dynamic shared memory,
which is above the 232448 B standard opt-in ceiling. Its binding
therefore sets the oversized mode (`cudaFuncAttributeSharedMemoryMode`)
through the CUDA runtime. The only guard is a compile-time `#if
CUDART_VERSION < 13040` / `#error` against the toolkit headers. The JIT
module links libcudart dynamically without rpath, so at run time it uses
whichever `libcudart.so.13` the process has already loaded, for example
from torch's `nvidia-cuda-runtime` wheel. With CUDA runtime 13.0 loaded
(the default runtime wheel of torch 2.14.1+cu130), the attribute call
fails even though the driver supports the mode.

## Fix

- Add a cached host predicate, `_k64_sibling_launchable(arch, device)`.
It returns true only when all three of these hold:
  - the CUDA toolkit is >= 13.4
- the process's loaded CUDA runtime is >= 13040, read with
`cudaRuntimeGetVersion` from the already-mapped `libcudart.so.<major>`
- the driver reports
`CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_OVERSIZED_SHARED_MEMORY_PER_BLOCK` (150) >=
272512 B. If the driver doesn't report the attribute, it is treated as
having no oversized mode.
- The predicate is evaluated once per `(arch, device)`, and only for
SM107 launches of >= 48 rows. `_k64_variant` now takes the query's
device.
- When the predicate is false:
- Launches below 128 rows run the route's own K=32 program (225280 B,
standard mode).
- Launches of >= 128 rows run the lane-issued program
`fp8_h128_prefill_source_persistent`, as before #8679. SM107 keeps these
short-query launches on the uniform route only for the K=64 program.
  - The grid and partials are the same.
- sm_100a and sm_103a are unaffected: they have no oversized program,
and the predicate returns true without probing.
- The change is host-only (`flashinfer/mla/cake_dsv4.py`,
`tests/cpu/mla/test_cake_dsv4.py`). No generated source changes.

## Testing

CPU: `tests/cpu/mla/test_cake_dsv4.py` passed (586 tests). The new tests
cover routing for launchable True/False × rows 8/47/48/127/128/160/1024
× PDL on/off, plus the predicate's inputs. pre-commit passed (ruff,
ruff-format, mypy, whitespace).

GPU: sm_107a R200-class GPU (212 SMs, driver 620.43 / CUDA 13.5 driver
API version 13050, CUDA 13.4 toolkit, torch 2.14.1), 36 launch cases
(rows 32-160, top-k 4x and 128x width):

| build | loaded CUDA runtime | gate | launches raising | outputs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main | 13.4.92 | n/a | 0 / 36 | reference |
| main | 13.0.96 | n/a | 32 / 36 (`cudaFuncSetAttribute failed: invalid
argument`) | n/a |
| this PR | 13.4.92 | true (K=64 program) | 0 / 36 | bitwise identical
to main, 36 / 36 |
| this PR | 13.0.96 | false (fallback programs) | 0 / 36 | bitwise
identical to main with 13.4.92, 36 / 36 |

### [8fb7dbf](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/8fb7dbf8521c3dc102a0fdce1bb6141b04a0ab20)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T08:28:28Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_kcp): opt-in light_akk save mode keeps Akk tape to skip the solve (#8754)

Cake ships four GDN training variants in FlashInfer. There is a
non-deterministic and a deterministic form, and each comes as a
single-rank package and a context-parallel (KCP) package. This PR
changes only the non-deterministic KCP package,
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_train_kcp`.

It adds an opt-in `save_mode="light_akk"`. The forward keeps one extra
BF16 tensor, the chunk-local A_kk matrix (Akk tape). The light backward
then runs a new solve-free replay program, `fwd_prep_replay_l2n`. Before
this, it re-ran the forward prep program with its triangular solve. The
mode requires `use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True`. The default stays
`save_mode="light"` and is unchanged. Under `torch.utils.checkpoint` the
forward saves as `"light"`. The deterministic route refuses
`"light_akk"`.

The extra tensor costs memory. Per GDN layer, the saved set grows from
3.031 to 4.533 GiB at shape A (+1.50 GiB). At shape M it grows from
0.379 to 0.569 GiB (+0.19 GiB). The forward peak grows by the same
amount. Checkpointed steps keep 3.000 GiB (A) and 0.375 GiB (M) in both
modes.

These are the forward + backward times at shape A under the sustained
protocol:
- B200: light 36.835 ms, deterministic Cake 38.740 ms, light_akk 35.399
ms.
- GB300: light 34.041 ms, deterministic Cake 35.923 ms, light_akk 32.457
ms.

Forward and checkpointed rows stay within 0.3 % of light (light /
light_akk 0.997-1.000); the checkpointed step saves as light.

Two baselines are faster than light_akk. FROST is faster than every Cake
arm at CP1 (SOTA/light_akk 0.34-0.83). FlashQLA is faster on B200 CP8
(0.959). In that B200 run, the software power cap was active in
11.8-25.4 % of samples for the Cake arms and 0 % for FlashQLA. The ratio
is reported as measured. On GB300 CP4, light_akk beats FlashQLA (1.021).

**Baselines:**
- light is this package on FlashInfer main at its default.
- Deterministic Cake is `cake_gdn_det_train_kcp` on the same main.
- At CP1, SOTA is the cuDNN frontend 1.32.1 GDN (FROST). The forward row
uses the fastest FROST forward (`checkpoint_every_n_tokens=0`). Forward
+ backward and the checkpointed step use `checkpoint_every_n_tokens=64`.
- At CP > 1, SOTA is FlashQLA 0.1.3 (tilelang 0.1.15) with its own dual
context parallelism. It is the strongest non-Cake option that applies
there.

Ratios are baseline ms / light_akk ms. Above 1 means light_akk is
faster.

**Shapes:**
- A: 4 sequences (98304, 65536, 57344, 40960) = 262,144 tokens.
- M: 5 sequences (12000, 9000, 6000, 3768, 2000) = 32,768 tokens.

Both shapes use H_qk 16, HV 48, head dim 128, BF16 q/k/v, FP32 g/beta,
contiguous layout, in-kernel q/k L2 norm, and no conv1d.

**Software:** torch 2.14.1+cu130, with the Cake units built with CUDA
13.4.

B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), CUDA 13.4, CP1, shapes A and M: times in ms for
forward, forward + backward and checkpointed forward + recompute +

Cake ships several output variants of the MiniMax-H3 fused pre-attention
kernel, and this PR changes the MXFP8 output variant on sm_103a. It adds
a new program, `FUSED_TILE_LANE`. This fused QKV GEMM's epilogue warps

changes the non-deterministic single-rank package,
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_gdn_train`. On sm_107a (R200), its
forward WY stage now runs the packed-triangular WY program at five CTAs
per SM (`wy_tc2`). It replaces the previous WY program (`wy_tc`) on that
architecture. PR #8665 already moved sm_100a (B200) and sm_103a (GB300)
to `wy_tc2`. The deterministic package
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_det_train` already runs it on sm_107a
(#8695). With this PR, the non-deterministic single-rank package runs
`wy_tc2` on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

Baselines in the tables:

- **Deterministic Cake**: the deterministic package at FlashInfer main
7a13d7ba. It is unchanged on this PR's base, main e7ec0e68.
- **Non-Cake SOTA**: the fastest qualified non-Cake implementation for
each operation. The candidates are FLA 0.6.0 (Triton) and the GDN from
cuDNN frontend (FROST) in two modes: states recomputed ("cuDNN FROST")
or states stored every 64 tokens ("cuDNN FROST (chunk 64)"). In these
tables it is cuDNN FROST for fwd and cuDNN FROST (chunk 64) for fwd+bwd
and ckpt. FLA 0.6.0 is slower on every row. FlashQLA has no sm_107a
build, so it is not a candidate.
- **Previous**: this package on main before this PR.

Every ratio is baseline ms / this PR ms, so a value above 1 means this
PR is faster. ckpt is the checkpointed step (forward, recompute and
backward).

Against the previous version, this PR is faster on 44 of 45 rows for
each beta dtype. The one exception is the 3 x ~4.25k real-pack ckpt row
(0.995x with FP32 beta, 0.997x with BF16 beta), which is within noise.
Against deterministic Cake, which runs the same WY program on sm_107a,
every row is faster or at parity, with ratios from 0.998x to 1.113x. The
ratio is above 1.000x on 32 of 45 FP32-beta rows and 36 of 45 BF16-beta
rows. Against the non-Cake SOTA, this PR is faster on every fwd+bwd and
ckpt row: 1.079x to 2.276x with FP32 beta and 1.063x to 2.248x with BF16
beta. It is slower than cuDNN FROST's forward on 12 of 15 fwd rows for
each beta dtype, down to 0.460x with FP32 beta and 0.442x with BF16
beta.

* Added support for running the `wy_tc2` implementation on SM107 GPUs.
It now uses the same chain and produces the same outputs as the existing
implementation on that architecture.
* **Bug Fixes**
* Updated SM107 shared-memory addressing for the `wy_tc2` execution
path.
* **Documentation**
* Updated the architecture support and implementation details for
`wy_tc2`.

### [367e4bc](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/367e4bc5c3679b5116db2e6bd914dd2e4e2d67ad)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T07:50:28Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_causal_conv1d_det): SM-wide row-group backward for 264 <= C < 512 on SM100 and SM103 (#8761)

FlashInfer's deterministic causal conv1d + SiLU training kernels have 8
variants. This PR changes only the default deterministic backward
variant (`bwd`). The baseline is FlashInfer main before this PR. On
B200, all 36 rows are faster: backward is 1.15x-1.32x faster, and
forward + backward is 1.12x-1.21x faster. On GB300, all 100 rows are
faster: backward is 1.02x-1.31x faster, and forward + backward is
1.03x-1.21x faster.

### [095edbb](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/095edbb93e9eb06cd0623567b3e6d7df9039c189)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T07:44:38Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kimi_k3_fp8_projection): SM103a MMA-warp TMEM allocation twin of the TMA-store GEMM for TP1 kv_b M 513..1024 (#8767)

`flashinfer.gemm.kimi_k3_fp8_projection` (experimental, backend
`"cake"`) computes the TP-local projection GEMMs of Kimi-K3. Cake ships
one data-type/layout variant of this kernel. It takes row-major BF16
activations quantized per token to E4M3 with 1x128 UE8M0 scales and E4M3
`[N, K]` weights with 128x128 UE8M0 block scales. It accumulates in FP32
and outputs BF16. This PR updates that variant. The baseline is the
previous Cake version, merged in #8690, which is current FlashInfer
main.

What changes:
- sm_103a (GB300) only: the 192-wide, 128-K TMA-store GEMM program gets
a twin in which the MMA warp allocates tensor memory. The load warp then
skips the allocation rendezvous and goes straight to the
programmatic-dependent-launch wait. The twin is used for M 513 to 1024
of the TP1 kv_b projection (N 24576, K 512). In the table that is one
shape, TP1 kv_b M = 1024. Grids are unchanged.
- sm_100a (B200): no change. Its programs and routes are identical to
main, so B200 was not re-measured and the table covers GB300 only.

On GB300, TP1 kv_b M = 1024 goes from 18.720 us to 18.480 us, a 1.012x
speedup. That is the median of 10 paired interleaved rounds, and the
per-round ratios span 1.0103-1.0139. The other 197 shapes run the same
programs as main. Their ratios are 0.995-1.002 (median 1.000), with 17
above and 29 below 1.000 at 3 decimals. The lowest is TP1 f_a M = 64
(0.995, per-round 0.9947-1.0000) and the highest is TP1 q_proj M = 16384
(1.002). Across all 198 shapes, ratios are 0.995-1.012 (median 1.000),
with 18 above and 29 below 1.000 at 3 decimals.

Other TP1 kv_b M values that use the new twin are not in the shape list.
They were measured on GB300 in a separate 16-round interleaved pass:

| M | main (us) | PR (us) | speedup |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 513 | 15.360 | 15.152 | 1.012 |
| 768 | 16.400 | 16.224 | 1.012 |
| 896 | 18.176 | 17.976 | 1.011 |
| 1023 | 18.496 | 18.328 | 1.010 |

Output is bit-identical to FlashInfer main on all 198 shapes on GB300
and B200, and on the extra M values above.

NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a), CUDA 13.4. `main (us)` and `PR (us)` are the
median per-call latency in microseconds for FlashInfer main and this PR.
`speedup` is the median of per-round paired ratios (FlashInfer main /
this PR) over 10 to 16 interleaved rounds on the same GPU, so it can
differ from the ratio of the two medians.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Added support for an additional FP8 projection workload on compatible
SM103a hardware.
* The workload now selects a matching computation path and produces
bfloat16 output. Existing routing for other tested workloads remains
unchanged.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

---------

Co-authored-by: Avery Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [97ce955](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/97ce95504d8b49854f0ad845432ab8af7c3f2241)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T07:43:42Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_det_kcp): fold the output program into the forward walks of the deterministic KCP package (#8755)

Cake's deterministic context-parallel GDN training kernel has one
data-type variant: BF16 q/k/v/out/dout with FP32 scalar log-decay g and
beta. The grouped Q/K head counts `(H_qk, HV)` are runtime parameters,
with production shape (16, 48). There are three partition layouts:
contiguous (C), whole-buffer zigzag (Z) and per-document zigzag + ragged
(D). This PR delivers the same variant. The change applies to the
light-save forward (`save_mode="light"`, `boundary_mode="saved"`, the
defaults). That forward used to run the state walk and then launch a
separate output program that re-read the per-chunk states. Now one fused
walk, `kcp_fwdh_out`, writes the output while it carries the state. It
runs at value-tile widths 128 and 64, and picks the 64-wide form by the
same width rule as the forward walk. Other save modes and the
checkpoint-replay path keep the split form. Outputs and gradients are
bitwise equal to the split form on every row below. The forward (B1) is
5–14 % faster, and the full step (B3) is up to 5 % faster.

main = the same build with the output program launched separately, which
matches main's launch list; new = this PR's shipped call; new/main < 1
is faster. ms = median of the slowest rank over interleaved main/new
visits; B1 = module forward with autograd recording; B3 = forward +
non-reentrant checkpoint replay + backward, including all communication
and copies; s1/s2 = two independent sessions. Packs (tokens /
documents): P1 241,817 / 6, P2 261,987 / 3, P3 259,174 / 2, P4 254,976 /
1 (one document spans the whole group), P5 249,856 / 4. Heads (16, 48);
causal conv1d width 4 over 10,240 channels. CP 2 and 4 run on one node;
CP 8 runs on two nodes of four GPUs. CUDA 13.4 toolkit, torch
2.14.1+cu130.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Added a fused forward path that computes outputs during the state walk
without allocating intermediate tapes in supported configurations. The
split path remains available, and fused execution can be disabled.
* Added workspace queries that account for saved tensors and fused or
split forward execution.
* **Documentation**
* Documented fused-path selection, workspace requirements, and
forward-mode behavior.
* **Tests**
* Added coverage comparing fused and split paths, including outputs,
gradients, and workspace lifetimes.

### [c4bbce7](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c4bbce78d717a9ba75b7ebbd92f15703727f8c0b)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T07:36:39Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_det_gemm): plan the 4096 -> 12288 input gradient with the row-half-release program at T-exact keys (#8765)

This PR changes the Cake `dense_projection_det_gemm` package in
`flashinfer.experimental`, the deterministic dense projection GEMM. Most
programs in the package are BF16-operand GEMMs (forward, dgrad and
wgrad), and one is an FP32 router GEMM. The package already ships the
forward (K-major B) form of the half-tail tall program with a
column-grouped raster, whose tall epilogue releases output by row half
(the row-half-release program). This PR adds the input-gradient
(MN-major B) form of that program, built from the same kernel source
family for `sm_100a` and `sm_103a`. The number of compiled libraries in
the package goes from 275 to 277. The PR adds 3 new row rules for the
4096→12288 input gradient (BF16 output). Each rule applies at a single
token count T. They cover `sm_100a` at T 16384 and `sm_103a` at T 16231
and 16384, and they use 16-column-tile raster groups. Before this PR,
these rows used the overlapped half-tail program from the ragged rule,
in the same 16-column-tile groups. On `sm_100a`, the T 16231 row keeps
its current plan. The rule count goes from 388 to 391 (`sm_100a` 153 →
154, `sm_103a` 110 → 112). The `sm_107a` rules are unchanged, and no
`sm_107a` library is added. The baseline is the previous Cake version of
the package on main. The gain is small, about 1 % on every measured row.
On GB200, the T 16384 row has a speedup of 1.010 on one node and 1.011
on the other. On GB300 the rows measure 1.010 at T 16231 and 1.011 at T
16384. On B200 the row measures 1.009, and on B300 both rows measure
1.011. No changed row is slower on any of the four GPUs. Every rule
keeps the K split of the row's previous plan (whole K per output tile),
so outputs on those rows are bitwise identical to main. All other rows
of the 294-row shape list plan the same programs as main.

**Speedup of this PR over the previous Cake version on main.** GB200
(`sm_100a`, 152 SMs, two nodes), GB300 (`sm_103a`, 152 SMs), B200
(`sm_100a`, 148 SMs), B300 (`sm_103a`, 148 SMs); CUDA 13.4, cold L2,
BF16 output. Speedup = previous time / this PR time, and values above 1
mean this PR is faster.

| GPU (arch, SMs) | layer (in→out) | op | out | T | previous µs | this
PR µs | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GB200 node 1 (sm_100a, 152) | 4096→12288 | input gradient | BF16 |
16384 | 926.2 | 916.7 | 1.010 |
| GB200 node 2 (sm_100a, 152) | 4096→12288 | input gradient | BF16 |
16384 | 938.2 | 928.2 | 1.011 |
| GB300 (sm_103a, 152) | 4096→12288 | input gradient | BF16 | 16231 |
820.0 | 811.5 | 1.010 |
| GB300 (sm_103a, 152) | 4096→12288 | input gradient | BF16 | 16384 |
820.2 | 811.6 | 1.011 |
| B200 (sm_100a, 148) | 4096→12288 | input gradient | BF16 | 16384 |
987.0 | 978.2 | 1.009 |
| B300 (sm_103a, 148) | 4096→12288 | input gradient | BF16 | 16231 |
877.3 | 867.8 | 1.011 |
| B300 (sm_103a, 148) | 4096→12288 | input gradient | BF16 | 16384 |
878.6 | 869.1 | 1.011 |

The package also ships FP32-output forms, weight-gradient (wgrad)
programs and the FP32 router GEMM (run through BF16x3 emulation), on
`sm_100a`, `sm_103a` and `sm_107a`.

### [72c91f4](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/72c91f405da0660a402ebd20bac712122c223ad2)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T07:11:24Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): restore the K1 weight-gradient routes that meet the deterministic package's absolute FP64 budgets (#8743)

Cake's dense projection GEMM ships as two packages: the deterministic
`flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_det_gemm` and the
non-deterministic `flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm`. The
non-deterministic package holds two GEMMs, K1 (BF16 or FP32 output) and
an FP32 router GEMM. Each has forward, weight-gradient (wgrad) and
input-gradient (dgrad) programs. This PR restores K1 wgrad routes to the
non-deterministic wgrad programs (block_n 64–256, one or two K splits)
on the `deterministic=False` path. It does so only in windows where
those programs meet the deterministic package's original absolute error
budgets. For BF16 output the budget is atol = rtol = 1e-2 with zero
violations. For FP32 output it is rel_fro ≤ 5e-5 and max_abs ≤ 1e-3 ·
max|ref|. On main these windows run the deterministic package's wgrad
program. The restored windows cover the following parts:
- 148-SM B200 (sm_100a) and B300 (sm_103a)
- 152-SM GB200 (sm_100a) and GB300 (sm_103a)
- 212-SM and 208-SM R200 (sm_107a)

Depending on shape and part, the windows run from T = 1025 up to T =
65537. The README lists the exact windows. Several of them apply only
when T spans an odd number of 64-token K blocks. On 148-SM B300, the PR
also moves 5120→48 and 5120→64 BF16 from main's (64, 2) split route to
the deterministic program, because the split program misses the BF16
budget there. Zones where neither program meets the budget keep main's
route, and the README discloses them. sm_107a parts with 216 or more SMs
also keep main's route until a follow-up qualifies them. The other
variants (the deterministic package, the router GEMM, and K1's forward
and dgrad programs) also ship for sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a, and this
PR changes K1 wgrad routing only.

**Restored windows (231 rows).** In wgrad, the new route is 1.03–2.37x
faster than deterministic Cake, which is main's route there. The
whole-step gain is smaller: 0.99–1.69x for bwd and 0.96–1.36x for the
checkpointed 2fwd+bwd step.

Three rows fall below 1.00x. Each is inside its part's A/A noise band:
- R200 (212 SMs) 4096→1024 at T = 16384, 2fwd+bwd: 0.96x in the first
run and 0.99x in a repeat run.
- GB200 4096→64 at T = 65537, bwd: 0.99x (1.00x in a repeat run).

One more row drops below 1.00x only in eager timing, which the tables
below do not show. GB200 4096→64 at T = 16173 is 1.01x in 2fwd+bwd under
CUDA graph but 0.99x in eager.

Against non-Cake SOTA:
- **sm_100a and sm_103a parts:** the restored wgrad route loses at T =
1025, the first T of every window that starts there (0.62–0.66x), and at
the last timed T of the two 4096→128 windows (0.82x at T = 4031 on
GB200, 0.94x at T = 6079 on GB300). It wins in every table row with T ≥
12289 (1.09–1.22x).
- **R200 parts:** wgrad is 0.54–1.06x on 212 SMs and 0.77–1.02x on 208
SMs. It reaches 1.00x or better only for 4096→512 near T = 16k, and for
4096→128 at T = 7615 on 212 SMs. Every R200 whole-step row stays below
SOTA (0.50–0.99x).

**B300 rows moved to the deterministic program (9 rows).** On B300 (148
SMs), 5120→48 BF16 (T = 40961–49151) and 5120→64 BF16 (T = 47105–49152)
now run the deterministic program. These rows are at parity with
deterministic Cake by construction (1.00x) and are 0.99–1.09x vs SOTA.
They are slower than main's split route by 5.38–6.31 % in wgrad,
2.64–3.41 % in bwd and 1.31–1.67 % in 2fwd+bwd.

*Min and max speedup over the 240 rows of the per-shape table below. The
rows cover the 32 (shape, GPU) windows this PR changes: 30 restored
windows, plus the 2 B300 windows moved to the deterministic program.
Each window appears at its first and last timed token count T, plus T =
16172 / 16173, 16231 and 16384 where the window includes them. Points
timed in two runs appear twice; the second is marked "repeat run". Where
a window edge was not timed exactly, the row uses a timed T with the
same number of 64-token K blocks. For example, the GB200 4096→128 window
ends at T = 4032 and is shown at T = 4031. The exception is B300 5120→64
BF16, where only T = 47105 was timed and the window end, T = 49152, was
not. GPUs: B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), GB200 (sm_100a, 152 SMs), B300
(sm_103a, 148 SMs), GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), R200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs),
R200 (sm_107a, 208 SMs). CUDA 13.4 toolchain (nvcc 13.4.92), cuBLAS /
cuBLASLt 13.8.0, torch 2.14.1+cu130. Drivers: 580.82.07 (B200),
580.126.20 (GB200), 580.126.09 (B300), 580.159.03 (GB300), 620.43 (R200,
212 SMs), 615.71.10 (R200, 208 SMs). Latency method: CUDA graph replay,
with L2 flushed (a 2 x L2 buffer zeroed) before every iteration,
measured as the CUPTI span of all launches of the operation. Each value
is the median over 4 processes of the per-process medians. The 4
processes are two launch layouts x two row orders; B300 uses 8, running
each combination twice. Whole-step medians use 15 groups per process on
sm_100a and sm_103a parts and 9 on R200. Deterministic Cake = the
deterministic package's program, which is main's current route for every
restored window. Non-Cake SOTA = the faster of torch.mm (cuBLAS
heuristic) and the cuBLASLt heuristic's top-8 algorithms, with the same
BF16 inputs and output dtype, measured in the same processes. For bwd
and 2fwd+bwd, SOTA uses the fastest library launch per operation.
Speedup = baseline latency / new latency (> 1 means the new route is
faster). bwd = dgrad + wgrad. 2fwd+bwd = checkpointed step (2 x forward
+ dgrad + wgrad). Each Cake arm uses its own package's forward and dgrad
programs. A/A noise: the deterministic wgrad program was timed against a
second, independently prepared instance of itself in the same processes,
over all timed points. In bwd and 2fwd+bwd, the second instance runs
with the non-deterministic package's forward and dgrad. The ratios over
wgrad, bwd and 2fwd+bwd were 0.970–1.025 (B200), 0.943–1.020 (GB200),
0.988–1.017 (B300), 0.992–1.019 (GB300), 0.957–1.128 (R200, 212 SMs) and
0.940–1.023 (R200, 208 SMs). For B300 5120→48 / 5120→64 BF16, the new
latency is that second instance.*

### [632f980](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/632f980fa43412ed0bb870b06a7480f0c321cd65)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T07:08:50Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fmha): FP8 paged-context runtime-size programs for the non-causal, LSE and sink forms (#8759)

Cake's FP8 paged-context attention (head dim 128, FP8 e4m3 Q, K, V and
output) already ships AOT programs for the plain causal form:
runtime-size RUNTIME_PACK<p> programs with page 16 and 64, split-KV and
one-stage variants.

Five other forms had no AOT program and ran a JIT-compiled module:
- non-causal (NC)
- causal with LSE (LSE)
- causal with sink (SINK)
- non-causal with LSE (NC_LSE)
- non-causal with sink (NC_SINK)

This PR adds 45 runtime-size programs, RUNTIME_PACK<p>_<FORM>, for these
five forms at GQA packs 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12 and 16, on sm_100a and
sm_103a. Calls with both LSE and sinks keep the JIT module. So do causal
LSE and sink calls whose JIT pack has no program.

Outputs are bitwise equal to the JIT module on every timed row. The
baseline is the previous Cake path for these calls, which is the JIT
module. trtllm-gen is shown as a second column. On B200, this PR is
1.053x-2.697x faster than the previous path on the 80 shapes that run a
program. On GB300, it is 1.080x-3.938x faster on 80 shapes.

B200 (sm_100a), CUDA 13.4 (13.4.2 toolkit). GPU time with cold L2, 100
ms warm-up and 1000 ms per measurement. Each µs value is the median of 3
rounds on one seeded memory layout, with the arms rotated each round.
Shape is batch x query tokens x keys, query/KV heads and page size. A
ratio above 1 means this PR is faster.

On both architectures, calls with more than 8192 keys and more than 256
(request, KV head) streams keep the JIT module. A sweep over 10 seeded
layouts x 4 rounds found shapes in this class where the program did not
beat the JIT in every layout, so the whole class stays on the JIT. The
128 x 1 x 16384 rows (32/8 heads) fall under this rule. Their "this PR"
column repeats the JIT time, and the program column gives the measured
program time.

trtllm-gen has a lower median than this PR on 7 B200 rows, with
trtllm-gen/PR as low as 0.930:
- 2 x 200 x 700 in the NC, LSE, SINK and NC_SINK forms
- 8 x 32 x 1024 at 16/8 in the SINK form
- 1 x 2048 x 8192 in the NC and NC_SINK forms (both round to 1.000)

It also has a lower median on 24 GB300 rows, with trtllm-gen/PR as low
as 0.867. All 24 rows are at these shapes: 2 x 200 x 700, 1 x 2048 x
8192, 4 x 512 x 4096 at 8/8 and 16/8, 8 x 32 x 1024 at 16/8, and 32 x 64
x 2048 at 32/32.

Cake's causal FP8 paged-context programs and its BF16 and NVFP4-KV
context programs are unchanged, and this FP8 family ships on sm_100a
(B200) and sm_103a (GB300).

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Expanded FP8 context attention routing to support non-causal, LSE, and
sink output forms across additional configurations.
* Runtime programs can now receive caller-provided LSE and sink outputs
where supported; LSE inputs must use contiguous token-by-head layout.
* Unsupported forms and long-cache cases continue to use the JIT route,
with checks to ensure the selected program matches the requested form.

### [e9caf65](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/e9caf652777e9f342addd7a54ac425e8a084093f)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T07:02:29Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_lm_head_loss): make the log-prob backward's gradient buffers behind its recompute launch (#8762)

Cake's chunked LM-head + loss training backend covers cross-entropy
loss, policy loss, log-probability with no temperature, a scalar
temperature or a per-token FP32 `[T]` temperature, support
log-probability and support-KL, on BF16 hidden states and weights. The
backend has a deterministic form and a non-deterministic (ND) form.
`deterministic=False` on the public `flashinfer.chunked_lm_head` entries
(`chunked_lm_head_loss`, `chunked_lm_head_logprob`,
`chunked_lm_head_support_logprob`, `chunked_lm_head_support_kl`) selects
the ND form, implemented in
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_lm_head_loss`. This PR changes the
host path of the ND log-probability backward. On each GPU, the main
shape list has 165 cells (log-probability with no, per-token or scalar
temperature; T = 4600-65031). The small-T screen has 93 cells (T =
1-8117, also covering cross-entropy and policy loss). The tables leave
out forward-only rows because this PR does not change the forward.
Against the previous ND on FlashInfer main, the new ND is faster in 18
small-T cells at T = 1, 32 or 256 (1.0127x-1.0339x; 7 on B200, 10 on
GB300, 1 on R200). Examples: GB300 backward 1.683 -> 1.628 ms, GB300
checkpointed 3.924 -> 3.858 ms, B200 forward + backward 2.825 -> 2.774
ms, R200 backward 1.153 -> 1.126 ms. All other cells are at parity or
inconclusive; none is slower. Main-list cells span 0.9779x-1.0117x.
Against deterministic Cake, the new ND is faster in 382 of 495 main-list
cells (124 / 124 / 134 on B200 / GB300 / R200; 1.0186x-2.1277x) and
slower in none. On the small-T screen, it is faster in 120 of 279 cells
and slower in 4 (0.2294x-0.9824x). Two omitted forward-only R200 cells,
unchanged from the previous ND, are also slower (0.9444x and 0.9779x).
Only the main list has a non-Cake baseline. With per-token or scalar
temperature, the new ND is faster than PyTorch chunked + torch.compile
in all 180 cells (1.0444x-2.1994x). With no temperature, it is faster
than Cut Cross-Entropy 25.1.1 (torch.compile path) in 128 of 315 cells
and slower in 160 (0.6850x-0.9823x). In every slower table cell, the
previous ND is also slower by point estimate.

Shape legend, shared by all three GPUs (identical shape lists). T
(valid) = tokens (valid rows); C = chunk; z = target fraction of valid
rows with zero dlogp, pattern = their placement, zero = actual
zero-dlogp rows. Modes: LP = log-prob; LP+tT = log-prob + per-token
temperature; LP+t0.7 = log-prob + scalar temperature 0.7; CE = CE loss;
PL = policy loss. p, h, s = owner shape list (log-prob; per-token
temperature; scalar temperature); t = small-T screen.

### [c97fae0](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c97fae06db0007bfc286f94053b16da0f9f340a3)

- **作者**: Cindy Zhang

- **提交信息**: fix(ci): harden sccache fallback handling (#8001)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description
Harden the GPU test sccache wrapper's fail-open behavior.
This PR:
- clears inherited `FLASHINFER_CXX_LAUNCHER` and
`FLASHINFER_NVCC_LAUNCHER` values on every uncached fallback path;
- centralizes uncached execution in `run_uncached`, covering sccache
installation failure, CUDA-version detection failure, and sccache setup
failure;
- explicitly propagates `sccache --zero-stats` failures, which would
otherwise be hidden because `setup_sccache` is called from an `if ! ...`
condition where Bash suppresses `errexit`;
- stops the already-started sccache server when statistics
initialization fails;
- adds regression coverage for inherited compiler launchers and
`--zero-stats` failure handling.

Without the launcher cleanup, a fallback that reports "running without
the compiler cache" can still invoke an inherited sccache executable. If
that executable is missing, later JIT compilation can fail instead of
failing open.

Without explicit `--zero-stats` failure propagation, setup can report
success and publish cumulative statistics from earlier runs as if they
belonged to the current test lane.

## Reviewer Notes
Please focus on the fail-open contract and the setup_sccache
control-command failure handling.

setup_sccache is intentionally called from if ! setup_sccache ...; Bash
therefore suppresses errexit inside the function. Both --start-server
and --zero-stats now propagate failures explicitly.

When --zero-stats fails after the server has started, the implementation
performs a best-effort --stop-server before returning failure and
running the test lane uncached.

setup, or required CUDA-version detection fails.

prevent uncached test runs.
* Inherited cache launchers and state are cleared for uncached runs,
preventing them from unintentionally using compiler caching.

cache-server cleanup.

### [e7ec0e6](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/e7ec0e68cfe214a63c9874b32f436599bb93a57f)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T05:17:50Z
- **提交信息**: feat(cake_dsa_indexer_det): opt-in FP8 (e4m3) form (#8749)

Cake ships two variants of the deterministic DSA indexer top-k,
`flashinfer.dsa_indexer.dsa_indexer_det_topk(..., backend="cake")`, in
FlashInfer. They are the BF16 form, which stays the default, and the FP8
form. This PR adds the FP8 form as an opt-in. The input dtype selects
it: `float8_e4m3fn` `q` and `k`, plus a per-key FP32 `k_scale`. On GB300
and B200, the FP8 form is faster on every row than DeepGEMM
`fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` followed by FlashInfer top-k. The speedup is 1.02x
to 1.45x on GB300 and 1.16x to 1.51x on B200. DeepGEMM does not run on
sm_107a, so sm_107a has no DeepGEMM comparison. Against the Cake BF16
form, the FP8 form is at parity or slower. The ratio is 0.77x to 0.97x
on GB300, 0.88x to 1.01x on B200, and 0.77x to 1.02x on sm_107a. The FP8
form has no wide or CTA-pair programs, which the BF16 default uses on
some shapes. The largest gap is on s1_8k_on_64k, where the BF16 default
runs a wide program on all three GPUs: 0.77x to 0.90x. On GB300, the FP8
kernel is also 3-9 % slower than the BF16 kernel of the same program
kind.

**Table 1. NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), CUDA 13.4, PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130.** All rows: top-k 2048, key ratio 1, causal (each
segment's queries are its last positions). Each call's time is the CUPTI
GPU interval that covers every kernel the call launches, with cold L2
and eager launch. Cake arms time the complete operator of a prepared
runner into caller-owned outputs and workspace. The DeepGEMM arm times,
per segment, the logits call (its logits allocation included) and the
top-k call. It does not time the conversion of its output to ascending
segment-local ids with aligned scores. Each value is the median of all
samples over three arm orders (A then B, B then A, and interleaved).
Cake BF16 is the shipped BF16 form of the same kernel on the same
shapes, with its default program choice. DeepGEMM + FlashInfer top-k is
DeepGEMM `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` (branch `nv_dev`, commit `b64107f2`,
2026-09-24) with FP32 per-key K scales and FP32 logits. Then FlashInfer
`top_k_ragged_transform(deterministic=True, tie_break=LARGE)` runs over
each row's visible keys. This is the strongest applicable baseline
because it computes the same score from the same inputs (e4m3 `q` / `k`,
FP32 per-key scale, FP32 logits). Newer DeepGEMM releases on SM100 take
MX block scale factors and return BF16 logits, a different input format
and output precision. On every row of Tables 1 and 2, this DeepGEMM
composition returns the same ids and scores as Cake FP8, bit for bit.
"vs Cake BF16" = Cake BF16 time / Cake FP8 time. "vs DeepGEMM" =
DeepGEMM composition time / Cake FP8 time. A value above 1 means the FP8
form is faster.

| Shape | Queries T | Keys Tkv | Segments | Cake BF16 (ms) | DeepGEMM +
FlashInfer top-k (ms) | Cake FP8 (ms) | vs Cake BF16 | vs DeepGEMM |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| P1 (recorded packed training call) | 16231 | 268757 | 8 | 2.940 |
3.986 | 3.170 | 0.93x | 1.26x |
| glm2k_16k | 2048 | 16384 | 1 | 0.303 | 0.347 | 0.321 | 0.94x | 1.08x |
| s1_8k_on_64k | 8192 | 73728 | 1 | 2.765 | 3.661 | 3.573 | 0.77x |
1.02x |
| s2_4x2k_packed (4 x 2048 queries over 18432 / 43008 / 67584 / 100352
keys) | 8192 | 229376 | 4 | 2.511 | 3.357 | 2.698 | 0.93x | 1.24x |
| s3_cold16k | 16384 | 16384 | 1 | 1.144 | 1.702 | 1.174 | 0.97x | 1.45x
|

**Table 2. NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), CUDA 13.4, PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130.** Same shapes, baselines, timing method and ratio
definitions as Table 1. A second run on the same node reproduced every
value within 2.1 %. On B200 the medians of the Cake arms in the three
arm orders differ by up to 16 % (on s2_4x2k_packed), so the P1 and
s3_cold16k ratios of 1.01x and 1.00x mean parity with the BF16 form, not
a speedup.

| Shape | Queries T | Keys Tkv | Segments | Cake BF16 (ms) | DeepGEMM +
FlashInfer top-k (ms) | Cake FP8 (ms) | vs Cake BF16 | vs DeepGEMM |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| P1 | 16231 | 268757 | 8 | 3.652 | 4.438 | 3.602 | 1.01x | 1.23x |
| glm2k_16k | 2048 | 16384 | 1 | 0.324 | 0.383 | 0.331 | 0.98x | 1.16x |
| s1_8k_on_64k | 8192 | 73728 | 1 | 3.292 | 4.261 | 3.671 | 0.90x |
1.16x |
| s2_4x2k_packed | 8192 | 229376 | 4 | 2.786 | 3.784 | 3.152 | 0.88x |
1.20x |
| s3_cold16k | 16384 | 16384 | 1 | 1.263 | 1.903 | 1.257 | 1.00x | 1.51x
|

**Table 3. sm_107a (212 SMs), CUDA 13.4, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.** Same
shapes, timing method and ratio definitions as Table 1. DeepGEMM
`nv_dev` `b64107f2` does not run on sm_107a: its FP8 logits kernel stops
with a device-side assert. This table therefore has no DeepGEMM values.

| Shape | Queries T | Keys Tkv | Segments | Cake BF16 (ms) | DeepGEMM +
FlashInfer top-k (ms) | Cake FP8 (ms) | vs Cake BF16 | vs DeepGEMM |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| P1 | 16231 | 268757 | 8 | 2.002 | unsupported | 2.168 | 0.92x | n/a |

n/a |
| s1_8k_on_64k | 8192 | 73728 | 1 | 1.746 | unsupported | 2.254 | 0.77x
| n/a |
| s2_4x2k_packed | 8192 | 229376 | 4 | 1.696 | unsupported | 1.734 |
0.98x | n/a |

The kernel's other Cake variant is the default BF16 form; the kernel and

### [199a353](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/199a353e7df105bca7c1e7ab51b553bdd1ec2ce3)

`flashinfer.experimental.mega_moe_v3` runs the Cake MegaMoE v3 prepared
pipeline in a single kernel launch. It has single-rank routed-FP4,
single-rank routed-FP8 and grouped-GEMM-routes variants, plus a TP/EP
rank variant. The rank variant has 32 programs, covering TP4 EP1, TP8
EP1, TP4 EP4 and TP8 EP8 at 1 to 4096 tokens. This PR changes 3 of the
32 rank programs: TP4 EP1 at 512 and 1024 tokens, and TP8 EP8 at 1024
tokens. The other 29 rank programs are unchanged.

Speedup over the previous Cake version, which is the rank variant on
FlashInfer main after #8731. Speedup = previous / this PR, computed from
unrounded latencies. Values are given for two independent replicates, a
/ b. Each value is the median of 6 paired rounds, with the previous
version and this PR run in separate processes.

- TP4 EP1 at 512 tokens: 1.0009x / 1.0006x, saving 0.27 / 0.18 µs per
call.
- TP4 EP1 at 1024 tokens: 1.0012x / 1.0014x, saving 0.37 / 0.46 µs per
call.
- TP8 EP8 at 1024 tokens: 1.0024x / 1.0024x, saving 0.34 / 0.36 µs per
call.

Speedup over the issue baseline, autotuned
`trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe`, with speedup = TRT-LLM / this PR.
These numbers come from a separate run that used the same harness as

replicates. The speedup ranges from 1.0133x to 1.1768x in replicate a

### [ab4668c](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/ab4668c32dd1832ff7a4a3fc440bb2a11b82b695)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T05:05:36Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_gdn_det_kcp): send only written data in the backward boundary-adjoint all-to-all (#8741)

In `flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_det_train_kcp`, the backward pass
sends boundary adjoints between ranks in a single all-to-all (b1). Until
now, each rank's b1 send buffer gave every fragment that crosses in a
map slot. For fragments that do not cross out, half of their send region
was never written but was still sent. The receiver never read those
bytes, so outputs were unaffected, but they used network bandwidth and
memory checkers reported them as uninitialized reads. The send buffer is
now dense: it holds the adjoint slots of the fragments that cross in,
then map slots only for fragments that cross both in and out. This
changes host-side planning only, with no kernel or launch change, and
outputs and all gradients are bitwise equal to main in every measured
form. Under CUDA compute-sanitizer initcheck (GB200, context parallel 4,
eight 2,048-token documents, per-document zigzag), main reports
4,718,592 errors on rank 0 in this all-to-all and the change reports 0.

Setup: 8 GPUs (2 nodes x 4), context parallel 8; four documents of
98,304 / 65,536 / 57,344 / 40,960 tokens, 32,768 tokens per rank; (H_qk,
HV) = (16, 48); median ms of the slowest rank over interleaved
main/change visits, two independent sessions; "main" is main's b1 send
layout on the same build; CUDA 13.4 toolkit, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. The
main ms and change ms columns are the mean of the two sessions.

**GB300 (sm_103a)**

| Layout | In-kernel L2 norm | Scope | main ms | change ms | change/main
(session 1) | change/main (session 2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| contiguous | off | forward + checkpoint recompute + backward | 14.983
| 14.980 | 0.9998 | 0.9998 |
| contiguous | on | forward | 2.818 | 2.816 | 0.9981 | 1.0005 |
| contiguous | on | forward + checkpoint recompute + backward | 7.835 |
7.828 | 0.9989 | 0.9991 |
| per-document zigzag | off | forward + checkpoint recompute + backward
| 14.960 | 14.955 | 0.9995 | 1.0000 |
| per-document zigzag | on | forward + checkpoint recompute + backward |
7.695 | 7.702 | 1.0020 | 0.9996 |
| zigzag | off | forward + checkpoint recompute + backward | 15.195 |
15.196 | 1.0002 | 1.0000 |
| zigzag | on | forward + checkpoint recompute + backward | 7.940 |
7.945 | 1.0012 | 1.0003 |

**GB200 (sm_100a)**

| Layout | In-kernel L2 norm | Scope | main ms | change ms | change/main
(session 1) | change/main (session 2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| contiguous | on | forward + checkpoint recompute + backward | 7.792 |
7.784 | 0.9997 | 0.9984 |
| per-document zigzag | on | forward + checkpoint recompute + backward |
7.767 | 7.763 | 0.9993 | 0.9999 |
| zigzag | on | forward + checkpoint recompute + backward | 8.088 |
8.084 | 0.9989 | 0.9999 |

End-to-end time is unchanged within noise, and at this size the b1
all-to-all on its own also takes the same time; the change removes data
from the wire, not time.

**b1 all-to-all bytes sent per backward, summed over ranks (same
documents)**

| Context parallel | Layout | main MiB | change MiB |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | contiguous | 18 | 9 |
| 4 | zigzag | 30 | 18 |
| 4 | per-document zigzag | 168 | 156 |
| 8 | contiguous | 30 | 18 |
| 8 | zigzag | 78 | 66 |
| 8 | per-document zigzag | 360 | 348 |

Cake also ships these separately: a non-deterministic variant of this
kernel, single-GPU GDN training packages without context parallelism
(deterministic and non-deterministic), GDN inference kernels for chunked
prefill and decode, and the KDA deterministic context-parallel training
sibling, which covers the per-channel-gate form; this kernel ships on
sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
* Corrected communication-size calculations for map data associated with
fragments crossing both into and out of a rank.
* Updated buffer layout and tile indexing to match the revised
map-transfer counts, improving consistency across planning and backward
execution.
* Added checks for send-tile coverage, map counts, receive-offset
bounds, and communication-byte totals.
