### [2f8cd0a](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2f8cd0a1e7069b4f6c3f5db35b01fb28ac3af7ff)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T04:44:23Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsv4): refine the SM107 FP8 64-head decode route edges by complete-tile count (#8753)

The Cake backend of `trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4` has 49
programs: BF16 and FP8 programs for 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128 query heads
(several bodies per head count, picked per shape by the host route) and
an NVFP4-KV decode family. On sm_107a it ships six FP8 programs for the
DeepSeek-V4 decode route: three 128-head persistent programs (the
persistent program, the uniform-gather program and its K=64 sibling),
the 64-head single-CTA M64 single-tile and multi-tile programs, and the
SWA low-head prefill program. This PR changes only the sm_107a host
route for FP8 64-head decode rows. It changes no program and refines the
route that the previous PR in this series added. Before this PR, rows
with one complete 128-key tile (sparse widths 129-255) ran the M64
multi-tile program past 12 tokens. Rows of two, three or four tiles
(tile count = ceil(sparse width / 128)) switched from the 128-head
persistent uniform-gather program to the M64 programs from den x tokens
> num x SM count on, with (num, den) = (1, 8), (1, 4) and (3, 10) for
two, three and four tiles. Now, rows with one complete tile and at least
half of a second (widths 192-255) run the persistent uniform-gather
program from 13 tokens until the M64 switch. Widths 176-191 run it for
13 to 16 tokens only, and narrower widths keep the M64 program. The M64
switch is now keyed by (tile count, complete-tile count) instead of the
tile count alone. Two tiles with one complete take (3, 20), which is
from 32 tokens on at 208 SMs and from 33 at 216 SMs. Three tiles with
two complete (widths 257-383) take (51, 200), from 54 tokens at 208 SMs
and 56 at 216 SMs, previously 53 and 55. Four complete tiles (width 512)
take (13, 50), from 55 tokens at 208 SMs and 57 at 216 SMs, previously
63 and 65. Two complete tiles (width 256), three complete tiles (width
384) and four tiles with three complete (widths 385-511) keep (1, 8),
(1, 4) and (3, 10). Rows of five or more tiles, and the other
architectures, are unchanged. Speedups are measured against the previous
Cake route (FlashInfer main eb3eb68d) on the rows whose program changes,
on two VR200 boards at 208 SMs with 49 rows per board. They range from
0.99x to 1.05x. Rows with one complete tile measure 1.02-1.05x at 13-16
tokens (widths 176-252), 1.00-1.04x at 20-24 tokens and 0.99-1.03x at
28-31 tokens. Three tiles with two complete measure 1.01-1.03x at 53
tokens, and width 512 measures 1.00-1.05x at 55-60 tokens.

VR200 (sm_107a, 208 SMs), two boards (board 1 and board 2 in the table),
CUDA 13.4. The workload is DeepSeek-V4 decode with 64 query heads per
rank and an FP8 query and KV cache, on the top-k 128x layer, where
sparse width = 128 + context / 128. The table lists the context and the
width per row. Rows = batch x q_len, and the table has q_len 1 rows
(rows = tokens) and q_len 4 (MTP) rows. Each time is per call, from
eight back-to-back calls with `enable_pdl=True` in one CUDA graph with a
512 MiB L2 flush before each graph launch, taking the median of 4 rounds
with rotating program order. Both programs of a row are timed in the
same process on the same board, and speedup = previous / this PR. The
table lists only rows whose program changes. Rows below and above these
edges run the same program before and after.

### [c5bd9da](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c5bd9da26d951ec36b904b3a3d0c9ad6c8836f9a)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T04:18:01Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fmha): four-stage K ring for program 0 of the E4M3 head_dim-128 balanced DCP family (sm_100a, sm_103a) (#8751)

`flashinfer.cake_dcp` (`run_dcp_spec_decode`) has three Cake on-device
load-balanced families. This PR changes the E4M3 head_dim-128 family,
`dcp_spec_bf16_fp8_balanced`, which runs BF16 Q over an E4M3 page-64 KV
cache. That family has three programs. Program 0 is the persistent
planner without the idle-CTA eight-slice fold. Program 1 is the same
planner with the fold. Program 2 is the plan-free static one-wave
program. This PR changes only program 0, in its 32-row and 64-row packed
instances on sm_100a and sm_103a. Program 0 now holds a four-stage K
ring instead of three. The baseline P is the previous Cake version,
program 0 of the `balanced` route on FlashInfer main. Speedups (P/new)
per GPU and mode:

- **B200:** 1.0106–1.0275× under CUDA-graph replay and 1.0111–1.0313× in
eager.
- **GB300:** 1.0195–1.0468× under CUDA-graph replay and 1.0193–1.0473×
in eager.

New is faster than P on every row in both modes on both GPUs. Auto
routing and the public API are unchanged.

*Rows are the 25 E4M3 head_dim-128 rows of the DCP spec-decode benchmark
that program 0 serves (page size 64):*
- *`b`: batch*
- *`s`: global KV prefix length per request*
- *`q`: query tokens per request*
- *`cp<N>`: DCP world size N, measured on rank 0 unless the name ends in
`_r<k>`*
- *`cp1_peer`: world size 1*
- *`_residue`: prefixes 8191–8194*
- *`dcp_fp8_agentx_b16`: cycles a fixed list of agentic-trace lengths
over 16 requests*
- *`dcp_fp8_random_128_<max>_b<B>`: seeded random lengths from 128 to
max*

*Statistic: CUPTI kernel time with L2 flushed before every launch. One
start is a fresh set of processes that times P and new for 10 rounds.
Each value is the median over starts of the per-start medians, with
starts split evenly between both launch orders of P and new. P/new > 1
means new is faster.*

### [dfc8e4d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/dfc8e4d687971f2af4ad09968d328cf8082395fd)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T04:13:02Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda): TMA entering-state load for short many-task turnover launches in BF16 KDA prefill (sm_100a) (#8750)

The Cake chunked KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) prefill behind
`flashinfer.recurrent_kda(..., backend="cake")` has modules with BF16
inputs and modules with TF32 inputs. Both come in fused and split forms.
This PR changes only the prepared BF16-input path with FP32 state
(`flashinfer.prepare_bf16_kda_prefill`), and only on sm_100a (B200). On
sm_100a, the unbounded direct route now uses a new turnover build for
short tasks with many tasks per SM (at most two chunks per task and at
least four tasks per SM). When the state pool is updated in place, this
build loads the next task's entering FP32 state with TMA boxes instead
of a per-lane cp.async loop, starting from the second task of a bin, and
the load overlaps the previous task's compute. Every other sm_100a
launch keeps the existing build. Routes and plans stay the same.
Outputs, final states and checkpoint rows are bit-identical. The tables
compare this PR with the previous Cake version on FlashInfer main, on
B200 only. They report the median latency per call in microseconds, with
a cold L2. Each table has 56 rows: 12 or 16 heads, no gate lower bound
or -5, and 14 sequence-length shapes. One table covers the plan-cache
fast path and the other covers the serving pattern. TIE means no
difference beyond the measurement band. Two rows are faster in each
table, both with no gate lower bound and shape BS64 x T64. With 12
heads, latency goes from 56.40 to 53.66 us (1.05x) on the fast path and
from 56.53 to 53.38 us (1.06x) in the serving pattern. With 16 heads, it
goes from 66.72 to 63.52 us (1.05x) and from 66.82 to 63.49 us (1.05x).
The other 54 rows are TIE, and none is slower. We also swept all 170
launch shapes outside the tables that this PR moves to the new build
(short many-task batches with 8, 12 and 16 heads, layer and wrapper
calls). On B200 all 170 are faster (latency ratio this PR / main 0.89 to
0.98), and none is slower. The family also ships the TF32-input modules
and the split forms, on both sm_100a and sm_103a (GB300). This PR does
not change those variants or any sm_103a program or route.

B200: NVIDIA B200, sm_100a, 148 SMs, driver 580.82.07. CUDA 13.4 (nvcc),
PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.

### [ee42a1d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/ee42a1d117ca3d0d3c2c09cdeb9286ec149085b3)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T04:10:50Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): compensated FP32 SIMT router programs in few-token windows (#8707)

Cake's dense projection GEMM ships as two packages: the deterministic
`flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_det_gemm` and the
non-deterministic `flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm`. The
non-deterministic package holds two GEMMs, K1 (BF16 or FP32 output) and
an FP32 router GEMM. Each has forward, weight-gradient (wgrad) and
input-gradient (dgrad) programs. The family ships for sm_100a, sm_103a
and sm_107a. This PR adds new FP32 router wgrad and dgrad programs (E =
256 experts) on the `deterministic=False` path. They cover 148-SM B200
(sm_100a) and B300 (sm_103a) parts at H = 4096, 5120 and 6144 in
few-token windows: wgrad for T = 1–160 and dgrad for T = 1–32. They are
FP32 SIMT programs with compensated (Kahan / Dot2) accumulation. Outside
these windows the router route is unchanged (on 148-SM parts, the
deterministic program).

Inside these windows, this package currently runs deterministic Cake.
The new programs beat it by 1.10–5.00x in all 102 rows. They lose to the
strongest non-Cake library kernel for each shape (non-Cake SOTA) in 94
of 102 rows, at 0.25–0.99x. They win only for dgrad at H = 5120 and 6144
with T = 17 and 32, at 1.11–1.13x. The checkpointed step gains least:
1.10–1.27x vs deterministic Cake and 0.25–0.58x vs SOTA, because its two
forward calls still run the deterministic program.

| GPU | op | rows | vs deterministic Cake, min | vs deterministic Cake,
max | vs non-Cake SOTA, min | vs non-Cake SOTA, max |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| B200 sm_100a | wgrad | 24 | 1.12 | 5.00 | 0.37 | 0.85 |
| B200 sm_100a | dgrad | 9 | 1.48 | 1.59 | 0.59 | 1.13 |
| B200 sm_100a | bwd (T≤32) | 9 | 1.40 | 2.48 | 0.57 | 0.81 |
| B200 sm_100a | 2fwd+bwd (T≤32) | 9 | 1.11 | 1.27 | 0.25 | 0.58 |

| B300 sm_103a | dgrad | 9 | 1.48 | 1.60 | 0.57 | 1.13 |
| B300 sm_103a | bwd (T≤32) | 9 | 1.38 | 2.44 | 0.56 | 0.80 |
| B300 sm_103a | 2fwd+bwd (T≤32) | 9 | 1.10 | 1.26 | 0.25 | 0.57 |

*Min and max speedup over the 102 rows of the per-shape table below
(FP32, E = 256, H = 4096 / 5120 / 6144, T inside the shipped windows).
GPUs: B200 (sm_100a) and B300 (sm_103a), 148 SMs each. CUDA 13.4
toolchain (nvcc 13.4.92), cuBLAS / cuBLASLt 13.1.1, torch 2.14.1+cu130.
Latency method: CUDA graph replay with L2 flushed before every
iteration, measured as the CUPTI kernel span. Each cell takes the median
of paired groups per process, then the median of run A (all rows in one
process) and run B (one process per row). A/A noise: the same Cake
program timed as two arms gave paired ratios of 0.959–1.030 on B200 and
0.935–1.100 on B300 (per shape, op and run). Speedup = baseline latency
/ new latency (> 1 means the new program is faster). Deterministic Cake
= the deterministic package's program. Non-Cake SOTA = for each shape,
the fastest of cublasSgemm, cuBLASLt FP32 (top-8 heuristics) and
torch.mm with TF32 off, measured in the same runs. bwd = dgrad + wgrad.
2fwd+bwd = checkpointed step (2 x forward + dgrad + wgrad), where the
forward is the deterministic program in every Cake arm. Whole-step rows
cover T ≤ 32, where the route uses both new programs. B300 has 23 wgrad
rows because the H = 4096, T = 33 row is left out.*

supported compensated workloads.

### [cad5b93](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/cad5b93135e3eb11e408da76bc68407753de6fa9)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T04:10:13Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_indexer_det): split few-query calls so each split holds at most top_k keys on sm_100a and sm_103a (#8725)

`flashinfer.dsa_indexer.dsa_indexer_det_topk` is the Cake deterministic
DSA indexer top-k scan. It ships in the package
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_dsa_indexer_det`. It uses BF16 queries and
keys, and FP32 head weights and scores. It returns the top-k key ids for
each query. The ids and scores do not depend on partitioning or
chunking. Ties go to the larger id. Cake ships one variant of this
kernel in FlashInfer. This PR changes the split count for calls with few
queries per segment on sm_100a and sm_103a. These calls split each
segment's keys over several CTAs, and then a merge combines the splits.
The split count used to come from a floor rule, so one split could hold
more than top_k keys. Now each split holds at most top_k keys, and these
calls run faster.

- A split call reads every key of its range in the scan. The merge then
reads its staging in chunks of 4096 entries.
- On sm_100a and sm_103a, the host first checks whether ceil(mean keys
per work unit / top_k) splits fit the split limit and the grid. If they
fit, the host uses that count, rounded up to whole 4096-entry merge
chunks, if it is larger than the floor rule's count.
- Each split then holds at most top_k keys, so the scan does not need to
select inside a split.
- Only calls that the floor rule already splits change. For example, 5
splits become 12, and 7 become 16. Every other call keeps its plan,
program and timing.
- sm_107a keeps its current split plans.
- Every scan program takes one more kernel argument. It is a per-key
FP32 scale that only an FP8 form uses. The BF16 programs in this package
never read it. The host passes a one-element placeholder made once per
device. This change does not affect speed.
- The kernels are regenerated. The merge and finalize programs compile
to the same machine code. The scan programs differ only by the 8-byte
parameter and by instruction-order or padding details.

| GPU | prepared calls (64 ratios: 32 shapes x sampling on/off) min /
median / max | split-count rule rows (16 ratios: 8 shapes x sampling
on/off) min / median / max | eager entry (8 shapes) min / median / max |
|---|---|---|---|
| GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs, CUDA 13.4) | 0.991x / 1.000x / 1.252x |
1.061x / 1.578x / 1.670x | 0.999x / 1.001x / 1.239x |
| GB200 (sm_100a, 152 SMs, CUDA 13.4) | 0.982x / 0.999x / 1.235x |
1.057x / 1.554x / 1.672x | 0.997x / 1.000x / 1.233x |
| sm_107a (212 SMs, CUDA 13.4) | 0.990x / 1.001x / 1.017x | plans
unchanged | 1.000x / 1.000x / 1.002x |

Only two prepared-call rows change their plan. A1 has 4 queries and
22018 keys and goes from 5 to 12 splits (GB300 0.0605 -> 0.0485 ms,
1.247x). A2 has 4 queries and 30466 keys and goes from 7 to 16 splits
(GB300 0.0639 -> 0.0570 ms, 1.121x). The split-count rule rows are
causal tails with 1 to 64 queries over 16k or 32k keys. The 16k rows go
from 3 to 8 splits and are about 1.5-1.7x faster. The 32k rows go from 7
to 16 splits and are about 1.06-1.23x faster. All other rows are
unchanged within run-to-run noise. On sm_107a no plan changes, and every
row, including the side-stream rows (0.996x-1.007x), is unchanged within
run-to-run noise.

The baseline is the previous Cake version, FlashInfer main `2b9ce0e9`.
Speedup is main time divided by this PR time, so values above 1 mean
faster. Every row is timed in a fresh process, in both arm orders. Each
time is the CUPTI GPU time of one synchronized call, and the reported
value is the median over processes. Output bits match main on every row
of every table.

Cake ships no other variant of this kernel in FlashInfer, and this
variant ships on sm_100a (GB200), sm_103a (GB300) and sm_107a.

### [acce1ec](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/acce1ecd12382cd5853e32d61f18fd2c67cee463)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T04:07:39Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_deepgemm_dense_mqa): honour clean_logits in the row-range split; B200 raw-variant test points (#8742)

## 📌 Description

This PR has three commits. They fix correctness issues in the
experimental dense MQA package and its tests.

### Commit 1: honour `clean_logits` in the row-range split

`fp8_mqa_logits` can split a call by query-row range (#8308). A 32-head
FP8 call whose `[Q, logits_stride(K)]` logits pass `MAX_LAUNCH_LOGITS`
runs one `DenseMqaPlan` launch per range of query rows.

#8329 added "raw" route variants. With `clean_logits=False` (the
default, DeepGEMM semantics), raw-store programs leave cells outside
each row's window unwritten. With `clean_logits=True`, those cells are
set to -inf.

**Runtime bug.** The split loop built each range's `DenseMqaPlan`
without passing `clean_logits`. So the split path always ran the route's
own cleaned programs:

- With `clean_logits=False`, the split path did not use the raw variant.
- On a route whose programs are raw, the split path did not reject
`clean_logits=True`.

Fix: `flashinfer/experimental/deepgemm_dense_mqa/dense_mqa.py` now
passes `clean_logits=bool(clean_logits)` to every range's plan. This is
a one-line change.

**Test bug.**
`tests/experimental/test_dense_mqa_generated.py::test_fp8_mqa_logits_row_ranges[1030]`
and `[1027]` failed on main. The test used `torch.equal` to compare
every cell of two default (`clean_logits=False`) calls. After #8329, the
one-launch call runs a raw program that leaves out-of-window cells
unwritten. The split call wrote -inf there. So the full-buffer
comparison failed.

Diagnosis on GB300, H=32, K=4096:

| Q | Differing cells inside windows | Differing cells outside windows |
|---|---|---|
| 1030 | 0 | 3,164,360 |
| 1027 | 0 | 2,978,574 |

All the cells that differed outside the windows were unwritten in one
output and -inf in the other. With `clean_logits=True`, the two outputs
were fully equal. On the window cells, both outputs match an fp32
reference with a max abs error of 6.1e-5.

The test now checks:

- `clean_logits=True`: the split call equals the one-launch call on all
cells.
- `clean_logits=False`: on the window cells, the split call equals the
one-launch call and equals the `clean_logits=True` result.

### Commit 2: B200 test points for the raw-variant bitwise test

`test_dense_raw_variant_is_bitwise_to_the_cleaned_window` used Q 16 and
Q 3 at K = 1048832 for the routes `fp8:full:le16` and
`fp8:partial:le16`.

On sm_100a, #8290 added a single-launch small-Q band
(`fused_scan32_small_q_max_kv` 1048832 for Q up to 29). That band serves
these points on the `le32:short` routes instead. So on B200, all 6 cases
(2 routes × 3 windows) failed at the route assertion, before any logits
were compared.

Fix: these cases now use K = 1049088. Both architectures serve that K on
the le16 routes. This commit only changes the test.

### Commit 3: review follow-ups

- The row-range test now records the `clean_logits` argument that each
split `DenseMqaPlan` receives, and asserts that it equals the caller's
value. The window check alone cannot detect a dropped `clean_logits`,
because raw and cleaned programs write the same window bits.
- The test compares logits as int32 bit patterns and passes
`clean_logits` as a keyword.
- The `fp8_mqa_logits` docstring now says that cells outside each row's
window are `-inf` only with `clean_logits=True`. With
`clean_logits=False`, a route that catalogues a `"raw"` variant leaves
them unwritten.

No commit claims a performance change.

## 🔍 Related Issues

- #8290 (single-launch small-Q band on sm_100a)
- #8308 (row-range split in `fp8_mqa_logits`)
- #8329 (raw route variants and `clean_logits`)

### [4987e0a](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/4987e0a3e0e701a3dcbc930bfcac1310664d5e89)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T03:52:17Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train): one-head inputs take the packed-rows L2 prefetch (#8748)

This PR lets single-head (H = 1) inputs of the non-deterministic package
of Cake's SiLU-gated RMSNorm training kernel
(`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train` with `deterministic=False`)
use the packed-rows path of its bulk kernels. Four kernels have a
packed-rows test: the mid forward, the extra-long forward, and the long
backward with BF16 dw and with FP32 dw. When the head dimension had size
1, the host-side kernel view reported a head stride of 0. A contiguous
one-head input therefore failed that test, and the four kernels skipped
their bulk L2 prefetch. The view now reports a stride of 128 (the head
dimension) for a size-1 head dimension. Kernels never read that stride
for a single head, so no address changes. The only effect is that
contiguous one-head inputs pass the test and issue the prefetch.
One-head inputs with a strided token dimension still fail the test and
keep the fallback. Inputs with H >= 2 are unchanged. No kernel source
changes.

The change reaches one-head inputs in these ranges (rows per SM):

- sm_100a (B200, 148 SMs): forward from 976 to below 2400; backward from
1280.
- sm_103a (GB300, 152 SMs): forward from 976 to below 2400, and from
3000; backward from 1280.
- sm_107a (R200, 212 SMs): forward from 800 (the mid forward below 1740,
the extra-long forward from 1740). The sm_107a backward does not change.

Every other one-head route runs the same code as before.

A speedup is baseline us / new us, so a value above 1 means this PR is
faster. The previous Cake version is this package on FlashInfer main
before this PR. Median previous / new over the changed op-instances of
the A/B (Table 2), with the minimum and count:

| GPU | forward | backward (BF16 dw) | ckpt step (BF16 dw) | ckpt step
(FP32 dw) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B200, sm_100a, CUDA 13.4 | 1.037 (min 1.018, n 42) | 1.057 (min 1.033,
n 45) | 1.045 (min 1.014, n 53) | 1.045 (min 1.014, n 53) |
| GB300, sm_103a, CUDA 13.4 | 1.061 (min 1.035, n 53) | 1.052 (min
1.024, n 50) | 1.055 (min 1.012, n 58) | 1.054 (min 1.012, n 58) |
| R200, sm_107a, CUDA 13.4 | 1.093 (min 1.033, n 42) | unchanged | 1.040
(min 1.014, n 42) | 1.041 (min 1.015, n 42) |

Against the other two baselines on the one-head shapes of Table 1
(ranges over rows):

| GPU | det / new, fwd + fwdg | non-Cake / new, fwd + fwdg | det / new,
bwdg + ckptg | non-Cake / new, bwdg + ckptg |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B200 | 1.088-1.121 | 0.982-1.033 | 1.065-1.187 | 1.071-1.167 |
| GB300 | 1.103-1.168 | 1.025-1.143 | 1.065-1.148 | 1.048-1.117 |
| R200 | 1.105-1.175 | 1.071-1.100 | 1.027-1.171 | 1.034-1.092 |

The deterministic Cake kernel is slower than new in every row. The
strongest non-Cake kernel is faster than new in 7 cells, all on B200
forward rows. In each of them the winner is torch.compile
max-autotune-no-cudagraphs (best of 5), and new is slower by 0.1-1.8 %:

- 148015x1 fwdg 0.996 (23.200 vs 23.296 us)
- 262144x1 fwd 0.999 (37.136 vs 37.167 us)
- 262144x1 fwdg 0.994 (37.088 vs 37.312 us)
- 393216x1 fwd 0.986 (53.360 vs 54.144 us)
- 393216x1 fwdg 0.989 (53.488 vs 54.080 us)
- 524288x1 fwd 0.982 (69.568 vs 70.848 us)
- 524288x1 fwdg 0.983 (69.744 vs 70.952 us)

148015x1 and 262144x1 are inside the changed B200 forward range.
393216x1 and 524288x1 are above 2400 rows per SM, where this PR does not
change the B200 forward. Every previous / new value below 1 is in a cell
that runs the same code in both versions. "Cells below 1x" lists each
one.

The kernel has two other Cake variants. One is the deterministic package
`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train` (the same API with
`deterministic=True`), which this PR leaves unchanged. The other is the
FP32 weight-gradient output of the non-deterministic package, which
takes this change as well. Both packages ship on sm_100a, sm_103a and
sm_107a.

## How the tables were measured

- Inputs are BF16 x / z / y with head dimension 128 and BF16 dw unless
an op says FP32 dw. All times are in us. Table 1's det, non-Cake and new
columns are CUPTI kernel time with a cold L2; the A/B values are
CUDA-event time per call.
- Table 1 (det, strongest non-Cake, new): one process per shape group.
Each value is the median of 10 round medians.
- Previous vs new comes from an in-process interleaved A/B in which both
versions run in the same process with rotating buffers. Each value is
the median over the 8 valid processes (2 nodes per GPU) of the round
medians. Tables 2 and 3 are CUDA-graph replays.
- Table 1 shows the A/B's previous value and its own new value only
where the A/B has that exact shape. Otherwise the cells are blank (B200
148015x1 and 310815x1; GB300 152015x1 and 319215x1; R200 173861x1,
212021x1 and 360421x1).
- The A/B instance set per GPU covers the one-head targets,
training-shaped one-head inputs and H >= 2 controls. GAIN / NEUTRAL /
LOSS is the A/B's verdict per instance.
- Strongest non-Cake kernel per row: the fastest of FLA 0.6.0
`rms_norm_gated`, mamba_ssm v2.3.2 `rmsnorm_fn`, torch.compile default
and max-autotune-no-cudagraphs (best of 5 fresh compiles each) and
inductor's Triton kernel launched directly (forward rows only), all
measured on every row and named in the "non-Cake" column. The column
uses these labels (torch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0):
  - `FLA`: fla 0.6.0 `rms_norm_gated`.
- `tc-max`: torch.compile max-autotune-no-cudagraphs, best of 5
compiles.
  - `tc-def`: torch.compile default, best of 5 compiles.
- Stages:
  - `fwd`: one eager forward call.
  - `fwdg`: the forward replayed from a CUDA graph.
  - `bwdg`: the backward replayed from a CUDA graph.
- `ckptg`: the checkpointed step (2 x forward + backward) in one CUDA
graph.
  - "ckpt step (FP32 dw)": the same step with an FP32 dw.

## Cells below 1x

- Against the strongest non-Cake kernel (Table 1): the 7 B200 forward

### [b8b89d5](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/b8b89d5e766115cd99e22adaa4a816f203b37e38)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T03:48:01Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fmha): interleave the tail units of runtime-size BF16 context launches (#8746)

The Cake paged context attention kernel ships three families: BF16,
FP8-KV and NVFP4-KV. This PR changes only the BF16 family's runtime-size
programs for causal attention with head dim 128. These are
RUNTIME_PACK<g> for g in {1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12, 16} on sm_100a and
sm_103a, for 18 programs in total. On each launch, the host now picks
the order of the work units that come after the last whole 8-unit L2
section. They run either one after another, as before, or interleaved by
m-block with the largest m-block first. A makespan model of the
persistent schedule makes the choice. Only the tile order changes, so
outputs stay bitwise identical to before and to the JIT module. The
baseline is the previous Cake program on FlashInfer main (b791f514). The
JIT module and trtllm-gen are shown as extra columns. On B200, this PR
is 1.016x-1.046x faster than the previous program on 5 of 9 shapes and
at parity on the other 4. On GB300, it is 1.016x-1.059x faster on 5 of 9
shapes and at parity on the other 4. A parity row is either within A/A
(run-to-run) noise or a shape where the host keeps the previous order.
This PR is faster than trtllm-gen on every row except the q>kv row
(1-16384-12288-32-4) on both GPUs. On that row, this PR takes 1791.1 µs
vs 1178.8 µs for trtllm-gen on B200, and 1320.9 µs vs 790.5 µs on GB300.

B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), CUDA 13.4.2, driver 580.82.07. CUPTI cold-L2
kernel time, median over 10 memory layouts x 2 rounds (x 4 rounds on
rows that changed within A/A noise), one process per layout. Shape =
batch-q-kv-Hq-Hkv, page 16, causal, BF16; order = what the host picks.
Ratios above 1 mean this PR is faster.

### [eb3eb68](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/eb3eb68d7deebbe619e05d93ecfd9796e4eaf2e3)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T03:08:34Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mhc): with grad, slab-order bands for the 152-SM sm_103a board at hidden 7168 (#8662)

Cake's mHC (manifold-constrained hyper-connections) kernel with grad has
a deterministic mode (det) and an opt-in non-deterministic mode, nd
(`deterministic=False` of
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_mhc_train`). The workload is X BF16
[T, 4, H] (4 streams) with an FP32 mapping and H = 4096, 5120 or 7168.
It is a local (non-KCP) operator and also runs on a context-parallel
rank's local shard. The nd backward finish is an atomic column slab.
Host rules pick its unit order and its two-size LPT
(longest-processing-time) geometry for each token count T. This PR
retunes the unit order for one board: sm_103a with 152 SMs (GB300) at H
= 7168.

- nd's per-board override table `BWD_SLAB_ORDER_OVERRIDES` gets an order
cell for `("sm_103a", 152, 7168)`. In 33793..63091 there are 48
token-count segments whose column-slab chunk count is at least 19. On 47
of them (18355 token counts), the nd backward column slab now runs the
slab-fastest unit order (`"slab"`, program `dynr_os`) instead of the
chunk order (`"chunk"`, program `dynr`). The segment 34817..35264 keeps
the chunk order. Every other token count below 63092 also keeps the
chunk order. From 63092 the existing `"slab"` band applies as before.
- This board has no two-size (LPT) calibration cell at 7168, because
sm_103a routes no LPT program at 7168. The PR adds no new program and
makes no build change.
- Nothing else changes. Every other board (sm_100a with 148 or 152 SMs,
sm_103a with 148 SMs, sm_107a with 208, 212 or 216 SMs), every other
token count and every other hidden size launch exactly as before. The
forward is unchanged on every board.
- Outputs were checked at the 14 token counts of Table 2. nd's forward
outputs, dX, dB, the saved-statistics gradients, dscale and dbase are
bitwise equal to det. nd's dfn relative L2 vs det is at most 1.07e-07.
The only change is the order of nd's atomic dfn additions.

## Speedup vs the previous nd version

No row is below 1.000 in either timing. The backward is 1.002..1.019
(evd) and 1.002..1.018 (graph) faster, saving up to 70.3 us (evd) and
69.3 us (graph). The checkpointed step is 1.002..1.010 faster in both
timings, saving up to 66.7 us (evd) and 69.1 us (graph).

**Table 1.** The table has 47 token counts, one per changed segment (T =
33920..62778). It covers two operations: the backward and the
checkpointed 2x forward + backward. previous = FlashInfer main's routing
on this GPU; new = this PR. Speedup = previous / new; above 1 means new
is faster. Noise reference: 12 token counts launch the same programs in
both versions (13344, 21824, 24192, 32768, 33312, 33792, 47605, 49152,
52384, 56128, 63092, 65536). At those counts the backward reads
1.000..1.000 (evd) and 1.000..1.001 (graph), and the checkpointed step
reads 1.000..1.000 in both modes. These control rows are not listed in
the table.

Timing: 4 processes, one per GPU of one 4-GPU node, run concurrently.
Each process times every token count with all arms on the same inputs,
with the arms rotated and mirrored inside each group. evd = eager calls
timed with CUDA events. Each call follows a 512 MiB L2 flush and a GPU
spin that lets the host enqueue the whole call first (16 groups x 16
calls). graph = CUDA-graph replays, each after a 512 MiB L2 flush (16
groups x 30 replays). Each process takes the median over groups; the
table shows the median over the 4 processes.

Setup: NVIDIA GB300, sm_103a, 152 SMs, driver 580.159.03, power limit
1400 W, max SM clock 2070 MHz. Cake kernels were built with CUDA 13.4.
PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0), Triton 3.8.0. Inputs are random, with
X BF16 [T, 4, 7168], an FP32 mapping, 4 streams and non-KCP.

## Speedup vs det and B0

- **det**: `deterministic=True` from the same build (this PR's head).
This is the original deterministic Cake implementation, and this PR does
not change it.
- **B0**: for each row, the faster of IEEE-FP32 eager PyTorch and
`torch.compile` running the same mHC function with grad. `torch.compile`
uses the inductor default, `fullgraph=False`, `dynamic=False` and TF32
off; it won all 42 rows. B0's dfn relative L2 vs det is at most
5.00e-06, with 0 dX mismatches at 1e-2.
- **Why B0 is the strongest applicable baseline**: it is the only
non-Cake implementation of this exact function at these sizes.
TransformerEngine's mHC (TF32 mapping math, log-domain Sinkhorn without
eps) and Megatron-LM's fused mHC (TF32 projection) compute a different
function. FlashInfer's `flashinfer.mhc` kernels and DeepGEMM's mega_mhc
are inference only.
- **new**: nd with this PR.
- **Operations**:
  - forward = forward prepare + forward finish.
  - backward = backward prepare + backward finish from saved statistics.
- checkpointed step = forward + statistics recompute + backward on the
checkpoint path. For B0 the checkpointed step is a no-grad forward + a
with-grad forward + the backward.

**Table 2.** The table has 14 token counts x 3 operations (42 rows).

Main columns: CUPTI kernel-sum latency, which is the sum of the
operation's kernel durations. Each value is the median over 4
ABBA-ordered groups of the per-group median of 64 iterations (warmup 8,
cold L2). All three arms run in one process on the same random inputs. 4
processes (one per GPU) run concurrently, each on a share of the token
counts. Speedup = det / new and B0 / new; above 1 means new is faster.

Check columns: det / new nd latency and ratio in Table 1's evd and graph
timings, from the same 4-process runs. The forward comes from a separate
run of the same method.

Why the check columns: kernel-sum adds up kernel durations, so time in
which two kernels run at the same time is counted twice (for example
through programmatic dependent launch, PDL). nd overlaps more at large
T, so kernel-sum understates nd's backward and checkpointed-step speedup
vs det there.

Results over the 42 rows:

- **Forward**: parity with det, because nd runs copies of the
deterministic forward programs. vs det: 1.000..1.002 (kernel-sum) and
1.000..1.000 (evd and graph). vs B0: 16.431..17.035.
- **Backward**: vs det 0.913..1.057 in kernel-sum. It is below 1.000 at
T = 32768 (0.917), 33920 (0.960) and 65536 (0.913). T = 32768 and 65536
are outside this PR's changed bands and launch as before. In the evd and
graph checks every row is faster: 1.016..1.037 (evd) and 1.015..1.037
(graph). vs B0: 6.945..7.028.
- **Checkpointed step**: vs det 0.937..1.031 in kernel-sum. It is below
1.000 at the same 3 token counts (32768: 0.951, 33920: 0.976, 65536:
0.937). In the checks it reads 1.011..1.021 (evd) and 1.010..1.021
(graph), with no row below 1.000. vs B0: 14.511..14.932.

The kernel's other Cake variants are the deterministic mode and hidden
4096 and 5120, and the family ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a;
this PR changes only the nd backward column slab's unit order on 152-SM
sm_103a boards at hidden 7168.

### [bccd392](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/bccd3925683bac7fe1a7fd29ba9c5d87701d58b5)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T03:01:08Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_minimax_h3): staged norm and SF-ring GEMM for one and two NVFP4 destinations on SM103 (#8739)

This PR changes routing for the MiniMax-H3 fused pre-attention program
with NVFP4 output on sm_103a. It adds no new kernel. With one
destination (P = 1) from M = 32640 tokens, the FlashInfer host now
selects the staged norm program (NORM_V5) and the SF-ring fused GEMM
program (FUSED_PACK_K96_SFR5). It does the same with two destinations (P
= 2) from M = 16736 tokens. Both programs already ship. They write the
same bytes as the current NORM and FUSED_PACK_K96 programs. The family
has five fused QKV GEMM variants. There are two output formats, NVFP4
and E4M3, and each has a K = 96 form for sm_103a and an EPI8 form for
sm_100a. The SF-ring program is the fifth variant and is NVFP4 output
only on sm_103a. #7943 sent P = 8 to it. This PR uses it and the staged
norm for large P = 1 and P = 2 token counts too. Smaller token counts, P
= 4 and P = 8 routing, E4M3 output and sm_100a stay the same. For the 13

### [0439690](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/0439690156e9b60dfa9ac537297b49f4a61ab9ec)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T02:48:06Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_det_gemm): plan the sm_103a 17408 -> 5120 and 12288 -> 4096 forwards with the row-half-release program at T-exact keys (#8737)

This PR changes the Cake `dense_projection_det_gemm` package in
`flashinfer.experimental`, the deterministic dense projection GEMM. Most
programs in the package are BF16-operand GEMMs (forward, dgrad and
wgrad), and one is an FP32 router GEMM. The package already ships the
half-tail tall program with a column-grouped raster whose overlapped
epilogue releases output by row half, built for `sm_100a`, `sm_103a` and
`sm_107a`. This PR changes only the row rules. No kernel source or
compiled library changes, and the package still has 275 compiled
libraries. The PR plans this row-half-release program at 4 `sm_103a` row
rules. Each rule applies at a single token count T. Two of these rules
already exist and cover the 17408→5120 forward (BF16 output) at T 16231
and 16384. They used the overlapped half-tail program with the
column-grouped raster in 12-column-tile groups. They now select the
row-half-release program, still with 12-column-tile raster groups. This
is the same rule that the `sm_100a` keys of this row already have. The
two new rules cover the 12288→4096 forward (BF16 output) at T 16231 and
16384. They use 8-column-tile raster groups. Before this PR, that row
used the overlapped half-tail program with 16-column-tile groups from
the ragged rule. The rule count goes from 386 to 388 (`sm_103a` 108 →
110). The `sm_100a` and `sm_107a` rules are unchanged. The baseline is
the previous Cake version of the package on main. On GB300 the
17408→5120 rows measure 1.010 at both T, and the 12288→4096 rows measure
1.014 and 1.013. On B300 the 17408→5120 rows measure 1.009 and 1.010,
and the 12288→4096 rows measure 1.011 at both T. These are small gains
of about 1 %, and no changed row is slower on either GPU. Every rule
keeps the K split of the row's previous plan (whole K per output tile),
so outputs on those rows are bitwise identical to main on both GPUs. All
other rows of the 294-row shape list plan the same programs as main.

**Speedup of this PR over the previous Cake version on main.** GB300
(`sm_103a`, 152 SMs) and B300 (`sm_103a`, 148 SMs); only `sm_103a` rules
change. CUDA 13.4, cold L2, BF16 output. Speedup = previous time / this
PR time, and values above 1 mean this PR is faster.

| GPU (arch, SMs) | layer (in→out) | op | out | T | previous µs | this
PR µs | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GB300 (sm_103a, 152) | 17408→5120 | forward | BF16 | 16231 | 1427.5 |
1413.8 | 1.010 |
| GB300 (sm_103a, 152) | 17408→5120 | forward | BF16 | 16384 | 1430.1 |
1416.1 | 1.010 |
| GB300 (sm_103a, 152) | 12288→4096 | forward | BF16 | 16231 | 823.9 |
813.0 | 1.014 |
| GB300 (sm_103a, 152) | 12288→4096 | forward | BF16 | 16384 | 824.9 |
814.3 | 1.013 |
| B300 (sm_103a, 148) | 17408→5120 | forward | BF16 | 16231 | 1576.6 |
1562.9 | 1.009 |
| B300 (sm_103a, 148) | 17408→5120 | forward | BF16 | 16384 | 1578.9 |
1564.0 | 1.010 |
| B300 (sm_103a, 148) | 12288→4096 | forward | BF16 | 16231 | 871.2 |
862.0 | 1.011 |

863.4 | 1.011 |

The package also ships FP32-output forms, weight-gradient (wgrad)
programs and the FP32 router GEMM (run through BF16x3 emulation), on

### [7a13d7b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7a13d7ba9b75c9bb9c02452df36e3f34417b5d57)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T02:34:33Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mxfp8_megamoe_ep16): sm_103a CuTe-DSL fused programs read the peer tables from shared memory (#8735)

`cake_mxfp8_megamoe_ep16` is the fused MoE kernel with BF16 activations
and MXFP8 weights for 16-way expert parallelism (EP16). It has a CUDA
backend and a CuTe-DSL backend. Each backend has three programs per
architecture: the fused kernel, the fused kernel with the return-all-CTA
config, and the top-k reduce. This PR changes only the two sm_103a
CuTe-DSL fused programs (CTA-0 and return-all-CTA).

Compared with the CuTe-DSL backend on current `main` (the previous Cake
version), EP16 on GB300 runs 1.004–1.014× faster with pre-sleep and
1.005–1.009× faster back-to-back.

**Table.** NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), 16 GPUs (4 nodes × 4
GPUs in one NVLink domain), CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, CuTe-DSL
(nvidia-cutlass-dsl) 4.7.0. Latency is one eager EP16 forward with a
cold L2 (516 MiB flush), timed with CUDA events. Each value is the
median over 16 rounds of the round value; a round value is the maximum
over ranks of the per-rank median of 40 iterations. Baseline is the
CuTe-DSL backend on current `main`, and Speedup = baseline / this PR. In
"Pre-sleep" mode, a GPU sleep of 1e6 cycles precedes each launch. In
"Back-to-back" mode, launches run with no sleep. T is tokens per rank.
`balanced` routing spreads routes evenly across experts, and `hotset50`
sends half of the routes to a hot set of experts.

| Launch mode | T | Routing | Baseline (µs) | This PR (µs) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Pre-sleep | 16 | balanced | 286.35 | 282.29 | 1.014× |
| Pre-sleep | 16 | hotset50 | 285.61 | 282.27 | 1.012× |
| Pre-sleep | 32 | balanced | 285.37 | 284.30 | 1.004× |
| Pre-sleep | 32 | hotset50 | 286.37 | 285.01 | 1.005× |
| Pre-sleep | 64 | balanced | 287.38 | 285.60 | 1.006× |
| Pre-sleep | 64 | hotset50 | 288.42 | 286.34 | 1.007× |
| Back-to-back | 16 | balanced | 285.84 | 283.30 | 1.009× |
| Back-to-back | 16 | hotset50 | 285.34 | 283.29 | 1.007× |
| Back-to-back | 32 | balanced | 285.34 | 283.56 | 1.006× |
| Back-to-back | 32 | hotset50 | 286.10 | 284.57 | 1.005× |
| Back-to-back | 64 | balanced | 287.38 | 285.34 | 1.007× |
| Back-to-back | 64 | hotset50 | 289.44 | 287.36 | 1.007× |

The CUDA backend, the sm_100a and sm_107a CuTe-DSL programs, and the
top-k reduce programs are unchanged; the family ships on sm_100a,
sm_103a and sm_107a.

### [c528929](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c528929d7ab91ca3efbc9f2621499ede00975684)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T02:31:50Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda): overlap the short tail of the BF16 KDA prefill mixed-length range split (sm_100a, sm_103a) (#8738)

The Cake chunked KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) prefill behind
`flashinfer.recurrent_kda(..., backend="cake")` has modules with BF16
inputs and modules with TF32 inputs. Both come in fused and split forms.
This PR changes only the prepared BF16-input path with FP32 state
(`flashinfer.prepare_bf16_kda_prefill`). Within that path, it changes
only the host-side launch of the range ("rng") mixed-length split. The
owner/helper part of that split now runs on a side stream between the
existing fork and join events. The short M64 parts enqueued on the
caller stream therefore run beside it instead of after it. No kernel or
program changes. Routes, bins and plans stay the same. Outputs are
bit-identical. The change applies to both sm_100a and sm_103a. The
tables compare this PR with the previous Cake version on FlashInfer
main. They report the median latency per call in microseconds, with a
cold L2. Each table has 56 rows: 12 or 16 heads, no gate lower bound or
-5, and 14 sequence-length shapes. TIE means no difference beyond the
measurement band. On B200, one row is faster in each table: 12 heads,
gate lower bound -5, 2x(8128+64). It goes from 291.98 to 281.02 us
(1.04x) on the fast path and from 292.93 to 282.08 us (1.04x) in the
serving pattern. All other B200 rows are TIE. On GB300 that row takes a
different (chain) split, so all counted GB300 rows are TIE. One GB300
fast-path row is marked † and is not counted: 16 heads, gate lower bound
-5, 2x(8128+64). Its timing drifted on both sides beyond the measurement
guard within one run. The same drift also happens when FlashInfer main
is timed against itself. We also swept every launch shape outside the
tables that this PR moves (mixed-length shapes that take the range
split; 8, 12 and 16 heads), and none is slower: on B200, 22 of 23 are
faster (latency ratio this PR / main 0.643 to 0.886) and 1 is TIE; on
GB300, 18 of 23 are faster, 2 are TIE and 3 are not resolved by the
measurement guard on either side, with no slowdown observed.

B200: NVIDIA B200, sm_100a, 148 SMs, driver 580.82.07. GB300: NVIDIA
GB300, sm_103a, 152 SMs, driver 580.159.03. CUDA 13.4 (nvcc), PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130.

### [b9455a2](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/b9455a23c6cb63894b28c878e6290fec7899d48b)

- **作者**: chengmingz-nv
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T02:25:39Z
- **提交信息**: fix(sm12x): correct packed scale layouts and kernel reuse (#7704)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Packed activation scales may reach these kernels as either byte or Int32
views. Measuring the byte-view extent before recasting overstates both
the scale descriptor's row extent and its K-plane stride, so a valid
input can read unrelated scale bytes and produce NaNs. Derive the extent
after recasting in FC2 finalize and all three siblings: FC1 activation,
FC1 activation with Q1, and grouped GEMM.

Also include the actual A/B scale element types in all four
compiled-kernel cache keys. Reusing a byte-specialized kernel for an
Int32 view (or the reverse) otherwise retains the wrong representation
assumptions. Add poisoned-backing, already-Int32, swapped-operand, and
bidirectional dtype-transition regressions without changing existing
assertions or tolerances.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Addresses [Brian’s sibling-kernel
review](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/7704#issuecomment-6612195003).

### [c7ce2f5](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c7ce2f5bf2602323edb70fe22823a7019d436466)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T02:03:57Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_dsv4): reject FP8 8-head prefill items wider than 1152 (#8733)

The FP8 low-head prefill program (`fp8_lowhead_prefill`, built for
sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a) stages an item's sparse indices in a
shared-memory buffer of 1152 int32 slots. Its index-loading loop runs
`ceil(sparse_topk / 128)` passes and has no cap. When `sparse_topk >
1152`, the tenth pass writes past the buffer. It overwrites the
SWA-window count and runs past the end of the 205952-byte dynamic shared
memory. The binding does not check the width. `_route` sends FP8 8-head
rows with `max_q_len >= 257` to this program at any width; only sm_107a
sends widths <= 1152 to the M64 programs instead. The 16/32/64-head M64
bindings already reject widths above 1152.

On VR200 (sm_107a, CUDA 13.4), an 8-head FP8 prefill with 257 query
tokens and `sparse_topk = 1280` failed with `CUDA error: an illegal
memory access was encountered`. compute-sanitizer reported an
out-of-bounds 16-byte `__shared__` write from warp 10, which runs index
pass 9. sm_100a and sm_103a have the same buffer and loop. That is from
reading the code; it was not run on those GPUs.

`_route` now raises `ValueError` for these rows when `sparse_topk >
1152`, on every architecture and before any launch.
`cake_dsv4_workspace_requirement` raises it too. The new
`_FP8_LOWHEAD_PREFILL_MAX_WIDTH = 1152` records the buffer size. The
routing comment that said wider items keep the low-head producer is
corrected. `test_fp8_h8_prefill_wider_than_1152_is_rejected` replaces
the sm_107a test that expected 1156 and 2048 to route. It covers
sm_100a/103a/107a and an unknown architecture at page sizes 2 and 64:
1152 still routes, and 1156, 1280 and 2048 raise.

Widths up to 1152 are unaffected. That includes the DSv4 rows (384 / 640
/ 1152).

Validation: CPU tests in `tests/cpu/mla/` (`test_cake_dsv4.py`,
`test_cake_dsv4_out_placement.py`, `test_cake_dsv4_nvfp4_route.py`) give
653 passed, versus 647 on main (8 new cases, 2 replaced). No failures.
pre-commit passes on both changed files.

### [100a6c8](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/100a6c8d72d29e3354b166522e7f71c6e55d0e68)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T01:50:29Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mhc): with grad, the non-deterministic collapse pass reads the mapping-pass input from L2 on sm_107a (#8732)

Cake's mHC (manifold-constrained hyper-connections) kernel with grad has
a deterministic mode (det) and an opt-in non-deterministic mode, nd
(`deterministic=False` of
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_mhc_train`). The workload is X BF16
[T, 4, H] (4 streams) with an FP32 mapping and H = 4096, 5120 or 7168.
It is a local (non-KCP) operator and also runs on a context-parallel
rank's local shard.

This PR makes nd's forward mapping pass on sm_107a use the X-hint
(L2-hint) forms that FlashInfer #8698 added to the deterministic
package. At hidden 4096 on sm_107a, for 64 < T <= 14928 and 15288 < T <=
65536 tokens, the mapping pass now leaves X in L2 so the collapse pass
can read it from there, as det's forward does. Hidden 5120 and 7168,
sm_100a and sm_103a, the backward, and det are unchanged. On the 212-SM
R200 at the 35 token counts of the timing runs (T = 1 to 98304), nd's
forward outputs and the checkpointed step's dX, dB, saved-statistics
gradients, dscale and dbase are bitwise equal to det, and nd's dfn
relative L2 vs det is at most 1.02e-07, the same as before this PR.

## Speedup vs the previous nd version

Timing: 4 processes, one per GPU of one node, run concurrently, and the
arms are rotated and mirrored inside each group. evd times eager calls
with CUDA events after a 512 MiB L2 flush (16 groups x 2 x 16 calls per
arm). graph times CUDA-graph replays, each after a 512 MiB L2 flush (16
groups x 30 replays). Each process takes the median over groups, and the
table shows the median over the 4 processes. previous = FlashInfer
main's routing on this GPU; new = this PR; speedup = previous / new. T =
15288 runs the same kernels in both versions and serves as a control
row.

checkpointed step (2x forward + backward) is 1.000..1.026 (evd) and
0.999..1.028 (graph), up to 12.1 us (evd) / 10.3 us (graph) faster. The
only rows below 1.000 are graph 0.999 at T = 14928, the upper edge of
the first band, for both operations. evd reads 1.000 there.

## Speedup vs det and B0

- **det:** `deterministic=True` from FlashInfer main's deterministic
package. This is the original deterministic Cake implementation, and
this PR does not change it.
- **B0:** per row, the faster of IEEE-FP32 eager PyTorch and
`torch.compile` (inductor default, fullgraph=False, dynamic=False, TF32
off) running the same mHC function with grad. torch.compile won all 57
rows.
- **Why B0 is the strongest applicable baseline:** it is the only
non-Cake implementation of this exact function at these sizes.
TransformerEngine's mHC (TF32 mapping math, log-domain Sinkhorn without
eps) and Megatron-LM's fused mHC (TF32 projection) compute a different
function. FlashInfer's `flashinfer.mhc` kernels and DeepGEMM's mega_mhc
are inference only.
- **new:** nd with this PR.
- **Operations:**
  - forward = forward prepare + forward finish.
  - backward = backward prepare + backward finish from saved statistics.
- checkpointed step = forward + statistics recompute + backward on the
checkpoint path. det runs its checkpointed step the way its autograd
function does. For B0 it is a no-grad forward + a with-grad forward +
the backward.

The main columns show CUPTI kernel-sum latency. The check columns show
det / new nd in Table 1's evd and graph timings. Kernel-sum adds up
kernel durations, so time in which two kernels overlap is counted twice
(for example through programmatic dependent launch). nd's backward
overlaps more kernels than det's, so where kernel-sum reads below 1.000
it understates nd's backward and checkpointed-step speedup vs det.

Caption: main columns = CUPTI kernel-sum latency (the sum of the
operation's kernel durations), median over 4 ABBA-ordered groups of the
per-group median of 64 iterations (warmup 8, cold L2); det, new nd and
B0 run in one process on the same random inputs; 4 process(es) on one
node, each on a share of the token counts. Deterministic Cake =
FlashInfer main's deterministic package, its checkpointed step run as
its autograd function runs it. Non-Cake SOTA (B0) = per row the faster
of IEEE-FP32 eager PyTorch and torch.compile (inductor default,
fullgraph=False, dynamic=False, TF32 off) of the same mHC function
(variant in parentheses). Speedup = det / new nd and B0 / new nd; above
1 means new nd is faster. Check columns: det / new nd latency and ratio,
eager calls timed with CUDA events after a 512 MiB L2 flush (16 groups x
2 x 16 calls per arm, rotated and mirrored arm order) and CUDA-graph
replay (16 groups x 30 replays, 512 MiB flush per replay), median over 4
processes (one per GPU) run at the same time on one node (forward /
checkpointed step from Table 1's runs). Backward check cells only at T =
[1024, 4096] (the backward control runs); the backward is the same
kernels before and after this change. GPU R200 / sm_107a (212 SMs), DRAM
clock 3186 MHz, driver 620.43, CUDA toolkit 13.4.92, PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130 (built with CUDA 13.0); FlashInfer a6553b9c46e9.

Results over the 57 rows:

- **Forward:** at parity with det, because nd runs copies of det's
forward programs: 0.958..1.004 (kernel-sum), 0.995..1.001 (evd),
0.996..1.004 (graph). The kernel-sum 0.958 at T = 512 is noise: det's
own rerun differs from det by 4.3 % there. vs B0: 4.855..16.875.
- **Backward:** the kernels are the same before and after this PR. vs
det, 0.965..1.276 in kernel-sum, below 1.000 at T = 4096, 5120, 6144,
14928, 15288, 15590, 16114, 16132, 16164 and 65536 (worst 0.965 at
65536). Backward check cells exist only at T = 1024 and 4096:
1.067..1.070 (evd), 1.046..1.064 (graph). vs B0: 7.376..10.033.
- **Checkpointed step:** vs det, 0.980..1.194 in kernel-sum, below 1.000
at T = 14928, 15288, 16114, 16132, 16164 and 65536 (worst 0.980 at
65536). In the checks every row is faster: 1.005..1.117 (evd),
1.001..1.128 (graph). vs B0: 6.767..15.085.

The kernel's other Cake variants (the deterministic mode, and hidden
5120 and 7168) are not changed here; the family ships on sm_100a,
sm_103a and sm_107a, and this PR changes only nd's forward mapping pass
at hidden 4096 on sm_107a.

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [95e182c](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/95e182ce2682efabab6c9fbacc4f1fd668bc481e)

- **作者**: Adrian
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T01:38:55Z
- **提交信息**: fix(tests): copy CUDA graph function handles before retaining them (#8729)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Nightly pipeline 79161607 on 2026-11-04 failed CUDA graph occupancy
checks with `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE`.

The graph-inspection helper saved `params.func` from each CUDA
kernel-node parameter structure. This binding borrows storage from
`params`; retaining the wrapper does not preserve an independent handle
value after the parameter structure is replaced or released.

Copy the numeric handle into a new `CUfunction` while `params` is alive.
The existing null-function/kernel fallback stays unchanged. Existing
graph and occupancy tests cover the failure, so no additional unit test
is needed.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Observed in nightly pipeline 79161607 on 2026-11-04; no separate public
issue.

### [82caa56](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/82caa566896b90494463217ba581e47eefd0f720)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T01:27:26Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mega_moe_v3): faster TP8 EP1 T128 / T512 / T1024 rank programs on sm_103a (#8731)

`flashinfer.experimental.mega_moe_v3` runs the Cake MegaMoE v3 prepared
pipeline in a single kernel launch. It has single-rank routed-FP4,
single-rank routed-FP8 and grouped-GEMM-routes variants, plus a TP/EP
rank variant. The rank variant has 32 programs, covering TP4 EP1, TP8
EP1, TP4 EP4 and TP8 EP8 at 1 to 4096 tokens. This PR updates the rank
variant and changes 3 of its 32 programs: TP8 EP1 at 128, 512 and 1024
tokens. The other 29 rank programs are unchanged.

Speedup over the previous Cake version (the rank variant on FlashInfer
main after #8706), for replicates a / b:

- TP8 EP1 at 128 tokens: 1.0032x / 1.0027x, saving 0.55 / 0.47 µs per
call.
- TP8 EP1 at 512 tokens: 1.0026x / 1.0037x, saving 0.47 / 0.67 µs per
call.
- TP8 EP1 at 1024 tokens: 1.0089x / 1.0085x, saving 1.76 / 1.69 µs per
call.

Speedup over the issue baseline, autotuned
`trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe`: this PR is faster on all 32 shapes
in both replicates. The speedup ranges from 1.0212x to 1.1756x in
replicate a and from 1.0207x to 1.1740x in replicate b. On the three
changed shapes it is 1.1607x / 1.1593x at 128 tokens, 1.1679x / 1.1695x
at 512 tokens and 1.1483x / 1.1488x at 1024 tokens.

2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0). Columns 3-8 compare this PR with the previous
Cake version (FlashInfer main after #8706), with speedup = previous /
this PR. The previous version and this PR ran in separate processes over
6 paired rounds, with a previous-vs-previous control. Each value is the
median over the 6 rounds. Columns a and b are two independent
replicates, each on a different node. Speedups are computed from the
latencies before they were rounded to two decimals and are shown to 4
decimals. The savings quoted above are the differences of the displayed
latencies. The 3 changed programs are in bold. This PR leaves the other
29 rank programs unchanged, and they compile to identical machine code.
Across both replicates their ratios ranged from 0.9971 to 1.0024, and
their latency moved by up to 0.13 µs. That gives a run-to-run noise
envelope of up to 0.29 % in either direction. The largest deviation is
TP8 EP1 at 1 token in replicate b, at 12.23 vs 12.27 µs. The gains at
128 tokens (0.32 % / 0.27 %) and 512 tokens (0.26 % / 0.37 %) are about
the size of this envelope, so they are not claimed to be outside noise.
However, in both replicates all 6 paired rounds were above 1 on each of
the 3 changed programs, with a lowest paired ratio of 1.0024. By
contrast, no unchanged program had all of its paired rounds on the same
side of 1 in both replicates. A separate measurement with a different
harness agrees in sign and size. The 1024-token gain (0.89 % / 0.85 %)
is clearly outside the envelope. Columns 9-14 compare autotuned
`trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe` with this PR, with speedup = TRT-LLM
/ this PR. Their latencies are per-call medians from hot replays of CUDA
graphs of 20 calls, with the two sides interleaved. They come from a
separate run with the same harness used for #8682 and #8706, so the
this-PR latencies there differ slightly from columns 4 and 7.*

grouped-GEMM routes) ship on sm_100a and sm_103a, while the rank variant
ships on sm_103a only.

### [4664aa4](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/4664aa4a57594bd1b72fc0500574a5ab58c7fc87)

- **作者**: Ka-Hyun Nam
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T00:46:07Z
- **提交信息**: test(moe): pin W4A16 CuTe-DSL MoE batch invariance (#8399)

## 📌 Description

vLLM's batch-invariant Nemotron-H NVFP4 recipe (vllm-project/vllm#62191)
relies on FlashInfer's CuTe-DSL W4A16 MoE giving bitwise identical
output for a token whether it runs alone or inside a larger batch, using
a pinned tactic and `use_fused_finalize=False`. FlashInfer had neither a
test nor a docstring stating that contract, so a change to
`W4A16_MOE_TACTICS` or to the unfused finalize path could silently break
the recipe.

This PR adds `TestCuteDslMoeW4A16::test_unfused_batch_invariant`,
parametrized over the two tactics vLLM pins (`((256, 128, 256), (2, 1),
True)` and `((128, 8, 256), (1, 1), True)`), which asserts both tactics
are still in `W4A16_MOE_TACTICS` and that a probe token's row is bitwise
equal alone and inside batches of 2, 7, 64, 65, 513 and 1024 tokens, and
that a permuted batch returns permuted rows. It also documents in the
`CuteDslFusedMoEW4A16Runner` docstring that the unfused path with a
fixed tactic is batch invariant and the fused finalize path is not.

No kernel or dispatch code changes.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Refs #7938

### [65b7f8f](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/65b7f8fe896fa6f6e62c56e426256d03be662b79)

## 📌 Description

`trtllm_fp8_block_scale_moe` accepts `routing_replay_out` for every
`fp8_quantization_type`, but the existing `routing_replay_out` tests
only cover the BF16 path, the undersized-buffer rejection and the
fused-shared-experts width; no test called the FP8 block-scale API with
`Fp8QuantizationType.MxFp8` and a replay buffer, so the MXFP8 replay
write (which RL router-replay flows depend on) had no coverage on either
the FlashInfer or the integration side.

This PR adds `test_mxfp8_block_scale_moe_routing_replay_out`, which
plants an unambiguous top-k per token (Renormalize with bf16 logits, and
DeepSeekV3 with fp32 logits and a zero bias; E=128, K=6, T=1 and 300),
runs the MXFP8 block-scale MoE with Relu2 and MajorK shuffled weights,
and checks that an int16 `routing_replay_out` prefilled with -1 holds
exactly the planted experts in every row. Test-only change; no kernel or
Python API changes.

## 🔍 Related Issues

None public; this closes a coverage gap found while investigating an RL
router-replay report whose root cause was in the integration layer, not
in FlashInfer.

### [3d8944f](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3d8944f36ae63fd0e5221fbaa3d1bb575fb9dd94)

- **作者**: 0z5a
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T00:44:41Z
- **提交信息**: docs(sampling): explain why per-row filter params are keyed by row_idx (#5346)

## Description

Adds a comment to `TopKSamplingFromProbKernel` and
`MinPSamplingFromProbKernel` in `include/flashinfer/sampling.cuh`. It
explains why the per-row `top_k` / `min_p` values are read at `row_idx`
and not at `bx`: the per-row tensor has one entry per probability row.
Indexing by `bx` can select the wrong row's threshold when `indices`
reorders or reuses rows, and can read past the tensor when the output
batch exceeds the number of probability rows.

No code change. The fixes themselves landed in #5340 and #5348, and the
fuzzer this PR originally carried was superseded by #5341. After merging
main into this branch, the diff is only this comment, so the title and
description have been cut down to match.

Related: #3605.

### [1436cfa](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/1436cfa87139c21ab999b549adf13ebd51e289f4)

- **作者**: Ka-Hyun Nam
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T00:44:37Z
- **提交信息**: fix(moe): keep unified MoERunner persisted autotune keys rank-invariant, with a cross-process cache-hit test (#8581)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`MoERunner._cache_key_extras()` in `flashinfer/fused_moe/runners.py`
included `local_expert_offset`, and that tuple feeds both `__hash__` and
`get_cache_key_extras`, so every unified MoE backend persisted an
EP-rank-derived autotune key. Under `set_autotune_process_group` a warm
restart then let only the rank that wrote the cache file hit while the
other ranks blocked in the per-tactic reduce: the hang #6082 reported,
which #6139 fixed only for the legacy CuTe-DSL runners.
The fix moves the offset out of the persisted tuple and into `__hash__`
only, so the in-memory key still separates shards living in one process
while the on-disk key is rank-invariant.
`_GroupedGemmStageRunner.__hash__` now derives from its parent's hash so
the cuDNN grouped-GEMM stage runners keep the same split.
No backend enumerates tactics from the offset: `CakeWarpDecodeRunner`
rejects a non-zero offset in `_check_support`, the B12x runners remap it
to an `expert_map` before tuning, and the TRT-LLM and cuDNN runners only
pass it to the kernel at launch or use it to synthesise balanced routing
for profiling inputs, so ranks that differ only by offset enumerate the
same tactic set and can share one persisted entry.
A cross-process tune-then-load test now exercises the persisted key end
to end: one process tunes a `TrtllmFp8BlockRunner` layer at
`local_expert_offset=0` into an `autotune(cache=...)` file, a second
process at offset 8 must load it and measure zero tactics without
changing the file, and a control at a different `local_num_experts` must
still re-tune.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Refs #7920, completes the rank-invariant cache key for the unified
runners (#6139 covered the legacy ones)

request, please make sure the following items are complete.

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit`
(or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks all files with `pre-commit run --all-files`.
(ran the mypy, ruff check and ruff format hooks on the three changed
files; all pass)

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

New `tests/moe/test_moe_runner_cache_key.py` mirrors
`tests/moe/test_cute_dsl_moe_cache_key.py` over `TrtllmFp8BlockRunner`,
`TrtllmFp4RoutedRunner`, `TrtllmMxInt4RoutedRunner` and `CuteDslRunner`:
the persisted key is equal for offsets 0, 32 and 64 and still differs on
`num_experts` and `local_num_experts`; the in-memory hash differs across
offsets and is equal for identical configs. The rank-invariance test
fails on `main` without the fix.
The same file adds
`test_moe_runner_persisted_cache_hits_across_processes_and_ranks`, which
runs the tune-then-load scenario in subprocesses (skipped where the
TRT-LLM block-FP8 MoE is unsupported). On `main` the second process
re-measures all 352 tactics; with this fix it measures none and the
persisted entries are identical before and after.
`tests/moe/test_unified_moe.py` drops the `local_expert_offset` row from
`_DIMENSIONS` (it asserted that the offset moves the persisted key,
which is the bug) and adjusts one hash identity assertion in
`TestBuiltInRunnerLifecycle`.
On B200 (CUDA 13.0, fresh JIT cache): `pytest
tests/moe/test_moe_runner_cache_key.py
tests/moe/test_cute_dsl_moe_cache_key.py` passes (11 passed); the whole
`pytest tests/moe/test_unified_moe.py` passes (415 passed, 2 skipped).

## Reviewer Notes

The in-memory autotuner lookup still matches on `(runner class,
hash(runner), extras)`, so two shards in one process with different
offsets do not share a tuned tactic in memory; on disk they do, which is
what #6139 established for the legacy path.
The multi-rank warm restart under `set_autotune_process_group` itself is
still not exercised by a test; the cross-process test covers the
cache-file side of it on one GPU.

## 📌 Description

`cutlass_fused_moe` always defaulted to the fused GEMM2 finalize, which
reduces the top-k expert outputs with non-associative atomics, so a
caller that asked torch for deterministic execution
(`torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)`) still got run-to-run
differences unless it also knew to pass `use_fused_finalize=False`
(#7917). FlashInfer never read the torch flag, and
`cutlass_fused_moe_workspace_size` had no documented
`use_fused_finalize` entry even though its result depends on it.

`use_fused_finalize` on `cutlass_fused_moe` and
`cutlass_fused_moe_workspace_size` becomes `Optional[bool] = None`.
`None` resolves to `not torch.are_deterministic_algorithms_enabled()` at
the top of each function, before the `backend="cake"` forward, so every
downstream consumer still receives a `bool`. An explicit `True` or
`False` is honoured unchanged. Because the flag is part of the runner
instance key and the autotune cache key, a cache tuned without
deterministic mode can never replay a fused-finalize tactic under it.
The docstrings describe the rule and the workspace-size coupling.

Out of scope here and left for the MoE owners to decide: the
config-object API (`MoEFinalizeConfig.use_fused_finalize: bool = True`)
and `CutlassRunner` pass an explicit value and therefore still fuse
under deterministic mode, and an explicit `use_fused_finalize=True`
under deterministic mode is honoured silently rather than warned about.
The batch-invariant autotune flag (#7207) is a separate follow-up.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Fixes #7917. The `is_batch_invariant_tactic` follow-up for the fused
GEMM2 finalize tactics waits on #7207 and is tracked separately; the
Megatron-LM #8574 caller-side exclusion can be dropped once a release
carries this change.

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

New `test_moe_deterministic_mode_selects_unfused_finalize` in
`tests/moe/test_trtllm_cutlass_fused_moe.py`: under
`torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` with `autotune(True)`, two
runs of the same routed BF16 batch (256 tokens, hidden 1024, 8 experts,
top-k 4) with the flag left at its default must be bit-identical, match
the reference, report the same workspace size as an explicit
`use_fused_finalize=False`, and build no runner with
`use_fused_finalize=True`. The routing and the cuBLAS reference are
computed outside deterministic mode.

On B200 (torch 2.14.0+cu130), `pytest
tests/moe/test_trtllm_cutlass_fused_moe.py -k
'deterministic_mode_selects_unfused_finalize or unfused_finalize'`
passes (the new test plus `test_moe_unfused_finalize[128-2-2-128-1]`).
Not run on H100 or SM120; the resolution is host-side Python, the
kernels are unchanged.

## Reviewer Notes

The trigger is the torch flag because it exists on main today; no other
FlashInfer op reads it yet, so this sets a policy worth a look from the
determinism owners. Megatron-LM can drop its caller-side exclusion once
a release carries this.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* The default finalize behavior for CUTLASS MoE now adapts to PyTorch’s
deterministic-algorithm setting: fused finalize is used when
deterministic algorithms are disabled, and unfused finalize is used when
they are enabled.
* You can still explicitly choose fused or unfused finalize. When sizing
workspace, use the same finalize choice as the operation to ensure
compatible sizing.

### [ed5b388](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/ed5b3885fc0d165de624f77d0cf99e8703caf063)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T00:38:10Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_lm_head_loss): sm_107a ND backward uses the sm_103a GEMM tile rules (#8724)

Cake's chunked LM-head + loss training backend has a non-deterministic
(ND) form, `flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_lm_head_loss` with
`deterministic=False`. It supports cross-entropy loss and
log-probability with no temperature, a scalar temperature or a per-token
FP32 `[T]` temperature. It also has a support-KL entry that uses the
same dense dX. This PR changes the backward on sm_107a (R200) to use the
same split-K dX forms, swapped-tile dX, dW block grouping, long-chunk dW
grouping and wide/long rasters as sm_103a. Of the sm_103a GEMM tile
rules, the only one it does not adopt is the 3-stage long-chunk dX ring,
and the zero-gradient row-skip floor stays at the generic 4097 rows on
sm_107a (3891 on sm_103a). The support-KL dense dX now takes the split
tail on sm_107a, and sm_100a and sm_103a are unchanged. The sweep has
228 cells per record: 138 with no temperature, 63 with per-token
temperature and 27 with scalar temperature. On the 212-SM R200 (two
nodes), the new ND is faster than the previous ND (current main) in 13
of 228 cells, at 1.0191x-1.0296x. Those cells are 6 with no temperature,
3 with per-token temperature and 4 with scalar temperature, all at chunk
4096 and T = 8117-16231. Of the remaining cells, 76 are at parity and
139 are inconclusive; no cell is ND slower. Point estimates span
0.9886x-1.0435x (median 1.0072x). On a second R200 SKU with 216 SMs (one
board, one step per cell, kept as a separate record), 25 of 228 cells
are ND faster at 1.0122x-1.0643x, 89 are at parity, 114 are inconclusive
and none is ND slower. Point estimates there span 0.9883x-1.0643x
(median 1.0071x). Vs deterministic Cake, the new ND is faster in 145 of
228 cells on 212 SMs and in 155 of 228 on 216 SMs; the other cells are
at parity or inconclusive. Over all 228 cells the ratio spans
0.9885x-2.1465x (median 1.1121x) on 212 SMs and 0.9920x-1.9823x (median
1.1018x) on 216 SMs. No cell is ND slower, and the largest ratios are at
z = 0.5. Vs the strongest non-Cake baseline, the per-token and scalar
temperature cells are ND faster in every cell against PyTorch chunked +
torch.compile. On 212 SMs that is 63 of 63 (1.0732x-2.2465x) and 27 of
27 (1.0741x-2.2196x); on 216 SMs it is 63 of 63 (1.0392x-2.0323x) and 27
of 27 (1.0542x-2.0372x). With no temperature the baseline is Cut
Cross-Entropy 25.1.1 (torch.compile path). Of the 138 cells on 212 SMs,
the new ND is faster in 81, at parity in 5, inconclusive in 13 and
slower in 39; over all 138 cells the ratio spans 0.7223x-11.3745x. On
216 SMs the split is 84 / 2 / 11 / 41, and the ratio spans
0.7273x-11.8264x. The largest lead is on cross-entropy-loss backward, up
to 11.3745x on 212 SMs and 11.8264x on 216 SMs. In the table rows, Cut
Cross-Entropy is faster in log-probability cells at z = 0 and z = 0.166,
mostly backward-only; across the sweep the ratio goes down to 0.7223x on
212 SMs and 0.7273x on 216 SMs. This gap already exists on main: in each
of those table rows the previous ND is also slower than Cut
Cross-Entropy. For the support-KL entry, the dense dX now takes the
split tail. That is F 48 on the support-rule cell C1, and on the
large-vocabulary cell C2 it is F 22 on 212 SMs and F 20 on 216 SMs.
Where recorded, the previous ND had F 0. C2 is 1.126x-1.129x faster than
the previous ND on all three records. C1 is 1.114x on the 216-SM board
and 1.004x / 1.013x on the two 212-SM nodes, where the per-round ranges
cross 1. The C0 control takes no split tail on either arm and is
0.999x-1.001x. Vs deterministic Cake, the new ND is 1.058x-1.178x
(median) on every recorded support-KL row.

R200 216-SM sm_107a, separate one-board record. R200 (216 SMs, sm_107a),
driver 615.71.10, CUDA runtime 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, nvcc 13.4; H
6144, V 154880, BF16; per cell p 1 step x 1 node; h 1 step x 1 node; s 1
step x 1 node (one board, one pass; 7/3/1 step files for p/h/s; separate
record, never pooled with 212-SM; verdicts use this record's >= 1-step
rule). Latency = median over steps of the per-step median CUPTI GPU span
(L2 flushed). Verdict: band = max(1 %, A/A floor of nd2/nd), CI95
hierarchical bootstrap, every per-step ratio on one side of 1, >= 1
steps. Speedup = baseline / new ND (> 1: new faster). Previous ND =
FlashInfer main 74e87cef ND code. Operation: fwd + bwd = forward +
backward, ckpt = checkpointed 2x forward + backward. Modes: p = log-prob
(plus CE / policy loss rows), h = log-prob + per-token temperature, s =
log-prob + scalar temperature 0.7. Non-Cake SOTA peer measured (p: Cut
Cross-Entropy 25.1.1 (torch.compile path); h: PyTorch chunked +
torch.compile; s: PyTorch chunked + torch.compile); cell labels: CCE =
Cut Cross-Entropy 25.1.1, chunked = PyTorch chunked, compile =
torch.compile path. Rows: every cell faster than previous ND on the
212-SM record, a representative set (T in {2048, 8117, 16231, 65031},
chunk 4096, z 0 and z 0.5 random, backward and checkpointed, modes p and
h) and every chunk-8192 cell.

### [7fdb928](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7fdb9284c6b1665db4fff836f25af6178027b4dc)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T00:37:03Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_msa): blackwell_msa paged FP8-Q prefill (1 query token, 64/4 heads, 1 page) on a new union program (#8723)

The blackwell_msa sparse attention family has 52 routes backed by 49
programs at this PR, up from 51 routes backed by 48 programs on main.
This PR adds one route and one program and removes none. The routes
cover BF16, FP16 and FP8 (E4M3) data types and flat and paged KV
layouts. They span decode (`decode_m16`, `decode_uniform_fp8`,
`decode_fp8_q1`), prefill (`prefill_union`, `kmaj_p`, `kmaj_p_fused`,
`long_bf16_reverse`) and four top-k selection routes. On main, a prefill
call with FP8 (E4M3) Q as well as FP8 K/V raises `NotImplementedError`
("uniform FP8 Q/K/V is supported only by sparse decode"), so callers had
to convert Q to BF16 themselves. This PR adds a new unfolded
`prefill_union` program that reads FP8 Q directly in the kernel
(`prefill_union` float8_e4m3fn/float8_e4m3fn paged gqa0). It uses this
program for one dispatch case only: a paged causal FP8 Q/K/V prefill
call with 64 query heads, 4 KV heads, one request of one query token,
top-k 16, a page table of one page and no explicit `q_offset`, on
sm_100a and sm_103a. Its output, LSE and temperature LSE are bitwise
identical to the existing BF16-Q route run on Q converted to BF16. Every
other FP8-Q prefill call still raises the same `NotImplementedError`.

Main has no number for this case because it declines the call, and no
earlier Cake version of this variant exists. The baseline is therefore
the FP8 prefill kernel of the MiniMax MSA reference implementation
([MiniMax-AI/MSA](https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/MSA) at commit 8b2e229,
its q8kv8 FP8 prefill path). The reference/PR latency ratio is 4.1312 on
GB300 and 1.5655 on B200. A ratio above 1 means this PR is faster.
Latencies are pooled geometric means over 3 repetitions in µs, measured
with a cold L2.

**NVIDIA GB300, sm_103a, CUDA 13.3**

| shape | route | main (µs) | MSA reference (µs) | this PR (µs) |
speedup (reference / PR) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `prefill_fp8_paged_b1_q1_kv1_hq64_hkv4_k16` | none → `prefill_union`
float8_e4m3fn paged gqa0 | not supported | 50.77 | 12.29 | 4.1312 |

**NVIDIA B200, sm_100a, CUDA 13.3**

| shape | route | main (µs) | MSA reference (µs) | this PR (µs) |
speedup (reference / PR) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `prefill_fp8_paged_b1_q1_kv1_hq64_hkv4_k16` | none → `prefill_union`
float8_e4m3fn paged gqa0 | not supported | 20.24 | 12.93 | 1.5655 |

This PR leaves the family's other BF16, FP16 and FP8 decode, prefill and
top-k routes unchanged, and the family ships on sm_100a and sm_103a.

### [c367744](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c36774422e1499328b3679203b3598d32bf1c57e)

- **作者**: Zixin Huang
- **时间**: 2026-11-05T00:31:05Z
- **提交信息**: fix(moe): reject non-contiguous hidden_states in Prims-TS BF16 MoE (#6608)

## Impact
**`prims_ts_bf16_moe` / `prims_ts_bf16_routed_moe` silently return wrong
output when `hidden_states` is not contiguous** (for example a column
slice `x[:, :H]` of a wider buffer). Nothing raises; nearly every output
element is wrong. After this change such input raises `ValueError`, like
the other Prims-TS MoE dtypes.

## Problem
`prims_ts_bf16_moe` / `prims_ts_bf16_routed_moe` accept a row-strided
`hidden_states` and read it as packed rows. `build_bf16_launch_io` hands
the tensor to the FC1 GEMM as a raw pointer with an assumed row stride
of `hidden_size`, but only checks the routing metadata for contiguity.
The output is silently wrong; the NVFP4, MXFP4xMXFP8, MXFP4xBF16 and FP8
launch-IO builders already reject this.

```python
wide = torch.randn(64, 2 * 1024, device="cuda").bfloat16()
x = wide[:, :1024]                      # row stride 2048
out_nc = prims_ts_bf16_moe(logits, None, x, w1, w2, 8, 2, None, None, 512, 0, 8, routing_method_type=1)
out_c  = prims_ts_bf16_moe(logits, None, x.contiguous(), w1, w2, 8, 2, None, None, 512, 0, 8, routing_method_type=1)
# 64,484 / 65,536 elements differ (max abs diff 9.45); out_c matches an fp64 reference
```

## Fix
`build_bf16_launch_io` now checks `hidden_states`, both weight tensors
and both GEMM output buffers alongside the metadata, using the same loop
and `ValueError("<name> must be contiguous")` as the other dtype
builders. Because the check is in the adapter, it covers both public
BF16 entry points and the unified MoE Prims-TS runner.

## Test
`test_bf16_prims_ts_rejects_noncontiguous_hidden_states` (logits and
routed entry points): the contiguous call runs, and the `x[:, :H]` view
raises `ValueError`.

```
pytest tests/moe/test_trtllm_gen_fused_moe.py -k test_bf16_prims_ts_rejects_noncontiguous_hidden_states
```

The new test fails on `main` (no `ValueError` raised) and passes with
this change; the existing Prims-TS BF16 MoE tests and
`tests/moe/test_unified_moe_prims_ts.py` pass with this change.

cc @nekorobov @feih-nv

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
